title: Activation-Triggered Flows
text: An activation-triggered flow runs when a Data 360 activation is published — connecting segment data to external systems automatically via MuleSoft connectors or HTTP callouts, or sending to other marketing destinations.

title: Agentic Marketing
text: Agentic marketing uses autonomous AI agents to turn one-way marketing broadcasts into two-way conversations — marketers define the strategy (e.g., "increase loyalty among at-risk customers") while AI agents handle the heavy lifting of building audiences, drafting content, personalizing messages, and optimizing performance.

title: Allocations, Limits & Page Customization
text: Marketing Cloud Next has hard limits on flows, scoring, message credits, and CMS storage that differ between Growth and Advanced editions — and a few recommended Lightning components you should add to record pages for marketers.

title: Audience Flows
text: An audience flow is the unified flow creation experience for all audience-based, scheduled marketing flows. It runs on a schedule and sends messages to a specified audience, chosen from four audience sources : Segment, List, Record, or Campaign.

title: Business Units in Marketing Cloud Next
text: Business units create isolated "divisions" inside a single org — each with its own data space, content workspaces, and campaigns — so a global company can run separate brands/regions with data isolation while leadership keeps global visibility.

title: Campaign Record & Workflow
text: The campaign record is the centralized hub for a marketing effort — it shows flow summaries, performance insights, and content across flows, and it's where you create the first flow (via flow trigger, template, or quick start). Campaigns and flows are distinct objects: one campaign can relate to many flows, but each flow relates to only one campaign. <h4 id="permissions" Permissions</h4 <ul <li <strong Create and manage a campaign:</strong Marketing Cloud Manager permission set <strong OR</strong View Flows and Create and Edit Flows user permissions <strong AND</strong Permissions to all elements in the flow.</li </ul <h4 id="campaign-record-vs-flow-canvas" Campaign Record vs. Flow Canvas</h4 <div class="table-wrap" <table <thead <tr <th Surface</th <th What it shows</th </tr </thead <tbody <tr <td <strong Campaign record</strong </td <td Flow summaries (Start element + message/wait elements; >5 elements → messages in a table), sidebar (Campaign Insights, Influenced Opportunities), Overview tab (performance + deliverability insights, content across flows)</td </tr <tr <td <strong Flow Builder canvas</strong </td <td Advanced elements (decision branching, wait configuration)</td

title: Campaigns & Marketing Flows
text: A campaign organizes the assets, audience, and metrics of a marketing effort; a flow is the automation engine (a flow chart on a canvas) that actually distributes content. One campaign can contain many flows, but each flow belongs to one campaign.

title: Channels Overview (SMS, WhatsApp, Mobile App)
text: Marketing Cloud Next is multichannel — email, landing pages, SMS, WhatsApp, and mobile push — but each non-email channel requires its own add-on and specific setup steps before you can send.

title: Consent & Compliance
text: Consent is the gatekeeper of marketing: a strict, subscription-based opt-in model ties consent to specific contact points (email/phone) and channels, so each preference is tracked independently and enforced at send time to keep you compliant with GDPR, CAN-SPAM, and CASL.

title: Consent Audit Trail
text: The Consent Audit Trail is an append-only Data Cloud object that records a row for every consent change — the historical record of all opt-in/opt-out events — unlike the CSC DMO, which stores only current status and is updated in place.

title: Consent Cache (Send-Time Source of Truth)
text: At send time, Marketing Cloud Next does not read the Communication Subscription Consent (CSC) DMO directly — it reads a consent cache keyed by the recipient's email address, populated on demand, valid for 90 days , and only refreshed by supported write paths .

title: Consent Channels & Troubleshooting
text: Consent behaves differently per channel (transactional email, SMS, WhatsApp) and per unsubscribe method — and when consent "isn't working," a systematic 5-step troubleshooting path isolates whether the write ever reached the CSC DMO and whether it was written through a supported path.

title: Consent Data Model
text: Consent is stored in Data Cloud in the Communication Subscription Consent (CSC) Data Model Object (DMO) , keyed on the Contact Point value + Communication Subscription Channel Type (CSCT) ID — deliberately independent of PartyID — so a single address's preference is enforced conservatively at send time.

title: Consent Data Streams
text: Consent records reach the Communication Subscription Consent (CSC) DMO through the UnifiedMessagingConsent data kit , which installs two data streams (consent records + audit trail) — and in most orgs you will find two active generations of each stream feeding the same DMO , so every query must deduplicate on the latest record.

title: Consent Double Opt-In
text: Double opt-in (DOI) is a two-step subscription confirmation process: after a prospect submits a sign-up form, they receive a transactional confirmation email, and only after they click the confirmation link is their consent officially recorded — providing verifiable proof of consent for GDPR and CAN-SPAM.

title: Consent Objects & Models
text: Salesforce contains three separate consent models in one org, and Marketing Cloud Next reads only one of them (Communication Subscription Consent, through the cache) — so a perfectly maintained record in the platform's standard consent model has no bearing on whether an email goes out.

title: Consent Preference Pages
text: Preference Pages let subscribers manage their own consent, but the out-of-the-box pages have real limits (limited branding, no multi-channel, no coding) — for deeper control you build a custom experience with Forms + Form-Triggered Flows + Landing Pages.

title: Consent Segmentation
text: Segmenting directly on consent data isn't supported out of the box — the supported workaround is to build a Calculated Insight on consent data and use it in your segment filter (a metered, credit-consuming operation).

title: Consent Setup & Billing
text: Setting up consent requires enabling Data Protection and the right Data Cloud connector permissions before the consent packages install cleanly, and consent data has specific (mostly zero-cost) billing characteristics — but segmentation, Calculated Insights, and Identity Resolution on consent are metered.

title: Consent Sync: The 3-Flow Architecture
text: Salesforce CRM, Data 360 and Marketing Cloud Next stay in sync through three dedicated flows — because consent can only be written to MC Next via the native Create Consent action (Data Cloud-Triggered or Automation Event-Triggered), never by mapping fields straight into the CSC DMO.

title: Consent Sync & Hybrid
text: The standard Salesforce Email Opt Out field ( HasOptedOutOfEmail ) does not automatically sync with the Marketing Cloud Next Consent layer — you bridge the gap with a two-Flow solution (one CRM→MC Next, one MC Next→CRM), and use Consent Mapping tools to run Account Engagement / Marketing Cloud Engagement side by side.

title: Consent Write Paths
text: Only a handful of supported methods correctly write consent so it's honored at send time — everything else (direct DLO/DMO writes, legacy MessagingConsent actions) can silently produce stale or wrong consent.

title: Contact Point Resolution at Send Time
text: In Data 360 an individual can have multiple email addresses and multiple contact point values per channel — so before a message sends, Marketing Cloud Next must decide which contact point to use , and that decision is controlled by the flow configuration (data graph, API payload, activation source priority, or an activation template).

title: Contact Points & Activation Source Priority
text: When you publish a segment to an activation target , contact point selection decides which fields (email, phone, MAID, etc.) get sent, and source priority order decides which value wins when a contact has that data from multiple sources.

title: Content & Personalization in Marketing Cloud Next
text: The Content tab (powered by Salesforce CMS) is where you create emails, landing pages, forms, SMS/MMS, RCS, WhatsApp, and push messages. Personalization lets you swap content per-recipient using merge fields and dynamic content powered by personalization points, decisions, and targeting rules. <h4 id="content-types-cms-workspace" Content Types (CMS Workspace)</h4 <div class="table-wrap" <table <thead <tr <th Type</th <th Purpose</th </tr </thead <tbody <tr <td <strong Brand</strong </td <td Colors, fonts, button styles, brand identity + tone (used by Agentforce)</td </tr <tr <td <strong Email</strong </td <td Promotional/transactional</td </tr <tr <td <strong Landing Page</strong </td <td Promo pages, host forms</td </tr <tr <td <strong Form</strong </td <td Capture user info</td </tr <tr <td <strong SMS / MMS</strong </td <td Text (SMS) or media (MMS, US/Canada only)</td </tr <tr <td <strong RCS Message</strong </td <td Rich media + suggestions</td </tr <tr <td <strong WhatsApp</strong </td <td Template + session messages</td </tr <tr <td <strong Push / In-App</strong </td <td Mobile notifications</td </tr <tr <td <strong Tracked Link</strong </td <td Track external clicks</td </t

title: Conversational Marketing (Agentforce)
text: Conversational marketing shifts channels from one-way "broadcast" (do-not-reply) to two-way conversation, using Agentforce AI agents to understand intent, retrieve context, and respond to customers across SMS, email, and WhatsApp.

title: CRM Integration & Actionable Lists
text: Marketing Cloud Next is a Lightning app built on Data 360, so historically all audience data had to live in Data 360 — but since Spring '26 you can use CRM records directly as an audience source, and since Summer '26 you can work with campaign members and actionable lists , reducing the Data 360 dependency.

title: Data Architecture Layers (DLO, DMO, Data Graph, Data Lags)
text: Data in Marketing Cloud Next flows through distinct layers — raw DLO → standardized DMO → unified profile via identity resolution → exposed to personalization via the data graph — and each layer runs on its own schedule, so not all data is available everywhere instantly.

title: Data Kits & Data Streams
text: Data kits are pre-built packages of Data Model Objects (DMOs), fields, and data connections that make Marketing Cloud Next work. You install them, and their data streams auto-deploy in Data Cloud — like plugging in the wiring before you turn on the lights.

title: Data 360 Billing & Usage Types
text: Data 360 features consume credits based on records processed, queried, or analyzed — but some usage (internal Salesforce ingestion) is free, and the exact billing depends on your license type (Data Services vs. Flex Credits vs. Data 360 Profiles). <h4 id="license-billing-models" License & Billing Models</h4 <ul <li Orgs purchasing credits <strong before Feb 24, 2026</strong consume <strong Data Services credits</strong .</li <li Orgs purchasing/renewing <strong after Feb 24, 2026</strong can have <strong Data Services or Flex Credits</strong .</li <li If you have a <strong Data 360 Profiles-type license</strong , some usage types aren't consumed.</li <li If operating under a <strong Customer Data Platform license</strong , refer to Customer Data Platform Billable Usage Calculations instead.</li <li Monitor usage in your org's <strong Digital Wallet</strong .</li </ul <h4 id="data-service-usage-records-processedqueriedanalyzed" Data Service Usage (records processed/queried/analyzed)</h4 <div class="table-wrap" <table <thead <tr <th Billing Category</th <th How it's calculated</th </tr </thead <tbody <tr <td <strong Internal Data Pipeline</strong </td <td Rows of stru

title: Data 360 Segment Types
text: Data 360 supports five segment types — standard , real-time , waterfall , dynamic , and data-kit — each optimized for a different job: scheduled audience refreshes, millisecond on-demand evaluation, mutually-exclusive multi-offer priority lists, parameterized query-driven lists, and ready-made segments from prebuilt packages.

title: Decision Branching & Path Experiments
text: Flows route each customer to the right path using Decision elements (first-match-wins branching on data-graph attributes), and Path Experiments bring A/B testing into the flow so the winning variation can go out to the remaining audience automatically.

title: Distributed Marketing & Alerts
text: Distributed Marketing and Alerts lets marketers share approved email templates with non-marketing users (sales reps) so they can send on-brand, compliant one-to-one or bulk emails — with locked brand content and approved phrases/images.

title: Domain Settings
text: Marketing Cloud Next uses several domains for different jobs (login, email links, images, landing pages, SMS links), and you can configure My Domain, tracker domains, sending domains, and custom domains to brand and control your URLs.

title: Domain Warming & IP Sending Infrastructure
text: Marketing Cloud Next starts email sends on shared IPs and automatically assigns dedicated IPs based on volume , continuously rebalancing traffic for optimal delivery — but you still must warm your sending domain because major mailbox providers now treat domain reputation as the primary signal (with IP reputation as fallback for unknown domains).

title: Dynamic Content, Variations & Personalization Points
text: Dynamic content swaps whole components (subject line, image, CTA) per audience using variations governed by targeting rules . Each component with variations is tied to a personalization point ; each variation maps to a decision (same name). Link multiple components to one personalization point to control them together — and personalize more than 25 components per item. <h4 id="the-three-salesforce-personalization-concepts" The Three Salesforce Personalization Concepts</h4 <div class="table-wrap" <table <thead <tr <th Term</th <th Definition</th </tr </thead <tbody <tr <td <strong Personalization point</strong </td <td A content element eligible for a personalization decision (subject line, preheader, image component). Configuring the first variation <strong auto-creates</strong a personalization point for that component/field.</td </tr <tr <td <strong Personalization decision</strong </td <td Determines who's eligible to receive a response based on the targeting rules. Each variation is related to a decision, and they share the <strong same name</strong .</td </tr <tr <td <strong Targeting rule</strong </td <td The conditions that decide which variation shows — based on attribu

title: Dynamic From & Reply Addresses
text: Instead of one mailbox for every email, Dynamic From and Reply addresses resolve the sender, display name, and reply-to from related CRM or Data 360 records at send time — so subscribers see and reply to a specific person (contact owner, account manager, customer success manager) or a brand/region address. The right configuration depends on how you authenticate your sending domain.

title: Einstein Segments (Generative AI) & Data Prism
text: Einstein Segment Creation uses generative AI to turn a natural-language description into a suggested segment (attributes and values), grounded by Einstein Data Prism which maps your metadata to the semantic meaning of objects and fields so the AI understands your actual data.

title: Building & Personalizing Emails
text: The email editor lets you build structure on a canvas, add components, and layer personalization through rule-based dynamic content and merge fields — so a single email adapts its structure and its details to each recipient.

title: Creating & Editing Emails (Visual, Code View & Templates)
text: Emails are built in the Content Builder (visual canvas) or in Code View (HTML/CSS + Handlebars), previewed/tested against a segment, and published before a campaign flow can send them. Reusable email templates lock brand elements while letting authors edit within boundaries, and promotional emails must carry CAN-SPAM consent details via merge fields.

title: Email Domain Authentication (DKIM, SPF, DMARC)
text: To send email, you must authenticate a sending domain (and verify a From address) so receiving servers trust your messages aren't spoofed — improving deliverability and protecting your domain's reputation.

title: Email Sending Setup (Trust & Compliance)
text: Before sending trusted, compliant email you must establish a trusted sending identity (physical address, authenticated domain, from addresses, branded tracking links), configure consent, enable reply handling, and protect engagement metrics — building trust in both the email and the results.

title: Engagement Signals
text: Engagement signals are configured using a primary engagement DMO and mapped fields to identify and track individual engagements — they power Salesforce Personalization features like custom recommender objectives, custom attribution models, and personalization experiments.

title: External Forms & Form Handlers
text: Forms built in Marketing Cloud Next can be embedded on your own external website (via embedding code + CORS/clickjack/trusted-site configuration), or you can keep your existing site forms and use a form handler to capture their submissions into Salesforce — mapping your form's field names to Salesforce fields and triggering a flow.

title: Flow Builder Elements for Marketing
text: Flow Builder elements are the actions a flow can run (decisions, sends, record operations). Some elements are marketing-specific (Send Email/SMS, Create Consent, Path Experiment) and are available only in certain flow types. <h4 id="marketing-specific-flow-elements" Marketing-Specific Flow Elements</h4 <div class="table-wrap" <table <thead <tr <th Element</th <th What it does</th <th Flow types</th </tr </thead <tbody <tr <td <strong Create Consent</strong </td <td Updates consent status for a contact point related to a unified individual (Opt In/Opt Out)</td <td Automation Event-Triggered only</td </tr <tr <td <strong Determine CRM Record for Individual</strong </td <td Finds if a person has a contact, lead, or prospect record; set up different paths per situation</td <td —</td </tr <tr <td <strong Einstein Decision</strong </td <td Determines email engagement level via Einstein Engagement Frequency/Scoring; routes users by engagement level (if-then)</td <td —</td </tr <tr <td <strong Exit from a Flow</strong </td <td Removes individuals from a specific Marketing Cloud flow (e.g., remove a customer who purchased during a campaign)</td <td —</td </tr <tr <td <strong Marketing Compl

title: Flow Data Operations (Records, Collections & Transform)
text: Flows aren't connected to your data by default — Get Records pulls data into the flow, and Create/Update/Delete Records push it back to Salesforce. Assignment, Loop, Collection Filter/Sort, and Transform manipulate variables and collections, and flow operators define how filter conditions compare values.

title: Flow Elements Deep Dive (Messaging, Decision, Path Experiment, Subflow, Wait)
text: Flow Builder elements are the building blocks of a marketing flow. This page deep-dives the messaging elements (Send Email/SMS/RCS/Mobile/In-App), the Decision element (manual vs. AI logic), Path Experiments (A/B/N testing with automated winner selection), the Subflow element (calling other flows), and the Wait elements (pausing for time, dates, conditions, or events).

title: Flow Sharing & Campaign Management
text: Marketing flows related to a campaign inherit the campaign's sharing settings ; standalone flows are private by default . You can share flows dynamically (via categories + sharing rules) or manually (per user/group). <h4 id="campaign-flow-sharing-relationship" Campaign ↔ Flow Sharing Relationship</h4 <ul <li A flow related to a campaign <strong inherits the campaign's sharing settings</strong .</li <li When you <strong delete a campaign</strong , the sharing settings for each related flow revert to the flow record's defined sharing rules. title: Forms & Form Data Sources
text: Forms capture user information and are added as a component on a landing page (one form per landing page). A form has two parts — the fields/settings and the flow that processes submissions — and uses data providers to bridge form fields to Salesforce objects: a write data provider saves submissions, while read data providers pre-fill fields and drive progressive profiling. <h4 id="permissions" Permissions</h4 <ul <li <strong Create a form on a landing page:</strong Marketing Cloud Manager permission set <strong AND</strong any CMS workspace contributor role.</li <li <strong Publish a form and landing page:</strong Marketing Cloud Manager permission set <strong AND</strong a CMS workspace contributor role of <strong content admin or content manager</strong .</li <li <strong Create/publish a form using data source fields:</strong the above <strong AND</strong <strong Modify All Data</strong permission for the data source object, its fields on the form, and the record type selected.</li <li <strong Author with AMPscript:</strong the above <strong AND</strong the <strong AMPscript Author</strong permission.</li </ul <h4 id="create-a-form" Create a Form</h4 <ul <li Entry points: signup

title: Identity Resolution Match Rules
text: Match rules tell Data 360 which profiles to unify during identity resolution. Each rule contains one or more criteria; profiles match when all criteria in a rule are satisfied, and a unified profile is created if any single match rule is activated.

title: Identity Resolution Reconciliation Rules
text: Reconciliation rules select a single value to save to a unified field that can't hold multiple values (like a name) during identity resolution — they determine what's shown in the unified profile, not a "best" value, and they don't apply to contact points .

title: Identity Resolution Rulesets
text: Identity resolution matches duplicate and related records (from different systems) into a single Unified Individual record, so marketers can target real people instead of fragmented data fragments.

title: Landing Pages (Create, Templates, SEO & URLs)
text: Landing pages host introductory/brand content and forms for lead generation. They're built with components/templates (hosted on the auto-generated Marketing Landing Pages Experience Cloud site) or in code view (hosted on a marketing site), configured with SEO properties and URL aliases, and published to activate their URLs and any related form + flow. <h4 id="permissions" Permissions</h4 <ul <li <strong Create/edit content:</strong Marketing Cloud Manager permission set <strong AND</strong any CMS workspace contributor role.</li <li <strong Publish/unpublish content:</strong Marketing Cloud Manager permission set <strong AND</strong a CMS workspace contributor role of <strong content admin or content manager</strong .</li <li <strong Author with AMPscript:</strong the above <strong AND</strong the <strong AMPscript Author</strong permission.</li </ul <h4 id="hosting-two-kinds-of-sites" Hosting: Two Kinds of Sites</h4 <div class="table-wrap" <table <thead <tr <th Creation method</th <th Hosted on</th </tr </thead <tbody <tr <td <strong Components or template</strong </td <td <strong Marketing Landing Pages</strong — auto-generated Experience Cloud site, used only to host content, ge

title: Marketing Agents (Out-of-the-Box AI Agents)
text: Marketing Cloud Next ships with five out-of-the-box AI agents — Segment Creation, Campaign Creation, Content Creation, Journey Decisioning, and Account Discovery — each handling a different stage of the marketing workflow, from audience definition through to account-based discovery.

title: Marketing Cloud Next — Overview & Setup
text: Marketing Cloud Next is Salesforce's multichannel marketing platform that sits on top of Data Cloud , so before you can market to anyone you must first wire up the data foundation, identity resolution, channels, and consent.

title: Marketing Cloud Portfolio
text: Marketing Cloud is not a product — it's the brand name for Salesforce's whole next-generation marketing portfolio , and Marketing Cloud Next is just one product inside it (alongside Salesforce Personalization, Marketing Intelligence, and Loyalty Management).

title: Marketing Flow Types (Complete Taxonomy)
text: In Marketing Cloud Next, all outbound messaging is orchestrated through Flow — a major shift from Marketing Cloud Engagement, where messages could be sent from journeys, automations, triggered sends, UI sends, and more. These marketing flows (also called high-scale flows ) run off-core on a separate high-scale processing engine.

title: Marketing Objects, AMPscript & Handlebars
text: Beyond the data graph, you can store marketer-owned data in marketing objects (like legacy data extensions) and read it into messages using AMPscript or Handlebars , and you can reach fixed lists of known individuals with actionable lists — giving marketers autonomy without admin dependencies.

title: Marketing Sites
text: A marketing site hosts landing pages created in code view (component/template pages live on the auto-generated Marketing Landing Pages site instead). Each org has a default marketing site that publishes automatically when a landing page goes live, and its settings control public access, languages, integrations, security, and site-wide head markup.

title: Marketing Triggers (Behavioral Automation Events)
text: Marketing triggers detect key customer behaviors (abandoned carts, product views, price drops, low inventory) and start automation event-triggered flows so marketers can respond with personalized, timely messages across channels. <h4 id="available-triggers" Available Triggers</h4 <div class="table-wrap" <table <thead <tr <th Trigger</th <th Detects</th <th Key Parameters</th </tr </thead <tbody <tr <td <strong Abandoned Shopping Cart</strong </td <td Added items but didn't purchase</td <td Inactivity period (10 min–7 days)</td </tr <tr <td <strong Abandoned Page</strong </td <td Viewed key pages, left without action</td <td Inactivity period</td </tr <tr <td <strong Abandoned Product Browse</strong </td <td Viewed products, left without cart/purchase</td <td Inactivity period</td </tr <tr <td <strong Product Back In Stock</strong </td <td Unavailable product now available</td <td Lookback period (1–60 days)</td </tr <tr <td <strong Product Low Inventory</strong </td <td Stock below threshold</td <td Threshold (1–1M units)</td </tr <tr <td <strong Product Price Drop</strong </td <td Price dropped by %</td <td % drop (1–100%)</td </tr </tbody </table </div <h4 id="event-sources-f

title: Marketing Workspaces & Salesforce CMS
text: All marketing content in Marketing Cloud Next — images, landing pages, forms, brand assets, emails — lives in CMS content workspaces , and each workspace is tied to a specific business unit , so content is isolated by team, brand, or region unless it's explicitly shared as a common asset .

title: Marketing Cloud Engagement Journeys & Campaigns
text: Use the campaign object as a shared workspace across Marketing Cloud Engagement and Marketing Cloud Next — associate MCE journeys to a campaign to streamline workflows and enable in-depth reporting. <h4 id="associating-journeys-to-campaigns" Associating Journeys to Campaigns</h4 <ul <li When you create a campaign, you can select a <strong Quick Start</strong option (preconfigured flow) or <strong Build Your Own</strong (create campaign + flow from scratch).</li <li Connect MCE journeys to a Campaign to group them into a larger marketing effort and automatically create a grouped view of their marketing performance.</li </ul <h4 id="multi-org-scenarios" Multi-Org Scenarios</h4 <ul <li Marketing Cloud Engagement+ supports customers with <strong multiple orgs</strong .</li <li If org A builds campaign A and associates journey A, that same journey <strong isn't available</strong for org B to relate to campaign B.</li </ul <h4 id="campaign-reporting-with-journeys" Campaign Reporting with Journeys</h4 <ul <li For <strong new journeys</strong , reporting begins when the journey is connected to a Campaign.</li <li For a <strong running journey</strong , Salesforce attempts to associate

title: Merge Fields & Saved Expressions
text: Merge fields insert a single customer value (name, city, product) into content; saved expressions are reusable filter+sort criteria that pick which single value a data-graph merge field returns when many are possible (e.g., the most recent opportunity). Both live in the Salesforce CMS and are reusable across email, SMS, and WhatsApp.

title: Opportunity Influence & B2B Analytics
text: Opportunity Influence ties campaign engagement back to revenue (attribution), and B2B Analytics for Marketers connects CRM + engagement data to pipeline and revenue via ready-made dashboards — together they answer "which campaigns actually make money?"

title: People Records: Prospects, Leads, Contacts & Unified Individuals
text: Marketing Cloud Next tracks people through distinct lifecycle stages — Prospect (unqualified) → Lead (qualified) → Contact (customer) — while Identity Resolution merges their records into a Unified Individual used for segmentation. Each stage maps to DMOs in Data 360, and records can be created, imported, converted, and automated via flows. <h4 id="prospect-vs-lead" Prospect vs. Lead</h4 <div class="table-wrap" <table <thead <tr <th </th <th <strong Prospect</strong </th <th <strong Lead</strong </th </tr </thead <tbody <tr <td Definition</td <td Shared contact info, not yet qualified</td <td Qualified, shows buying intent</td </tr <tr <td Funnel Stage</td <td Top of funnel</td <td Middle of funnel</td </tr <tr <td Source</td <td Campaigns, events, signup forms, referrals</td <td Sales qualification, scoring</td </tr <tr <td Qualification</td <td Unqualified</td <td Qualified (budget, authority, need, timeline)</td </tr <tr <td Engagement</td <td May have interacted only once</td <td Actively engaging with sales/marketing content</td </tr <tr <td Ownership</td <td Marketing team (no owner)</td <td Sales team (assigned owner)</td </tr <tr <td Objective</td <td Nurture & qualify<

title: Personalization Data Sources in Marketing Cloud Next
text: A data source is any org object or element whose fields become available for personalization — merge fields, expressions, repeater components, and dynamic content. The Data Sources tab in Content Builder is where you add, view, and manage them, and the data graph (usually a profile graph on the Unified Individual DMO) is the backbone that most personalization depends on.

title: Repeaters & Personalization Recommenders
text: A repeater shows a series of items (products, order updates, events) in an email, fed by a data source (event, data graph attribute, or a Personalization recommender ). Recommenders pick the best item per contact at send time — no hand-written rules — and improve over time as they learn from engagement.

title: Reporting & Analytics Setup
text: Marketing Cloud Next uses Marketing Performance (Data Cloud + Tableau Next) and preconfigured analytics packages to give you embedded dashboards and reporting — but you must install the right packages, connect analytics objects, and share folders first.

title: Reporting Metrics & Dashboards (Measure Success)
text: Marketing Cloud Next reporting (powered by Data Cloud/Data 360 + Tableau Next) provides dashboards across every channel — email, SMS, RCS, WhatsApp, push, in-app, landing pages, forms, tracked links — with well-defined metric formulas for measuring campaign success. <h4 id="reporting-types-locations" Reporting Types & Locations</h4 <div class="table-wrap" <table <thead <tr <th Reporting Type</th <th Location</th <th Purpose</th </tr </thead <tbody <tr <td Campaign Performance dashboard</td <td Marketing Performance Intelligence tab + campaign records</td <td Aggregated/individual campaign KPIs</td </tr <tr <td Content Performance dashboard</td <td Content records</td <td Cross-channel KPIs + variation data</td </tr <tr <td Deliverability dashboard</td <td MPI tab + campaign records</td <td Email deliverability + failure reasons</td </tr <tr <td Email Engagement dashboard/reports</td <td Analytics tab</td <td Email KPIs (filterable)</td </tr <tr <td SMS/Forms/Landing Page Engagement</td <td Analytics tab</td <td Channel-specific KPIs</td </tr <tr <td Engagement Score / Details</td <td Prospect/Lead/Contact records</td <td Individual engagement</td </tr </tbody </table </div <h4

title: Starting Flows from REST API & Apex
text: Autolaunched flows can be started programmatically via a REST API call (invocable action endpoint) or from Apex ( Invocable.Action or Flow.Interview classes) — enabling external systems and custom code to trigger flows with input variables and read output values.

title: Sandbox & Deployment
text: Sandboxes are safe copies of your production org for testing, training, and development. Marketing Cloud Next supports all sandbox types, but you must handle Data Cloud objects, sender codes, and content replication carefully before deploying back to production.

title: Scoring Models (People & Accounts)
text: Scoring assigns a 0–100 value to leads, contacts, prospects, and accounts based on engagement (how they interact) and fit (how closely they match your ideal customer), so you can build segments and target content.

title: Segment Canvas & Filters
text: The Segment Canvas lets you build audiences by dragging direct (1:1, N:1) and related (1:N) attributes into containers, applying aggregation, AND/OR nesting, and advanced grouping/ranking/limiting — with population counts to validate each filter's impact.

title: Segments & Audiences
text: A segment is a group of Unified Individual IDs filtered by rules you define, and a Unified Individual is the consolidated record that merges multiple lead/contact records for the same person — the foundation of targeted marketing. <h4 id="key-terms-from-glossary" Key Terms (from Glossary)</h4 <div class="table-wrap" <table <thead <tr <th Term</th <th Definition</th </tr </thead <tbody <tr <td <strong Audience</strong </td <td Any collection of people who can receive marketing/transactional/operational content</td </tr <tr <td <strong Segment</strong </td <td A group of Unified Individual IDs based on filtering rule criteria</td </tr <tr <td <strong Unified Individual</strong </td <td Consolidated record of metadata from multiple prospect/lead/contact records for the same person</td </tr <tr <td <strong Unification</strong </td <td Process of matching lead/contact records to create a unified individual record for segmentation</td </tr <tr <td <strong Identity Resolution</strong </td <td Matching multiple records to create a unified profile</td </tr <tr <td <strong Identity Resolution Ruleset</strong </td <td Criteria used to identify/match related records (e.g., name, email)</td </t

title: User Access & Permission Sets
text: Marketing Cloud Next ships with two main permission sets — Marketing Cloud Admin and Marketing Cloud Manager — plus granular permissions and content roles that control who can build, publish, and manage campaigns, content, and flows.

title: Web Tracking (Landing Pages & External Sites)
text: Marketing Cloud Next can track page views, form submissions, link clicks, and button clicks on both hosted landing pages AND your external website — using cookies and an optional consent banner — to feed engagement data into Data Cloud for better segmentation. <h4 id="what-gets-tracked" What Gets Tracked</h4 <ul <li Page views</li <li Form submissions</li <li Link clicks</li <li Button clicks</li </ul <h4 id="two-tracking-scenarios" Two Tracking Scenarios</h4 <div class="table-wrap" <table <thead <tr <th Scenario</th <th Key Requirements</th </tr </thead <tbody <tr <td <strong Landing Pages with consent banner</strong </td <td Data Cloud integration + Data Cloud Web Tracking Consent Banner integration + banner design</td </tr <tr <td <strong Landing Pages without consent banner</strong </td <td Data Cloud integration + Relaxed CSP + event tracking code in head markup</td </tr <tr <td <strong External Sites with consent banner</strong </td <td External Tracking data kit + Website connector + banner design + embed code</td </tr <tr <td <strong External Sites without consent banner</strong </td <td External Tracking data kit + Website connector + embed code</td </tr </tbody </table </

title: Editions — A consultant is scoping a Marketing Cloud Next implementation for a mid-market c
text: A consultant is scoping a Marketing Cloud Next implementation for a mid-market company on the Enterprise edition. The marketing team wants to isolate data between three regional divisions and use on-canvas flow insights. Which product tier must the consultant recommend? Advanced.

title: Permission Sets — A new marketing operations hire needs to build campaigns, segments, and flows, b
text: A new marketing operations hire needs to build campaigns, segments, and flows, but must not have access to Setup. Which permission set should the consultant assign? Marketing Cloud Manager.

title: Business Units — A company on the Advanced tier has 150 Business Units configured. They want to d
text: A company on the Advanced tier has 150 Business Units configured. They want to deactivate one that is no longer used, then reactivate it next quarter if the division returns. What should the consultant advise? Deactivation is permanent — the Business Unit cannot be reactivated.

title: Business Unit Roles — A regional marketer needs to review flows and segments in their Business Unit bu
text: A regional marketer needs to review flows and segments in their Business Unit but must not be able to activate flows. Which Business Unit member role should be assigned? Marketer-ReadOnly.

title: CMS Workspace Sharing — A consultant shares an Enhanced CMS workspace from the Brand workspace to the Re
text: A consultant shares an Enhanced CMS workspace from the Brand workspace to the Regional workspace, and then shares the Regional workspace to the Local workspace. A Local author reports they cannot see the Brand content. What is the cause? CMS workspace sharing is non-transitive — the Brand workspace must be shared directly to the Local workspace.

title: Domain Authentication — A company wants to authenticate their sending domain in Marketing Cloud Next. Th
text: A company wants to authenticate their sending domain in Marketing Cloud Next. Their DNS team asks how many CNAME records are needed for DKIM and what key strength is used. What should the consultant state? 3 outbound CNAME records, using a 2048-bit DKIM key.

title: DMARC — A client's security team insists that DMARC must be configured before the sendin
text: A client's security team insists that DMARC must be configured before the sending domain can be activated. Is this correct? No — DMARC is recommended but not required to activate a sending domain.

title: DNS Propagation — A consultant adds the authentication records and the client asks how long until
text: A consultant adds the authentication records and the client asks how long until sending can begin. What is the maximum expected wait? Up to 48 hours for DNS propagation.

title: IP Infrastructure — A high-volume sender asks whether they should request a specific dedicated IP ad
text: A high-volume sender asks whether they should request a specific dedicated IP address and manage their own warming schedule. What should the consultant explain? Managed dedicated IPs are auto-assigned by volume with continuous rebalancing — the sender does not pick or manually manage them.

title: Reputation Signals — A deliverability specialist is troubleshooting inbox placement. They focus on IP
text: A deliverability specialist is troubleshooting inbox placement. They focus on IP reputation. What should the consultant recommend they prioritise instead? Domain reputation — it is the PRIMARY signal.

title: Warming Targets — A client is starting a domain warming program. What starting volume and quality
text: A client is starting a domain warming program. What starting volume and quality thresholds should the consultant recommend? Start with a few hundred sends per day; keep bounce rate < 2% and complaint rate < 0.1%.

title: List Hygiene — A client's engagement has declined and they ask when to stop mailing a contact.
text: A client's engagement has declined and they ask when to stop mailing a contact. What engagement cutoff should the consultant recommend? 6 months of no engagement.

title: Data 360 Provisioning — A consultant is planning the Data 360 foundation for a Marketing Cloud Next impl
text: A consultant is planning the Data 360 foundation for a Marketing Cloud Next implementation. The client asks which provisioning model applies. What should the consultant clarify? Whether the org uses a core-org configuration or a Data Cloud One / companion-org configuration.

title: Install Order — A consultant is setting up a new Marketing Cloud Next org. What must be installe
text: A consultant is setting up a new Marketing Cloud Next org. What must be installed first, and what follows automatically? Data kits install first; data streams auto-deploy afterwards.

title: Marketing Triggers Permission — A marketer needs to configure behavioural automation events. Which permission se
text: A marketer needs to configure behavioural automation events. Which permission set is required? Marketing Triggers Admin.

title: Sandbox Types — A client wants to test a Marketing Cloud Next implementation before go-live. Whi
text: A client wants to test a Marketing Cloud Next implementation before go-live. Which sandbox types are supported? All sandbox types — Developer, Developer Pro, Partial Copy, and Full Copy.

title: Sandbox Deployability — A consultant builds a campaign, a brief, a Communication Subscription, an email,
text: A consultant builds a campaign, a brief, a Communication Subscription, an email, and a segment-triggered flow in a Full sandbox. Which of these can be deployed to production? The email and the segment-triggered flow can be deployed. The campaign, brief, and Communication Subscription cannot.

title: Deploy Order — A consultant is deploying changes from sandbox to production. Which objects must
text: A consultant is deploying changes from sandbox to production. Which objects must be deployed first? Data Cloud objects first (segments, DMOs, DLOs, data graphs, calculated insights, data actions, Personalization Points, recommenders, engagement signals) — then activate/publish. Marketing Cloud Next objects follow (content records, email templates, brand, images, CMS workspace, flows).

title: Deployed Status — A consultant deploys a flow and an email to production and tells the client they
text: A consultant deploys a flow and an email to production and tells the client they are live. Is this correct? No — deployed flows and content always have Draft status in the target org and must be manually activated/published.

title: Email Blackhole — A consultant is testing in a sandbox and wants to prevent test emails reaching r
text: A consultant is testing in a sandbox and wants to prevent test emails reaching real customers. What should they enable, and what are the caveats? The Sandbox Blackhole (Setup → Blackhole → Sandbox Blackhole), which takes 10 minutes to take effect. It allows up to 5 permitted domains as exceptions, and does NOT suppress the Preview/Test window or the Debug flow window.

title: SMS Sender Code in Sandbox — A consultant copies the production SMS sender code into a sandbox to test SMS. W
text: A consultant copies the production SMS sender code into a sandbox to test SMS. What happens? It fails — a sender code can only be active in one org. Each channel needs unique configuration per sandbox (authenticated domain, tracking domains, WhatsApp number, blockout windows).

title: Default Domains — A client asks which domain types Marketing Cloud Next provides out of the box. W
text: A client asks which domain types Marketing Cloud Next provides out of the box. Which one is NOT provided by default? Email sending domains are NOT provided by default — you must authenticate them. My Domain, tracker domains, and landing page domains have defaults.

title: Tracker Domain — A client asks how Marketing Cloud Next captures email opens and clicks. What mec
text: A client asks how Marketing Cloud Next captures email opens and clicks. What mechanism should the consultant describe? The tracker domain, via "link rewriting" — URLs are rewritten with the tracker domain, engagement is captured, then the visitor is forwarded to the target.

title: Domain Per Use Case — A client wants to use one custom domain for email links, SMS links, and landing
text: A client wants to use one custom domain for email links, SMS links, and landing pages. What should the consultant advise? Each use case needs its own authenticated domain or subdomain — email links, SMS, and landing pages cannot share one.

title: Trusted Sending Identity — A consultant is establishing a trusted sending identity. What four elements make
text: A consultant is establishing a trusted sending identity. What four elements make it up? A physical mailing address · an authenticated sending domain · authenticated from addresses · branded tracking domains.

title: RMM Scope — A client wants Reply Mail Management enabled for one campaign only. Is this poss
text: A client wants Reply Mail Management enabled for one campaign only. Is this possible? No — RMM applies to all messages from the authenticated domain and cannot be turned on per campaign.

title: Metrics Guard Purpose — A client's open rates look inflated by automated scanning. Which feature should
text: A client's open rates look inflated by automated scanning. Which feature should the consultant enable? Einstein Metrics Guard — it uses AI to filter activity unlikely to be from humans (bot scans, security checks) so open and click rates stay meaningful. Enabled via Unified Messaging → Settings.

title: Send-Time Validation Failures — A client's campaign shows "messages not sent". What are the two most likely caus
text: A client's campaign shows "messages not sent". What are the two most likely causes? Consent Not Given or Invalid From Address .

title: Edition Limits — A client on Growth wants to run 600 active flows and use 2 scoring models. Is th
text: A client on Growth wants to run 600 active flows and use 2 scoring models. Is this possible? No — Growth allows 500 active flows and 1 scoring model. Advanced allows 750 active flows and 2 scoring models.

title: Recommended Lightning Components — A marketer wants to see a contact's engagement score and consent status directly
text: A marketer wants to see a contact's engagement score and consent status directly on the Contact record. Which components should the consultant add? Data Cloud Profile Insights (numerical engagement score) and Privacy Consent Status (subscriptions + consent values) — both available on Lead and Contact records.

title: Profile Insights Measure Fields — A consultant is configuring the Data Cloud Profile Insights component. Which Mea
text: A consultant is configuring the Data Cloud Profile Insights component. Which Measure field maps to the Overall Marketing Score? People Score c . (Marketing Engagement Score → Engagement Score c ; Marketing Fit Score → Fit Score c .)

title: Data Kits — A consultant is setting up a new org and asks what data kits provide. What shoul
text: A consultant is setting up a new org and asks what data kits provide. What should they explain? Data kits are pre-built bundles that install the data plumbing (DMOs, mappings, streams) for a use case — and data streams auto-deploy with them.

title: Channel Add-Ons — A client wants to send SMS, WhatsApp, and mobile app messages. Which channels re
text: A client wants to send SMS, WhatsApp, and mobile app messages. Which channels require a paid add-on? SMS (Salesforce Message Credits - SMS), WhatsApp (Salesforce Message Credits - WhatsApp), and Mobile App Messaging (Salesforce Message Credits - Mobile App Regional, Advanced Edition). Email and Landing Pages are included.

title: Government Cloud Restrictions — A public-sector client on Government Cloud wants to use SMS and WhatsApp. Is thi
text: A public-sector client on Government Cloud wants to use SMS and WhatsApp. Is this supported? No — SMS, WhatsApp, and Mobile App Messaging are not supported in Government Cloud. Email and Landing Pages are supported.

title: SMS Code Types — A client needs a 10-digit US SMS number. What must they request, and what is the
text: A client needs a 10-digit US SMS number. What must they request, and what is the lead time? A long code — it requires associated Brand + Campaign + Code requests, and existing 10-digit codes cannot be ported. Registration can take weeks.

title: WhatsApp Setup — A consultant is configuring WhatsApp. What are the setup steps?
text: A consultant is configuring WhatsApp. What are the setup steps? Setup → "Your" → Your Numbers · install the required managed packages for consent and engagement · create/connect a WhatsApp Business Account · review consent validation settings (Setup → "Channels" → WhatsApp).

title: Mobile App Messaging — A client wants mobile push notifications. What are the platform requirements?
text: A client wants mobile push notifications. What are the platform requirements? Advanced Edition plus the Mobile App Regional add-on, and the org must be hosted in Germany or the United States.

title: Custom Mobile App Events — A consultant has activated a custom mobile app event and now wants to delete one
text: A consultant has activated a custom mobile app event and now wants to delete one of its attributes. Is this possible? No — once an event attribute is activated, it cannot be deleted. You can deactivate (but not delete) active events.

title: Marketing Cloud Portfolio — A client asks the consultant to "implement Marketing Cloud." During discovery, t
text: A client asks the consultant to "implement Marketing Cloud." During discovery, the consultant learns the client needs a Data Cloud-native marketing platform, a real-time personalization engine, AI-powered analytics, and a no-code loyalty program. How should the consultant frame the recommendation? Marketing Cloud is the portfolio brand, not a single product. The client needs four products: Marketing Cloud Next, Salesforce Personalization, Marketing Intelligence, and Loyalty Management.

title: Configuration Steps — A consultant is enabling Marketing Cloud Next in a new org. The client's admin a
text: A consultant is enabling Marketing Cloud Next in a new org. The client's admin asks how many steps are required and which are automated. What should the consultant explain? At a minimum there are six key configuration steps. The first three — set up Data 360, enable Marketing Cloud, and deploy the required data streams — are driven by the Setup Assistant, each initiated with a single button click.

title: Data Cloud Architect Permission Set — A consultant needs to install data kits, deploy data streams, and configure iden
text: A consultant needs to install data kits, deploy data streams, and configure identity resolution in a new Marketing Cloud Next org. Which permission set must be assigned, and by whom? The Data Cloud Architect permission set, assigned by a user with a System Administrator profile.

title: Authorized vs Authenticated Domain — A client wants to use dynamic From and Reply-to addresses in their Marketing Clo
text: A client wants to use dynamic From and Reply-to addresses in their Marketing Cloud Next emails. They have already authenticated their sending subdomain. What additional configuration is required, and what does it provide? An authorized email domain. It verifies ownership with a simple verification record but does NOT provide the DKIM/DNS sending configuration that an authenticated domain establishes.

title: CMS Content Workspaces & Business Units — A global client runs three brands in separate business units. Where is all marke
text: A global client runs three brands in separate business units. Where is all marketing content stored, and what is the relationship between business units and content workspaces? All marketing content is stored in CMS content workspaces, and each workspace is associated with a specific business unit. A data space maps to no business unit or one; a business unit maps to one or more content workspaces.

title: Common Assets — A marketer in the "North America" business unit needs to use a brand asset creat
text: A marketer in the "North America" business unit needs to use a brand asset created in the "EMEA" business unit. What is the supported approach? Post the asset as a common asset, making it available to all business units; the marketer then copies it into their own workspace.

title: Business Unit Role Content Access — A sales representative needs visibility into marketing dashboards but should not
text: A sales representative needs visibility into marketing dashboards but should not be able to edit or publish CMS content. Which business unit role should be assigned, and what constraint applies? Marketing Read-Only — it provides access to the data space only, not CMS content. Note that users without the Marketing Manager or Marketing Admin permission sets can only be assigned this role.

title: Content Publishing & Form Activation — A marketer builds a form, adds it to a landing page, and saves both. They report
text: A marketer builds a form, adds it to a landing page, and saves both. They report that the form isn't creating leads. What is the most likely cause? The content was saved but not published. Publishing the form also activates its associated flow — and the landing page must be published with an active URL alias for the form to be visible.

title: Consent Model — A client asks what happens if a contact has never explicitly opted in but has al
text: A client asks what happens if a contact has never explicitly opted in but has also never opted out. Can Marketing Cloud Next send to them? No — Marketing Cloud Next uses strict opt-in, so the absence of an explicit "Yes" means the contact is blocked.

title: Composite Key — A consultant is explaining how consent records are uniquely identified. What thr
text: A consultant is explaining how consent records are uniquely identified. What three elements make up the consent composite key? Subscription + Contact Point + Channel Type.

title: PartyID — A developer inspects the consent audit trail and notices the PartyID field is bl
text: A developer inspects the consent audit trail and notices the PartyID field is blank on every row, even for known Contacts. Is this a data quality issue? No — PartyID is blank by design, because consent is keyed on Contact Point value + CSCT ID, not on the individual.

title: Shared Address — Two family members share a single email address. One of them unsubscribes from a
text: Two family members share a single email address. One of them unsubscribes from a newsletter. What is the effect on the other? The opt-out affects everyone sharing that address — there is no way to send to some and suppress others on the same contact point.

title: Audit Trail vs DMO — A compliance officer asks how to prove what a contact's consent status was six m
text: A compliance officer asks how to prove what a contact's consent status was six months ago. Which object should the consultant point to? The Consent Audit Trail — it is append-only and records every historical change.

title: Audit Trail Attribution — A client wants to report on which team member changed each consent record. What
text: A client wants to report on which team member changed each consent record. What should the consultant explain? There is no UserId/ActorId field — use caller-provided source attribution instead (ConsentCapturedSourceType, ConsentCapturedSourceName, ConsentCapturedSourceDetails, SenderId).

title: GDPR Deletion — A contact exercises their right to erasure. How should the consultant delete the
text: A contact exercises their right to erasure. How should the consultant delete their consent audit trail rows? Use the Consent API ShouldForget endpoint on the Individual — deletion is asynchronous and reprocessed at 30/60/90 days, then permanent.

title: Create Consent Inputs — A consultant is configuring a Create Consent flow action. What four input parame
text: A consultant is configuring a Create Consent flow action. What four input parameters does it require? Consent Status, Contact Point, Channel, and Communication Subscription.

title: Create Consent Availability — A consultant needs to write consent from a flow. Which flow type supports the Cr
text: A consultant needs to write consent from a flow. Which flow type supports the Create Consent action, and which legacy action must be avoided? Create Consent is available in Automation Event-Triggered flows (and Data Cloud-Triggered / On-Demand flows). Never use the legacy MessagingConsent action.

title: Unsupported Write Paths — A client plans to load consent by mapping an external system's data stream direc
text: A client plans to load consent by mapping an external system's data stream directly to the Consent DLO. What should the consultant advise? This is an unsupported write path — it will cause stale consent. Supported paths are Preference Pages, the Consent Status LWC, CSV imports, and Salesforce Flow (Create Consent).

title: Silent Dropouts — A client reports that consent records appear correctly in the UI, yet some conta
text: A client reports that consent records appear correctly in the UI, yet some contacts still receive no email. What is the most likely cause? External consent was mapped straight into the CSC DMO — it appears saved but is ignored at send time, causing silent dropouts.

title: Consent at Scale — A client needs to load consent for millions of records from an external system.
text: A client needs to load consent for millions of records from an external system. What two-step approach should the consultant recommend? 1) Batch Data Transform → DLO for the initial load. 2) A Data Cloud-Triggered Flow with Create Consent to write consent so it is honoured at send time.

title: CSV Import Limit — A client wants to use CSV consent imports as their ongoing weekly sync mechanism
text: A client wants to use CSV consent imports as their ongoing weekly sync mechanism. What should the consultant advise? CSV imports are limited to 50,000 rows per file and are intended for one-time loads — not sustained high-volume sync.

title: Send-Time Cache — A consultant updates a consent record directly in the CSC DMO and confirms the c
text: A consultant updates a consent record directly in the CSC DMO and confirms the change in the UI. The next send still goes out. Why? At send time, Marketing Cloud Next reads a cache keyed by recipient email — not the DMO directly. Direct DMO writes do not refresh the cache.

title: Cache Refresh Paths — Which actions refresh the send-time consent cache?
text: Which actions refresh the send-time consent cache? Manual layout update · Unsubscribe link / Preference Center · CSV import · and (officially) the Create Consent flow activity.

title: Double Opt-In — A client wants to confirm genuine intent before recording consent. What two-step
text: A client wants to confirm genuine intent before recording consent. What two-step process should the consultant implement, and what type of email must the confirmation be? 1) Submit the sign-up form and receive a transactional confirmation email. 2) Click the confirmation link to verify intent — only then is consent recorded. The confirmation email must be Transactional.

title: Wait Until Event — In a double opt-in flow, what does the Wait Until Event step monitor?
text: In a double opt-in flow, what does the Wait Until Event step monitor? The transactional confirmation email (flow action to monitor) and the opt-in confirmation link/CTA (link to monitor).

title: Preference Page Metrics — A client's Email Opt-Out Rate looks suspiciously low despite many preference pag
text: A client's Email Opt-Out Rate looks suspiciously low despite many preference page unsubscribes. What is the cause? Preference Page unsubscribes are processed as consent updates, not Email Engagement Unsubscribe events — so they are excluded from the Email Opt-Out Rate.

title: Channel Opt-Out Scope — A contact opts out of SMS. What is the scope of that opt-out, and how does it di
text: A contact opts out of SMS. What is the scope of that opt-out, and how does it differ from email and WhatsApp? SMS opt-out is per sender code. Email is per subscription + channel. WhatsApp is per contact point (blocked in-app).

title: Unsubscribe All — A contact clicks "Unsubscribe from all". Does this create a permanent block on a
text: A contact clicks "Unsubscribe from all". Does this create a permanent block on all future sends? No — "Unsubscribe from all" does not persist as a permanent block.

title: Never Delete a Subscription — A client wants to tidy up by deleting an unused Communication Subscription. What
text: A client wants to tidy up by deleting an unused Communication Subscription. What should the consultant advise? Never delete a Communication Subscription — it destroys the audit trail.

title: Transactional Consent — A client sends OTP codes via SMS and believes consent is not required because th
text: A client sends OTP codes via SMS and believes consent is not required because the messages are transactional. Are they correct? No — transactional SMS (OTP/2FA) still requires consent (TCPA). Transactional email consent is off by default, but selecting a Communication Subscription turns it on.

title: Spam Complaint — A contact files a spam complaint, which is processed via the feedback loop and R
text: A contact files a spam complaint, which is processed via the feedback loop and Reply Mail Management. What is the opt-out scope? All current subscriptions — there is no channel-level or account-level opt-out today.

title: Consent Banner — A client implements the consent banner on their website. They notice the first p
text: A client implements the consent banner on their website. They notice the first page view is missing from their analytics. Is this a bug? No — the first page view is not recorded when consent is required.

title: 3-Flow Consent Sync — A consultant is designing a CRM ↔ Data 360 ↔ Marketing Cloud Next consent sync.
text: A consultant is designing a CRM ↔ Data 360 ↔ Marketing Cloud Next consent sync. What is the non-negotiable rule for every consent write? All writes must use Create Consent (Data Cloud-Triggered or Automation Event-Triggered). Direct DMO field mapping is ignored at send time.

title: Consent Segmentation — A client wants to build a segment of contacts who have opted in to a specific su
text: A client wants to build a segment of contacts who have opted in to a specific subscription. What approach is required, and what is the cost implication? A Calculated Insight workaround — it is metered and consumes credits.

title: Web Tracking Scope — A client wants to understand what activity Marketing Cloud Next can capture on t
text: A client wants to understand what activity Marketing Cloud Next can capture on their website. What four activities are tracked? Page views, form submissions, link clicks, and button clicks.

title: Web Tracking Cookies — A consultant is explaining the cookies used by web tracking. Which cookie stores
text: A consultant is explaining the cookies used by web tracking. Which cookie stores the consent decision, and for how long? sfmc consent — 365 days, storing True (opted in) or False (opted out / ignored the banner).

title: First Page View — A client notices their landing page analytics are missing the very first view fr
text: A client notices their landing page analytics are missing the very first view from each visitor. Is this a tracking failure? No — when consent is required, the first page view is not recorded because it happens before the visitor has consented.

title: Landing Page Tracking Setup — A consultant is configuring web tracking on a landing page with a consent banner
text: A consultant is configuring web tracking on a landing page with a consent banner. What two integration tiles are required? The Data Cloud integration and the Data Cloud Web Tracking Consent Banner integration — then publish the site.

title: Tracking Without a Consent Banner — A client wants web tracking without displaying a consent banner. What configurat
text: A client wants web tracking without displaying a consent banner. What configuration is required? Set the security level to Relaxed CSP, add the Data Cloud integration (NOT the consent banner integration), and add the tracking code snippet to Head Markup — which dispatches a set-consent custom event.

title: External Site Tracking — A consultant needs to track activity on a client's external website. What two ar
text: A consultant needs to track activity on a client's external website. What two artefacts must be created? A Website Connector (Setup → Web Tracking → Website Connectors → New) and a Webpage Embed Code (name it, select the connector, choose the consent requirement, associate a campaign) — then add the embed code to the site's <head tag.

title: Custom Domain Tracking — A client hosts a landing page on a custom domain and wants to track activity. Wh
text: A client hosts a landing page on a custom domain and wants to track activity. What must the consultant configure? Add a custom URL for that domain in Setup and define the path as /lp .

title: Email Opt Out Sync Gap — A contact opts out via the standard Salesforce Email Opt Out field, but still re
text: A contact opts out via the standard Salesforce Email Opt Out field, but still receives marketing emails from Marketing Cloud Next. Why? HasOptedOutOfEmail does not automatically sync with the Marketing Cloud Next consent layer — you need a two-Flow bridge.

title: Two-Flow Bridge — A consultant is building the CRM ↔ MC Next consent bridge. What flow types and a
text: A consultant is building the CRM ↔ MC Next consent bridge. What flow types and actions are used in each direction? Flow 1 (CRM → MC Next): an Automation Event-Triggered Flow on the Contact/Lead using a Consent Request action. Flow 2 (MC Next → CRM): a Data Cloud-Triggered Flow using an Update Records action to set HasOptedOutOfEmail .

title: Infinite Loop Risk — A consultant builds the two-flow consent bridge and sees flows triggering each o
text: A consultant builds the two-flow consent bridge and sees flows triggering each other repeatedly. What is the cause and the fix? An infinite loop — the Data Cloud-Triggered Flow updating the Contact/Lead must not re-trigger Flow 1. Review trigger conditions carefully.

title: Hybrid Sending — A client runs Marketing Cloud Account Engagement and Marketing Cloud Next side b
text: A client runs Marketing Cloud Account Engagement and Marketing Cloud Next side by side. How is consent matched between them? Automatically (Match Overall Email Consent) or manually (Match Consent and Subscriptions). For Marketing Cloud Engagement, use the Consent Mapping tool — email and SMS are available today.

title: Consent Package Install Failure — A consultant's consent package installation fails with CustomField errors on Con
text: A consultant's consent package installation fails with CustomField errors on ConsentAuditTrail. What are the two prerequisites to check? 1) Data Protection must be enabled (Set Up Data Privacy). 2) The Data Cloud Salesforce Connector permission set must grant Read and View All Records on Communication Subscription, Communication Subscription Channel Type, and Engagement Channel Type.

title: Consent Data Stream Activation — A consultant's consent data streams will not ingest on a new sandbox. What is th
text: A consultant's consent data streams will not ingest on a new sandbox. What is the most likely cause? The data streams are in a NEEDS ACTIVATION state — expected on new sandboxes because connections are not activated by default. Activate each consent data stream in Data Cloud Setup.

title: Consent Billing — A client asks whether ingesting consent into Data Cloud consumes credits. What s
text: A client asks whether ingesting consent into Data Cloud consumes credits. What should the consultant explain? No — ingestion through an internal Salesforce connector is zero-cost (since Aug 7, 2025). External ingestion (Snowflake, S3) is a different usage type and does consume credits.

title: Consent Metered Operations — Which consent-related operations DO consume credits?
text: Which consent-related operations DO consume credits? Segmentation and Calculated Insights (billed on records processed), and Identity Resolution (billed under Batch Profile Unification).

title: Duplicate Consent Records — A client ingests the same individuals from two sources and sees higher-than-expe
text: A client ingests the same individuals from two sources and sees higher-than-expected credit consumption. Why? Duplicate consent rows increase record counts that downstream metered operations process — this is a data-model design consideration, not a defect.

title: Communication Subscription Deployment — A consultant wants to deploy Communication Subscriptions from sandbox to product
text: A consultant wants to deploy Communication Subscriptions from sandbox to production. Is this supported? No — it is currently unsupported. Communication Subscriptions are stored as data in the Communication Subscription DMO, and only metadata deploys to a sandbox.

title: Transactional Email Consent — A client sends transactional emails and wants to be certain consent is never eva
text: A client sends transactional emails and wants to be certain consent is never evaluated. What should the consultant advise? Do not select a Communication Subscription for transactional sends. The transactional consent check is off by default, but populating a Communication Subscription at send time causes consent to be evaluated even when the global setting is disabled.

title: Opt-Out Scope by Method — A consultant is documenting how each unsubscribe method behaves. What is the sco
text: A consultant is documenting how each unsubscribe method behaves. What is the scope of an email body unsubscribe link versus a spam complaint? An email body unsubscribe link opts out of the specific Communication Subscription used on that send. A spam complaint (FBL) opts out of ALL current subscriptions.

title: Global Subscription Opt-Out — A contact opts out of a global Communication Subscription that is sendable from
text: A contact opts out of a global Communication Subscription that is sendable from any business unit. What is the effect? The opt-out applies to sends from every business unit — opt-outs are independent of sending domain and business unit.

title: Opt-Out of All Behaviour — A contact performs an "opt out of all" action, then an admin later creates a new
text: A contact performs an "opt out of all" action, then an admin later creates a new subscription and opts them into it. Can the contact receive marketing again? Yes — "opt out of all" opts the recipient out of each of their current subscriptions individually. A newly created subscription is not covered, so the contact could receive marketing based on it.

title: Consent Troubleshooting Step 1 — A client reports "I opted out but I'm still receiving emails". What is the first
text: A client reports "I opted out but I'm still receiving emails". What is the first troubleshooting step? Confirm the consent record in the CSC DMO — open Data Cloud → Data Explorer → Communication Subscription Consent DMO and filter by contact point value and CSCT ID.

title: Consent Troubleshooting Step 3 — A consultant finds a mismatch between the CSC DMO and what is honoured at send t
text: A consultant finds a mismatch between the CSC DMO and what is honoured at send time. What is the next step? Identify the write path — check in order: MessagingConsent/MessagingConsentV2 flow actions, a Data Stream mapped directly to the Consent DLO, a Batch Data Transform writing to the Consent DLO, a Data Cloud Ingestion API call writing to the Consent DMO, or a custom integration writing consent fields directly. Any of these is an unsupported write path.

title: Consent Repair Paths — A consultant has identified stale consent records and needs to repair them. What
text: A consultant has identified stale consent records and needs to repair them. What are the three repair paths by volume? Single record/small set → update via the Consent Status LWC. Bulk (≤50k rows) → Consent Import CSV. Bulk ( 50k rows) → stage into a custom DMO, then run a Data Cloud-Triggered Flow calling Create Consent.

title: Consent Troubleshooting Step 5 — What is the final step of consent troubleshooting, and why does it matter?
text: What is the final step of consent troubleshooting, and why does it matter? Prevent recurrence — audit flows for MessagingConsent/MessagingConsentV2 and replace with Create Consent; audit Data Streams and Batch Data Transforms targeting the Consent DLO and reroute through a Data Cloud-Triggered Flow; audit Ingestion API and custom integrations for direct Consent DMO writes.

title: Three Consent Models — A client has meticulously maintained ContactPointTypeConsent records for GDPR pr
text: A client has meticulously maintained ContactPointTypeConsent records for GDPR proof, yet promotional emails are still blocked. What is the consultant's explanation? Salesforce contains three separate consent models, and Marketing Cloud Next reads only Communication Subscription Consent (through the cache). A perfectly maintained ContactPointTypeConsent record has no bearing on whether an email goes out.

title: Consent Object Id Prefixes — A consultant is documenting the consent objects. Which are CRM objects, and what
text: A consultant is documenting the consent objects. Which are CRM objects, and what are their Id prefixes? Communication Subscription ( 0Xl ), Engagement Channel Type ( 0eF ) and Communication Subscription Channel Type ( 0eB ) are CRM objects. The consent record itself (Communication Subscription Consent) lives in Data 360 only.

title: Subscription Governance — A client wants to change a Communication Subscription's scope from a single busi
text: A client wants to change a Communication Subscription's scope from a single business unit to all business units after go-live. What should the consultant advise? The scope cannot be changed after creation. With business units enabled (Advanced), a subscription is assigned either to a single business unit or to all of them, and this is fixed at creation — it also limits which channels can be added.

title: Duplicate Consent Streams — A consultant pulls a consent export and finds duplicate rows for the same contac
text: A consultant pulls a consent export and finds duplicate rows for the same contact point and subscription, in an org that has only ever run V2. What explains this? The org-ID naming quirk — Salesforce appended the org ID to the V2 stream names, both spellings stayed active, and both feed the same DMO. This is not a legacy migration artefact.

title: Consent DLO Name Portability — A consultant copies a consent query from a blog post into a Data Transform and i
text: A consultant copies a consent query from a blog post into a Data Transform and it fails. Why? No consent DLO name is portable — the org ID is appended to the stream name, so it differs per org (and changes when the org ID changes). Always read the actual stream name in your own org first.

title: Consent-Check Applicability — A client wants to disable consent checks entirely because consent is managed on
text: A client wants to disable consent checks entirely because consent is managed on another platform. What must they accept, and what does the change not affect? They must affirm in writing that they accept responsibility for compliance problems. The change does not affect active flows — anything already running keeps checking.

title: SMS/WhatsApp/RCS Granularity — A contact opts out of an SMS channel that maps to three subscriptions. What is t
text: A contact opts out of an SMS channel that maps to three subscriptions. What is the effect, and how does RCS differ? Opting out of the channel opts the person out of every subscription mapped to it — there is no per-subscription opt-out over SMS. RCS is the one exception: Salesforce says you can reuse existing SMS consent when the messaging use case stays the same.

title: The Party Field — A developer wants to build a segment filter on the consent DMO's Party field to
text: A developer wants to build a segment filter on the consent DMO's Party field to target individuals. What should the consultant advise? Don't build on the Party field — it is wired end to end from the DLO but always empty. To get from a consent record to a person, go through the Contact Point Email or Contact Point Phone DMO.

title: Four Levels of Consent Granularity — A client's compliance team asks the consultant to explain how granular Marketing
text: A client's compliance team asks the consultant to explain how granular Marketing Cloud Next consent can be. Which level does the platform enforce? Level 4 — a specific contact point (email address or phone number) AND a specific subscription type.

title: The Four Consent Objects — A consultant is mapping the consent data model for a client. Which four objects
text: A consultant is mapping the consent data model for a client. Which four objects come together to manage Level 4 consent, and what does each represent? Communication Subscription (the type/purpose/category of communication) · Communication Subscription Channel Type (the channel used to deliver a subscription) · Communication Subscription Consent (the individual's consent status for a subscription at a specific contact point value + subscription channel type) · Engagement Channel Type (the channel: email, SMS, WhatsApp, RCS).

title: Preference Page Channel Behaviour — A client wants a single preference page where subscribers can manage both email
text: A client wants a single preference page where subscribers can manage both email and SMS preferences. What should the consultant advise? A unified cross-channel preference page isn't available out-of-the-box. The message channel automatically determines which page is used — email links to the email preference manager, SMS uses a separate SMS-specific page. A unified experience requires custom development.

title: Preference Page Customisation Limits — A marketer wants to edit the button labels and reorder the subscription list on
text: A marketer wants to edit the button labels and reorder the subscription list on the standard preference page. What can they do? The standard subscription block doesn't allow editing button labels, headings, subheadings, or the order of the subscription list. As a partial workaround, rename the communication subscriptions from the Consent tab. Full text customisation is planned for an upcoming release.
