title: Preference Page Releases — A client asks when custom preference pages and multiple preference pages became
text: A client asks when custom preference pages and multiple preference pages became available. What should the consultant say? Custom preference pages were introduced in the Spring release; the Summer release expanded the capability to allow multiple preference pages (for example, separate pages per brand).

title: Data Layers — A consultant is explaining the data architecture to a client. A field exists in
text: A consultant is explaining the data architecture to a client. A field exists in the raw ingested data but is not available for personalization. What is the most likely explanation? The field has not been explicitly added to the data graph. Data in Data 360 does not automatically become available everywhere.

title: Ingestion Lags — A client updates a contact's email address in the source system and expects the
text: A client updates a contact's email address in the source system and expects the change to be reflected in a segment immediately. What should the consultant explain about timing? Expect staged lags: DLO 3 min (CDC) / 10 min (batch) · DMO same cycle · identity resolution once per day · segment 15–30 min · data graph up to 24 hours.

title: Identity Resolution Purpose — A client has the same person appearing as a Lead and a Contact with different em
text: A client has the same person appearing as a Lead and a Contact with different email addresses. What mechanism unifies them into a single profile? Identity resolution — it matches source records into a Unified Individual via rulesets.

title: Ruleset Count — A client wants to run two active identity resolution rulesets on the Individual
text: A client wants to run two active identity resolution rulesets on the Individual object to improve matching. What should the consultant advise? Recommend one active ruleset per object (Individual + Account) — running two doubles billing.

title: Match Rule vs Criteria — A consultant wants to increase consolidation so more records merge into unified
text: A consultant wants to increase consolidation so more records merge into unified profiles. Should they add more match rules or more match criteria? Add more match rules. More rules → higher consolidation; more criteria → lower consolidation.

title: Match Methods — A client's data has inconsistent email formatting — some addresses have trailing
text: A client's data has inconsistent email formatting — some addresses have trailing spaces and Gmail addresses use dots and plus-addressing. Which match method should the consultant use? Exact Normalized.

title: Fuzzy Matching — A client wants to match on Account names that are spelled slightly differently.
text: A client wants to match on Account names that are spelled slightly differently. What should the consultant know about fuzzy matching for Account fields? Fuzzy matching uses a BERT AI model with a 0.7 confidence threshold — but it is not available for Account fields.

title: Real-Time Matching — A client needs real-time identity resolution. Which match methods will actually
text: A client needs real-time identity resolution. Which match methods will actually be used, regardless of the scheduled method configured? All criteria run Exact, except phone and email which run Exact Normalized.

title: Match on Blank — A client enables "Match on Blank" to improve consolidation and then sees an erro
text: A client enables "Match on Blank" to improve consolidation and then sees an error about 50,000+ profiles. What is the cause? Match on Blank is ignored in real-time and can cause overmatching — the "50,000+ profiles" error.

title: Single Contact Point — A consultant proposes matching individuals on email address alone to maximise co
text: A consultant proposes matching individuals on email address alone to maximise consolidation. What is the risk? Matching on a single contact point mixes household members into one profile — except when using unique external IDs.

title: Default Rules — How many default match rules exist for Accounts, Individuals, and Households?
text: How many default match rules exist for Accounts, Individuals, and Households? Accounts = 2 · Individuals = 4 · Households = 1.

title: Known Profiles — A client asks when a unified profile is considered "known" for entitlement purpo
text: A client asks when a unified profile is considered "known" for entitlement purposes. What should the consultant explain? A profile is known if any source profile is known; account profiles are always known. Known profiles from all rulesets count toward entitlement.

title: Reconciliation Purpose — A unified profile has three different first names from three source systems. Wha
text: A unified profile has three different first names from three source systems. What determines which one is displayed? Reconciliation rules — they select a single value for a unified field that cannot hold multiple values.

title: Reconciliation vs Contact Points — A client wants to use reconciliation rules to control which phone number is used
text: A client wants to use reconciliation rules to control which phone number is used in an activation. Is this the right approach? No — reconciliation rules do not govern contact points. All contact points stay in the unified profile; use source priority in activations instead.

title: Segment Types — A client needs a segment that evaluates in milliseconds on demand, with no sched
text: A client needs a segment that evaluates in milliseconds on demand, with no scheduled publish. Which segment type should the consultant use, and what are its limitations? A real-time segment. It cannot use exclusion, nesting, or counts, and cannot be manually published. It requires Segment ID + Timestamp in the real-time graph.

title: Waterfall Segment — A client wants to present mutually exclusive offers in priority order, so each c
text: A client wants to present mutually exclusive offers in priority order, so each contact receives only the highest-priority offer they qualify for. Which segment type applies, and what is the limit? A waterfall segment — priority-ranked and mutually exclusive, with a maximum of 20 segments, one waterfall each, and no rapid publish.

title: Dynamic Segment — A client wants to pass parameters at runtime so the same segment definition prod
text: A client wants to pass parameters at runtime so the same segment definition produces different audiences per API call. Which segment type should the consultant use? A dynamic segment — it uses parameterized placeholders and is run via API or broadcast flow. It does not persist.

title: Segment Limits — A consultant is designing a complex segment. What are the key limits to respect?
text: A consultant is designing a complex segment. What are the key limits to respect? 9,950 segments per org · 50 filters per tab · 100 attributes · 20 filters per container · nest 3 levels within a container / 10 across the segment.

title: Lookback Window — A client needs a segment that looks back two years. Is this possible, and what i
text: A client needs a segment that looks back two years. Is this possible, and what is the default? Yes — the default lookback is 90 days and the maximum is 2 years. Container criteria override the segment-level setting.

title: Publish Cadence — A client needs a segment refreshed every 15 minutes. What should the consultant
text: A client needs a segment refreshed every 15 minutes. What should the consultant recommend, and what are the caveats? Rapid publish (1/4h). Caveats: maximum 20 rapid segments, SFMC/file storage only, and it cannot be converted to standard.

title: Composite Keys — A consultant wants to join two DMOs in the segment canvas using a two-field comp
text: A consultant wants to join two DMOs in the segment canvas using a two-field composite key. Is this supported? No — composite keys are unsupported in the canvas. Only single-field joins are allowed; use single unique primary key DMOs.

title: Prospect vs Lead — A client's marketing team has captured a contact who filled in a form once and h
text: A client's marketing team has captured a contact who filled in a form once and has no sales owner. Is this a Prospect or a Lead? A Prospect — top of funnel, unqualified, marketing-owned, may have interacted once, no owner, low-to-medium conversion potential.

title: Unified Individual Creation — A client wants to manually create Unified Individual records for a test. Is this
text: A client wants to manually create Unified Individual records for a test. Is this possible? No — Individual and Unified Individual records can only be created via sync and harmonization.

title: Prospect to Contact Conversion — A client wants to automatically convert Prospects to Contacts when they become q
text: A client wants to automatically convert Prospects to Contacts when they become qualified. What should the consultant configure? A Record-Triggered Flow on Prospect created/updated (e.g., ProspectStatus = Qualified) using the Convert Prospect action.

title: Conversion Overwrite — A Prospect is converted to an existing Lead that already has a populated Phone f
text: A Prospect is converted to an existing Lead that already has a populated Phone field. The Prospect has a different phone number. What happens? Only empty fields are overwritten — the existing Lead's populated Phone is preserved.

title: Multi-Currency Conversion — A Prospect and an existing Account have different currency codes. Which wins on
text: A Prospect and an existing Account have different currency codes. Which wins on conversion? The prospect's currency code wins — this avoids conversion problems.

title: Title Length Trap — A client reports that prospect-to-lead conversion is failing for certain records
text: A client reports that prospect-to-lead conversion is failing for certain records. The prospects have job titles up to 120 characters. What is the cause? A lead Title greater than 80 characters breaks conversion — the prospect allows 128, but the lead does not.

title: Custom Required Fields — A client added a custom required field to the Lead object. Now prospect-to-lead
text: A client added a custom required field to the Lead object. Now prospect-to-lead conversion fails. Why? Custom required fields on the Lead object block prospect-to-lead conversion.

title: Prospect Restrictions — A client wants to add Prospects as campaign members and bulk-delete stale ones.
text: A client wants to add Prospects as campaign members and bulk-delete stale ones. What should the consultant advise? Prospects cannot be added as campaign members, are not in the Data Import Wizard, and cannot be cloned or bulk deleted.

title: Actionable List — A client wants a static collection of contacts for a one-off send. What should t
text: A client wants a static collection of contacts for a one-off send. What should the consultant create, and what is the key constraint? An actionable list — a static collection of leads OR contacts (never both), used with a list-triggered flow.

title: Marketing Object Storage — A client on the Growth tier needs to store 30 marketing objects totalling 15GB.
text: A client on the Growth tier needs to store 30 marketing objects totalling 15GB. Is this possible? No — Growth allows 10GB and 25 objects. Advanced allows 40GB and 100 objects.

title: Marketing Object Immutability — A consultant needs to change a marketing object field from Text to Number and re
text: A consultant needs to change a marketing object field from Text to Number and rename its API name. What must they do? Delete and recreate the field — field API name, data type, and primary key designation are immutable after creation. Deleting the field deletes its data.

title: Marketing Object Delete — A client wants to delete a marketing object that is referenced by another object
text: A client wants to delete a marketing object that is referenced by another object. What happens? The delete is blocked if any other object references it. Deletion is otherwise permanent — all data is gone and cannot be restored.

title: Marketing Object Permissions — A user needs to view marketing object records but must not be able to create or
text: A user needs to view marketing object records but must not be able to create or delete objects. Which permission should be assigned? ViewAllMarketingObjectRecords (view only) — as opposed to ManageMarketingObjects (view + create/delete).

title: Segmentation Credits — A client asks when segmentation credits are consumed. What should the consultant
text: A client asks when segmentation credits are consumed. What should the consultant explain? On publish.

title: Cost Reduction — A client's Data 360 credit consumption is higher than expected. What four levers
text: A client's Data 360 credit consumption is higher than expected. What four levers should the consultant recommend? Fewer schedules, tighter lookback windows, preview before publish, and nesting common filters.

title: Internal Pipeline Cost — A client ingests data from Salesforce CRM and Marketing Cloud. Are they charged
text: A client ingests data from Salesforce CRM and Marketing Cloud. Are they charged for this ingestion? No — the Internal Data Pipeline is free (since Aug 7, 2025) for Salesforce CRM, Marketing Cloud, Commerce Cloud, and Personalization connectors.

title: Streaming Activation Cost — A client uses Activate DMO - Streaming with a data graph. How is this charged?
text: A client uses Activate DMO - Streaming with a data graph. How is this charged? Per record created/updated per activation — and the cost doubles if a data graph is used.

title: Batch Calculated Insights — A client runs a Calculated Insight that references the same object three times.
text: A client runs a Calculated Insight that references the same object three times. How is it charged? Charged only when underlying objects change, and objects used multiple times are counted once.

title: Minimum Decrement — A client's usage is fractional across the month. What is the minimum credit decr
text: A client's usage is fractional across the month. What is the minimum credit decrement? 1 per usage type (when fractional usage ≥ 1 over the month).

title: Retired Billing Card — Which billing card was retired on Sept 4, 2025, and what replaced it?
text: Which billing card was retired on Sept 4, 2025, and what replaced it? The "Segmentation and Activation" card was retired and merged into the Data Services card.

title: Direct vs Related Attributes — A consultant is building a segment and needs to filter on purchase history. Is p
text: A consultant is building a segment and needs to filter on purchase history. Is purchase history a direct or related attribute? A related attribute — it is a collection of data points (1:N, one customer to many orders). Direct attributes are single data points (1:1 or N:1), such as postal code or first name.

title: Containers and AND Logic — A client wants to find customers who bought a yellow scarf in a single order. Sh
text: A client wants to find customers who bought a yellow scarf in a single order. Should the "yellow" and "scarf" filters go in the same container or separate containers? The same container — attributes in the same container act on the same data row (AND logic on one record). Separate containers apply independently, so "yellow" in one and "scarf" in another would match anyone who bought any yellow product AND any scarf.

title: Aggregation Types — A client wants to target customers with at least five purchases. Which aggregati
text: A client wants to target customers with at least five purchases. Which aggregation type applies? Count — it defines how many times criteria must be met. The other types are Sum, Average, Max, and Min.

title: Case-Sensitive Joins — A consultant's segment returns fewer records than expected. The join is on an em
text: A consultant's segment returns fewer records than expected. The join is on an email address field. What should they check? Joins are case-sensitive — mismatched case means records do not link.

title: Primary and Foreign Keys — A consultant cannot find the primary key attribute on the segment canvas. Why?
text: A consultant cannot find the primary key attribute on the segment canvas. Why? Primary key and foreign key attributes do not appear on the canvas. To use them, create a custom attribute that is not assigned as a PK or FK.

title: Container Paths — A consultant is building a segment on an order object that has both a Buyer ID a
text: A consultant is building a segment on an order object that has both a Buyer ID and a Seller ID. Why does the path matter? When a container has multiple routes back to the segment-on entity, you must choose the path that builds the intended audience. Cyclic paths (a→b→a) degrade performance and are blocked by default.

title: Population Counts — A client wants to know how many people a segment will reach before publishing. W
text: A client wants to know how many people a segment will reach before publishing. What count should the consultant use, and what is its caveat? The Approximate Segment Population — a 95%-confidence range estimate (enable in Feature Manager). It is less accurate for small populations.

title: Value Matching — A consultant filters on a text field with the value 0852 . Will it match a recor
text: A consultant filters on a text field with the value 0852 . Will it match a record containing 852 ? No — type matching is exact. String 0852 does not equal 852 (leading zero) or "0852" (with quotes). Queries are case-insensitive for text but honour exact matching on special characters and accents.

title: Is In Operator Limits — A consultant needs to filter on 5,000 values using the Is In operator. Is this p
text: A consultant needs to filter on 5,000 values using the Is In operator. Is this possible? Yes — Is In / Is Not In accept up to 100 values, but bulk paste supports up to 10,000 for Is In .

title: Group, Rank and Limit — A client wants to target the top 10 accounts by Fit Score. Which feature applies
text: A client wants to target the top 10 accounts by Fit Score. Which feature applies, and what are the constraints? Group, Rank, and Limit — Group By (e.g. Account ID), Sort By (e.g. Fit Score descending), then Limit (top 10 per group). Max 3 group rules + 3 sort rules per ruleset.

title: Attribute Shortcuts — A consultant repeatedly navigates the same segment-on object, path, and target a
text: A consultant repeatedly navigates the same segment-on object, path, and target attribute. What should they create? An attribute shortcut — a reusable named shortcut. Limits: 500 per tenant, scoped to data space, saved at org level, packageable via DataKits.

title: Nested Segments — A client wants to reuse an existing segment as a filter inside a new segment. Wh
text: A client wants to reuse an existing segment as a filter inside a new segment. What are the modes? Nested segments — the child segment can be in Last Published Membership or Segment Criteria mode.

title: Hierarchical Aggregation — A client wants to roll up revenue across an account hierarchy. What are the limi
text: A client wants to roll up revenue across an account hierarchy. What are the limits? Hierarchical aggregation supports Account/Unified Account, up to 5 containers and 3 levels per DMO.

title: Event Time Window — A client wants to segment on engagement events from three years ago. Is this pos
text: A client wants to segment on engagement events from three years ago. Is this possible? No — engagement DMOs process up to 24 months of the event date field value.

title: Segmentation Operators — A consultant needs to filter on a date field for "the last 30 days". Which opera
text: A consultant needs to filter on a date field for "the last 30 days". Which operator applies, and what time zone is used? Last Number Of Days — date operators use the org time zone.

title: Text Operators — A consultant needs to match a text field using a regular expression. Which opera
text: A consultant needs to match a text field using a regular expression. Which operator applies? Matches (regex). Other text operators include Contains , Begins With , Exists As A Whole Word , Is In , and Is Not In .

title: Boolean and Numeric Operators — What operators are available for boolean and numeric fields in segmentation?
text: What operators are available for boolean and numeric fields in segmentation? Boolean: Is True , Is False , Has Value , No Value . Numeric: Is Equal/Less/Greater Than , Is Between , Has Value , No Value .

title: Vector Filters — A client wants to segment on unstructured text using natural language similarity
text: A client wants to segment on unstructured text using natural language similarity. Which feature applies? Vector filters (Beta) — the NLP-based Is Similar To operator for unstructured data.

title: Currency Data Type — A client operates in multiple currencies and wants to segment on a monetary thre
text: A client operates in multiple currencies and wants to segment on a monetary threshold. What should the consultant use? The currency data type — it normalises multi-currency values via a currency code during filter and aggregation.

title: Data 360 Capabilities Checklist — A consultant is preparing for the exam and asks which Data 360 capabilities they
text: A consultant is preparing for the exam and asks which Data 360 capabilities they must understand, given that Marketing Cloud Next is built on Data 360. What should they focus on? The Data 360 object model (DLOs and DMOs), data streams and DLO→DMO mapping, data spaces, data kits, calculated insights, data graphs, segmentation, activations, and identity resolution.

title: CRM Integration Timeline — A client wants to use CRM records directly as an audience source without first i
text: A client wants to use CRM records directly as an audience source without first ingesting them into Data 360. Which releases enabled this, and what did each add? Spring '26 added CRM records as an audience source (scheduled or event-based). Summer '26 added campaign members and actionable lists.

title: Sales Data Kit — A client manages customer identity outside Salesforce and wants control over whi
text: A client manages customer identity outside Salesforce and wants control over which CRM data enters Data 360. Should they deploy the Sales Data Kit? It's optional — they can skip it. But note that certain features (like reporting dashboards) then require extra configuration, and Opportunity Influence requires the Sales Data Kit.

title: Actionable List Consent Gap — A marketer imports 5,000 new trade-show leads into an actionable list and immedi
text: A marketer imports 5,000 new trade-show leads into an actionable list and immediately runs a list-triggered flow with a promotional email. The flow runs successfully but almost nobody receives the email. What is the most likely cause? Adding new leads to an actionable list does not create consent records. The leads have no consent record, so they are treated as opted out and suppressed at send time.

title: Actionable List Constraints — A client wants to build one actionable list containing both leads and contacts f
text: A client wants to build one actionable list containing both leads and contacts from a recent event. What should the consultant advise? An actionable list can contain either leads or contacts, but not both. A mixed audience requires two lists or a different mechanism such as a segment.

title: Contact Point Resolution vs Reconciliation — A unified individual has three source records containing two unique email addres
text: A unified individual has three source records containing two unique email addresses. A consultant expects reconciliation rules to select one address for sending. What actually happens? Reconciliation rules don't apply to contact points. All contact points are retained in the unified profile, and a separate message is sent to each unique email address — duplicate addresses are treated as a single contact point.

title: Contact Point Selection Methods — A consultant is configuring an audience flow that uses a segment. They need to c
text: A consultant is configuring an audience flow that uses a segment. They need to control which contact point is used at send time. What are the available methods? Four methods: (1) a data graph selected in the flow's automation properties, (2) the on-demand flow API payload, (3) the activation's source priority order, and (4) an activation template.

title: Activation Template Requirement — A consultant builds an audience flow on a segment whose segment-on object is the
text: A consultant builds an audience flow on a segment whose segment-on object is the Individual DMO (not Unified Individual). They configure a Send Email Message element but don't select an activation template. What is the problem? An activation template is required when the segment's segment-on object is NOT Unified Individual. Without it, contact point selection isn't defined for the send.

title: Personalization Method Selection — A marketing team wants to show a list of five recommended products per contact i
text: A marketing team wants to show a list of five recommended products per contact in an email, pulled from a catalog. Which personalization method should the consultant recommend? A repeater.

title: Saved Expressions — A client wants to display each contact's most recent purchase amount, reusing th
text: A client wants to display each contact's most recent purchase amount, reusing the same logic across email and SMS. Which method should the consultant use? A saved expression — it filters and sorts to return ONE value and is reusable across channels.

title: Personalization Limits — A designer has built an email with 20 personalization points and wants to add 10
text: A designer has built an email with 20 personalization points and wants to add 10 more. What should the consultant advise? The limit is 25 personalization points per item — only 5 more can be added.

title: Variations Export — A client wants to export an email with dynamic content variations and import it
text: A client wants to export an email with dynamic content variations and import it into another org. Is this possible? No — content with variations cannot be exported or imported.

title: Flow Type Selection — A client wants a flow to run when a customer submits a form, completing within a
text: A client wants a flow to run when a customer submits a form, completing within about 15 minutes. Which flow type should the consultant use? An automation event-triggered flow.

title: Activation-Triggered Flow — A client wants a flow to run whenever a Data 360 activation publishes. Which flo
text: A client wants a flow to run whenever a Data 360 activation publishes. Which flow type applies, and what is the refresh cadence? An activation-triggered flow — refresh is 10 minutes (incremental) / 24 hours (standard). It is the only Data 360 target type and uses MuleSoft or HTTP callout.

title: Broadcast Flow — A client needs a flow whose audience membership is determined after the flow sta
text: A client needs a flow whose audience membership is determined after the flow starts. Which flow type should the consultant use? A broadcast flow — it uses dynamic segments (membership after start) and can run asynchronously.

title: Campaign Flow Cardinality — A client asks whether one flow can belong to multiple campaigns. What should the
text: A client asks whether one flow can belong to multiple campaigns. What should the consultant explain? No — 1 campaign = many flows, but 1 flow = 1 campaign.

title: Flow Sharing — A consultant creates a standalone flow and expects the marketing team to see it.
text: A consultant creates a standalone flow and expects the marketing team to see it. They report it is invisible. Why? Standalone flows are private by default — share via categories + sharing rules, or manually. Flows related to a campaign inherit the campaign's sharing.

title: Flow Statuses — A client pauses a flow and asks whether it still counts as active. What should t
text: A client pauses a flow and asks whether it still counts as active. What should the consultant explain? Yes — a paused flow counts as active. Only one version can be active at a time.

title: Data Source by Component — A consultant needs to configure a decision split based on a customer attribute.
text: A consultant needs to configure a decision split based on a customer attribute. Which data source feeds decision splits? The data graph.

title: Data Graph Locking — A consultant tries to replace the data graph on an email that uses dynamic conte
text: A consultant tries to replace the data graph on an email that uses dynamic content variations. The option is unavailable. Why? The data graph is locked — it cannot be removed or replaced if the email has dynamic content variations or a recommender, or once a landing page content block is published.

title: Recommender Data Source — A client wants to remove a Personalization Recommender data source from an email
text: A client wants to remove a Personalization Recommender data source from an email. What should the consultant explain? A recommender can be replaced but not removed. It also requires ≥1 successful refresh and only works on trained recommenders on the same data graph.

title: Lookup Data Graph — A client needs to pull catalog data (non-profile data) into an email. Which data
text: A client needs to pull catalog data (non-profile data) into an email. Which data source applies, and what are the limits? A lookup data graph — for non-profile data, needs a primary key, cannot nest, and is limited to 5.

title: Changing a Data Source — A consultant changes the data source on an email after merge fields were already
text: A consultant changes the data source on an email after merge fields were already built from the old source. What must they do? Delete the merge fields, add the new source, and recreate the merge fields.

title: Combining Content Types — A client wants to combine a form and a landing page in one content item. What is
text: A client wants to combine a form and a landing page in one content item. What is the prerequisite? The data graphs must match.

title: Personalization Point — A designer adds the first variation to a subject line. What happens automaticall
text: A designer adds the first variation to a subject line. What happens automatically? The first variation auto-creates the personalization point.

title: Decision vs Targeting Rule — A consultant is configuring dynamic content. What is the difference between a de
text: A consultant is configuring dynamic content. What is the difference between a decision and a targeting rule? A decision is who is eligible (each variation maps to a decision with the same name). A targeting rule is the conditions for showing a variation (attributes, related attributes, calculated insights, segment memberships).

title: Default Variation — A client wants to change the priority of the default variation so it is evaluate
text: A client wants to change the priority of the default variation so it is evaluated first. Is this possible? No — the default variation's priority cannot be changed. It shows when no rule matches.

title: Clone vs Link — A consultant wants two components to share the same personalization logic. Shoul
text: A consultant wants two components to share the same personalization logic. Should they clone or link? Link — linking shares one personalization point. Cloning creates a separate copy.

title: Unlink — A consultant unlinks a personalization point. What is the result?
text: A consultant unlinks a personalization point. What is the result? The point is cloned ("Copy of …") so the component keeps its settings but becomes independent.

title: Repeater Behaviour — A designer changes the layout of a repeater that already has content and styling
text: A designer changes the layout of a repeater that already has content and styling. What happens? Changing the layout removes content, data, and style.

title: Objective-Based Recommender — A designer configures an objective-based recommender and sees a placeholder on t
text: A designer configures an objective-based recommender and sees a placeholder on the canvas. Is this a configuration error? No — the canvas shows a placeholder by design. Use Preview with a segment to see real output.

title: Decision Logic Methods — A consultant wants a Decision element where outcome order has no impact. Which l
text: A consultant wants a Decision element where outcome order has no impact. Which logic method should they use, and is it supported for Marketing Cloud flows? "Define with AI" evaluates outcomes simultaneously so order has no impact — but it is NOT supported for Marketing Cloud flows.

title: Decision Condition — What three parts make up a decision condition?
text: What three parts make up a decision condition? Resource (data-graph attribute) + Operator (Equals/Greater Than…) + Value.

title: Wait Element Restriction — A consultant adds a Wait element to a flow that also uses screens. What happens?
text: A consultant adds a Wait element to a flow that also uses screens. What happens? Wait elements require autolaunched flows — they cannot be mixed with screens or choice.

title: Wait Until Date — A Wait Until Date element has no time specified. When does it resume?
text: A Wait Until Date element has no time specified. When does it resume? 12 AM org time zone.

title: Wait Until Event — A consultant places a Wait Until Event element two steps after the monitored ema
text: A consultant places a Wait Until Event element two steps after the monitored email. Will it work? No — Wait Until Event must be immediately after the monitored element. Dynamic/merge-field links are also unsupported (use Any Link).

title: Path Experiment — A client wants to A/B test five email variations and have the winner selected au
text: A client wants to A/B test five email variations and have the winner selected automatically. Which feature applies, what edition is required, and when is the winner declared? A Path Experiment — requires Advanced + Personalization, and auto-declares a winner at 95% confidence (Bayesian). Max 10 variations.

title: Subflow — A consultant wants a Subflow to call a flow that contains a Wait element. Is thi
text: A consultant wants a Subflow to call a flow that contains a Wait element. Is this possible? No — a Subflow cannot call flows with wait elements. Variable API names are ≤ 40 chars, and it calls the active version (API 61.0+).

title: Get Records — A consultant configures a Get Records element to retrieve 25,000 records. What h
text: A consultant configures a Get Records element to retrieve 25,000 records. What happens? It fails — the limit is 2–20,000 records.

title: Update Records Trap — A consultant configures an Update Records element but forgets to add a filter. W
text: A consultant configures an Update Records element but forgets to add a filter. What is the effect? It updates ALL records.

title: Delete Records — Where do records deleted by a flow go, and how long are they retained?
text: Where do records deleted by a flow go, and how long are they retained? To the Recycle Bin for 15 days.

title: Transaction Completion — A flow creates a record and then immediately queries it in the next element. The
text: A flow creates a record and then immediately queries it in the next element. The query returns nothing. Why? Records change only when the transaction completes — the change is not visible mid-transaction.

title: Collection Elements — A consultant needs to sort a collection by four fields. Is this possible?
text: A consultant needs to sort a collection by four fields. Is this possible? No — Collection Sort supports up to 3 fields and modifies the collection directly.

title: Operators Restriction — A consultant wants to use the "Contains" operator as a filter condition. Is this
text: A consultant wants to use the "Contains" operator as a filter condition. Is this supported? No — Contains and Is Changed are not filter conditions. In/Not In are only available in Create/Get/Update Records.

title: Exit Rules — How many exit rules can a flow have, and when are they evaluated?
text: How many exit rules can a flow have, and when are they evaluated? Up to 10, evaluated on start/resume. Numeric attributes support aggregation (Average/Sum/Max/Min).

title: Engagement Signals — A consultant wants to use custom events from engagement signals. What edition is
text: A consultant wants to use custom events from engagement signals. What edition is required, and what are the other constraints? Advanced only for custom events. Signals use only Engagement-category DMOs, one related DMO (1:1 or many-to-one), and require an item identifier for recommenders.

title: Flow vs Org Data Graph — A consultant notices the flow uses a different data graph than the org default.
text: A consultant notices the flow uses a different data graph than the org default. Is this a problem? No — the org default data graph drives message personalization, while the flow data graph drives decisioning. They are intentionally separate.

title: Contact Point Selection — A client wants to control which phone number is sent to an activation target whe
text: A client wants to control which phone number is sent to an activation target when a contact has several. What should the consultant configure? Contact point selection (which fields go to the target) plus source priority order (which value wins).

title: Removing Any Source — A client removes "Any Source/Any Type" from their contact point configuration. W
text: A client removes "Any Source/Any Type" from their contact point configuration. What is the effect? A smaller population is targeted.

title: Copying an Email — A consultant copies an email that uses dynamic content variations and a recommen
text: A consultant copies an email that uses dynamic content variations and a recommender. What is preserved? Only default variations are copied — other variations, rules, and recommenders are not. Merge fields and repeaters are preserved.

title: Convert to Code — A designer converts an email to code view to add custom logic. What do they lose
text: A designer converts an email to code view to add custom logic. What do they lose, and can they revert? Convert to Code is one-way. It removes dynamic content (repeaters, conditional logic, content variants) and you lose drag-and-drop plus the Style tab.

title: View as Web Page — A client asks how long the View as Web Page link works and whether it shows the
text: A client asks how long the View as Web Page link works and whether it shows the original personalized content. What should the consultant explain? It works for 90 days after send, reflects the published version, and personalized values re-render against the recipient's current profile on each open.

title: Plain Text Version — A consultant manually edits the plain text version of an email. What is the cons
text: A consultant manually edits the plain text version of an email. What is the consequence? It desyncs from the HTML version — future changes are not included.

title: Test Sends — A consultant wants to send a test to 8 recipients. What should they know?
text: A consultant wants to send a test to 8 recipients. What should they know? Test sends are limited to 5 recipients, count toward message credits, and the From name must be from an authenticated domain.

title: CAN-SPAM — A client asks what is legally required in a marketing email. What should the con
text: A client asks what is legally required in a marketing email. What should the consultant state? A Physical Address merge field plus an opt-out link (Unsubscribe / Preference Manager / custom preference page).

title: Dynamic From/Reply — A client wants the From address to vary per sender while avoiding DMARC alignmen
text: A client wants the From address to vary per sender while avoiding DMARC alignment failures. What should the consultant recommend? A static From address with a dynamic display name — this uses subdomain senders and avoids DMARC alignment failures.

title: Direct Reply vs RMM — A client wants auto-replies and out-of-office processing on replies. Should they
text: A client wants auto-replies and out-of-office processing on replies. Should they use direct reply or Reply Mail Management? RMM — direct reply bypasses RMM, so there is no auto-reply, out-of-office, or unsubscribe processing.

title: Distributed Marketing Limits — A client wants to lock certain images so non-marketers cannot change them. Is th
text: A client wants to lock certain images so non-marketers cannot change them. Is this possible? No — only phrases can be required (locked); images cannot. The limits are 30 approved images + 30 approved phrases, with only one default image.

title: Distributed Marketing Availability — A consultant is configuring Distributed Marketing availability. What flow type a
text: A consultant is configuring Distributed Marketing availability. What flow type and event are required? An event-triggered flow with the Distributed Marketing and Alerts Message event. Get Records (List Email) + Decision (Status = Scheduled) prevent canceled sends.

title: Unschedule Behaviour — A user unschedules an email in a campaign. What happens to other emails schedule
text: A user unschedules an email in a campaign. What happens to other emails scheduled with it? Unschedule cancels the email — and any others scheduled with it in the campaign.

title: Landing Page URL Alias — A consultant needs to change a landing page's vanity URL. When can this be done?
text: A consultant needs to change a landing page's vanity URL. When can this be done? In Draft only — publishing activates aliases. Alias statuses are Draft / Active / Inactive (reactivatable).

title: Redirect URL — A client wants to set a redirect URL for an unpublished landing page. What are t
text: A client wants to set a redirect URL for an unpublished landing page. What are the requirements? It must start with https:// and be under 2,000 characters. Set it up before unpublishing to avoid the "URL no longer exists" page.

title: Form Visibility — A client has built a form and added it to a landing page, but visitors cannot se
text: A client has built a form and added it to a landing page, but visitors cannot see it. What is the likely cause? The landing page must be published with an active URL alias for the form to be visible.

title: Landing Page SEO — A client wants to add custom JavaScript to a landing page for SEO. Is this allow
text: A client wants to add custom JavaScript to a landing page for SEO. Is this allowed? No — only JSON-LD structured data is allowed (no JavaScript). Allowed tags are <link , <meta , and <script .

title: Template Locking Scope — A client locks a landing page template to prevent authors changing personalizati
text: A client locks a landing page template to prevent authors changing personalization logic. Will this work? No — template locking protects content/settings only. Authors can still edit targeting rules and variations. Clone the personalization point for logic control.

title: Form Cardinality — A client wants two forms on one landing page, each with its own flow. Is this po
text: A client wants two forms on one landing page, each with its own flow. Is this possible? No — one form per landing page and one flow per form. View modes must also match (block ↔ block, code ↔ code).

title: Form Write Data Provider — A consultant configures a form's write data provider. What are the rules?
text: A consultant configures a form's write data provider. What are the rules? Account/Contact/Lead/Prospect or a marketing object (default if available, else Lead); one object at a time; respects FLS.

title: Form Read Data Providers — A client wants to pre-fill form fields and use progressive profiling. What is th
text: A client wants to pre-fill form fields and use progressive profiling. What is the maximum number of lookup providers? 2 — a maximum of 1 marketing object plus 1 recipient data graph.

title: Unsupported Form Field Types — A client wants to add a "Number of Employees" field and a multi-picklist to a fo
text: A client wants to add a "Number of Employees" field and a multi-picklist to a form. Is this supported? No — Number of Employees and multi-picklist are unsupported. Also, no duplicate fields, and changing a field's API name breaks future saves.

title: Hidden Fields — A consultant adds a hidden required field to a form. What is required?
text: A consultant adds a hidden required field to a form. What is required? A fallback value — hidden required fields need one. Supported hidden types are Checkbox/Dropdown/Number/Plain Text/Text Area, and URL parameters (UTM) are supported.

title: reCAPTCHA — A client enables reCAPTCHA v2. What are the scope and caveats?
text: A client enables reCAPTCHA v2. What are the scope and caveats? It applies to marketing landing pages with forms only, applies to every form once enabled, is one per external page, and changing My Domain breaks it.

title: Progressive Profiling — A client wants to use progressive profiling with rules on hidden fields. Is this
text: A client wants to use progressive profiling with rules on hidden fields. Is this supported? No — there are no rules on hidden fields or related objects. Progressive profiling needs a read data provider, and changing the read source removes rule connections. Avoid pre-filling PII.

title: Unpublishing a Form — A client unpublishes a form to make edits. What happens?
text: A client unpublishes a form to make edits. What happens? It deactivates its flow, Submit stops working, and you must save the flow as a new version to edit and republish.

title: External Form Embedding — A consultant is embedding a Marketing Cloud Next form on an external website. Wh
text: A consultant is embedding a Marketing Cloud Next form on an external website. What does the embedding code consist of? 2 <script tags + 1 <fragment element, generated from the published version (republish to refresh).

title: External Form Security — A client embeds a form externally and sees a frame-ancestors 'self' CSP error. W
text: A client embeds a form externally and sees a frame-ancestors 'self' CSP error. What is the cause? The Experience Cloud site was not published after configuring CORS Allowed Origin List, clickjack protection, and Trusted Sites for Scripts.

title: Form Handler Field Names — A client's form handler is not capturing data correctly. The external form uses
text: A client's form handler is not capturing data correctly. The external form uses field names like first name . What is the likely cause? External field names must exactly match the HTML name attributes. Date = YYYY-MM-DD ; Time = hh:mm:ss ; DateTime = ISO 8601; selected checkbox = true .

title: Form Handler Mapping Timing — A consultant creates a form handler flow and then adds a new field mapping. Will
text: A consultant creates a form handler flow and then adds a new field mapping. Will the flow pick it up? No — map all fields before creating the flow. Edits afterwards do not reflect automatically.

title: Client vs Server Side Form Handlers — A client needs form handler submissions to support web tracking and identity res
text: A client needs form handler submissions to support web tracking and identity resolution, but their site has a strict CSP. Which approach should the consultant recommend? Neither fully satisfies both — client-side (JS snippet) supports web tracking + identity resolution; server-side (direct POST URL) has no tracking/identity resolution but works with strict CSP. Both need a CORS Allowlist entry.

title: Campaign Stage — A campaign has five flows; four completed successfully and one errored. What doe
text: A campaign has five flows; four completed successfully and one errored. What does the Campaign Stage show? Error — one Error flow makes the whole campaign Error.

title: Marketing Calendar — A client cannot find their form-triggered flow on the Marketing Calendar. Why?
text: A client cannot find their form-triggered flow on the Marketing Calendar. Why? Event-triggered and form-triggered flows do not appear on the Marketing Calendar. It shows Campaigns + Campaign Segment Flows + Segment Flows by default.

title: NotSentReason — A client wants to understand why emails were not sent. Which field should the co
text: A client wants to understand why emails were not sent. Which field should the consultant point to? NotSentReason — it maps to Engagement Action Reason on the Email Engagement DMO. Common values: no consent, no opt-in, unauthorized From, hard bounce, TTL exceeded.

title: On-Canvas Analytics — A client wants to view element-level analytics for a flow run from Winter '24. I
text: A client wants to view element-level analytics for a flow run from Winter '24. Is this possible? No — on-canvas analytics is not available for runs before Winter '25. It also requires Tableau Next Included App Business User, and opening element details consumes Data Cloud credits.

title: AI Campaigns — A consultant uses Agentforce to draft a campaign. What does the agent produce, a
text: A consultant uses Agentforce to draft a campaign. What does the agent produce, and what powers the agent actions? A brief plus a campaign preview (name, flow, multichannel content). Agent actions (Create/Draft/Save Brief, Save Campaign) are powered by Salesforce Flow. Generate Campaign Insights analyses the first flow.

title: CMS Content Types — A consultant is explaining where marketing content lives. What does Salesforce C
text: A consultant is explaining where marketing content lives. What does Salesforce CMS provide in Marketing Cloud Next? Salesforce CMS is the content repository — it holds content types (email, landing page, form, image, expression), organised into workspaces, with contributor roles controlling who can edit and publish.

title: Campaign Record vs Flow Canvas — A consultant needs to configure decision branching and wait configuration. Where
text: A consultant needs to configure decision branching and wait configuration. Where should they work? The Flow Builder canvas — the campaign record shows flow summaries and insights, while advanced elements (decision branching, wait configuration) live in Flow Builder.

title: Creating the First Flow — A client wants a preconfigured flow with CMS content they can customise. Which c
text: A client wants a preconfigured flow with CMS content they can customise. Which creation method should the consultant recommend? Quick start — it provides a common campaign use case with a preconfigured flow including CMS content (e.g. a customisable email).

title: Saved Expressions — A marketer wants a merge field to return the most recent opportunity for an acco
text: A marketer wants a merge field to return the most recent opportunity for an account. What should the consultant create? A saved expression — it defines filter and sort options across related data objects to select the right attribute for a merge field. It is stored in Salesforce CMS and reusable across email, SMS, and WhatsApp.

title: Expression Permissions — A consultant needs to create an expression and then publish it. What permissions
text: A consultant needs to create an expression and then publish it. What permissions are required for each step? Create/edit: Marketing Cloud Manager permission set AND any CMS workspace contributor role. Publish/unpublish: Marketing Cloud Manager AND a CMS workspace contributor role of content admin or content manager.

title: Merge Field Placement — Where can a marketer add merge fields in an email?
text: Where can a marketer add merge fields in an email? In the subject line and preheader (via Add Merge Field), and in the text of content (via the Add Merge Field icon in a text-based component's editing toolbar).

title: SMS/WhatsApp Merge Fields — A consultant is configuring merge fields for an SMS message and cannot find the
text: A consultant is configuring merge fields for an SMS message and cannot find the data source in the Data Sources panel. Why? SMS and WhatsApp merge fields use the default data graph configured in Setup — it does not appear in the Data Sources panel, but its data works in merge fields.

title: Signup Form Template — A consultant uses the signup form flow template. What does it automatically crea
text: A consultant uses the signup form flow template. What does it automatically create? A Flow + a Form + (optionally) a Landing page — automatically created and related.

title: Pause and Wait Interaction — A flow has a 48-hour Wait element. It is paused 12 hours in, and 24 hours elapse
text: A flow has a 48-hour Wait element. It is paused 12 hours in, and 24 hours elapse before resuming. When does the next email send? 24 hours after resume — pause duration counts toward the Wait element's total time.

title: Editing a Paused Flow — A consultant needs to edit an active flow. What is the correct procedure?
text: A consultant needs to edit an active flow. What is the correct procedure? Deactivate (choosing either "Deactivate and cancel work" or "Deactivate and complete work") → Edit As New Version (the version number is appended to the name) → Activate.

title: Changing an Active Flow's Campaign — A consultant needs to associate an active flow with a different campaign. What s
text: A consultant needs to associate an active flow with a different campaign. What should they know? Changing the association for an active flow causes reporting and data stream issues. For a draft flow, update the Associated Record field on the flow record.

title: Campaign Deletion — A client deletes a campaign that has flows associated with it. What happens to t
text: A client deletes a campaign that has flows associated with it. What happens to the flows? The relationship is removed but the flows remain intact. Sharing reverts to the flow's own rules (or private: owner, admins, View All Non-Setup Flows / Manage Flow).

title: Flow Sharing Categories — A consultant is configuring dynamic sharing for a standalone flow. What is the m
text: A consultant is configuring dynamic sharing for a standalone flow. What is the matching rule for category and subcategory? With the Equals operator, category/subcategory must match exactly. With Contains, it only needs to include the rule's category.

title: Marketing Triggers — A client wants to trigger a flow when a shopper abandons a cart. Which trigger a
text: A client wants to trigger a flow when a shopper abandons a cart. Which trigger applies, and what is the inactivity range? The Abandoned Shopping Cart trigger — inactivity period ranges from 10 minutes to 7 days.

title: Inactivity vs Job Frequency — A consultant is configuring a marketing trigger and sees both "Inactivity Period
text: A consultant is configuring a marketing trigger and sees both "Inactivity Period" and "Job Frequency". What is the difference? Inactivity Period is the wait after the last interaction; Job Frequency is how often the trigger job runs. They combine to determine when a shopper qualifies.

title: Product Triggers — What is the difference between the "Product Back In Stock" and "Product Low Inve
text: What is the difference between the "Product Back In Stock" and "Product Low Inventory" triggers? Back In Stock fires when an unavailable product becomes available (lookback period 1–60 days). Low Inventory fires when stock falls below a threshold (1–1M units).

title: Order Lifecycle API Events — A client's external commerce system needs to trigger flows on order events. What
text: A client's external commerce system needs to trigger flows on order events. What mechanism applies? Order Lifecycle API automation events — Order Status via API, Order Shipment Status via API, and Order Return via API. The external system POSTs to /services/data/<api version /actions/custom/flow/flowApiName .

title: REST API Flow Execution — A consultant needs to start a flow from an external system via REST API. Which f
text: A consultant needs to start a flow from an external system via REST API. Which flow type is required, and which version runs? Only autolaunched flows can be started via REST API, and the call runs the active version.

title: Multiple Flow Instances — A consultant needs to run the same flow for 100 records in one REST call. How sh
text: A consultant needs to run the same flow for 100 records in one REST call. How should they structure the request? Include multiple objects in the inputs array — each runs as a separate flow execution in a single transaction, with bulkifiable elements running as a bulkified operation.

title: Invocable.Action vs Flow.Interview — A consultant needs to run flows in batches from Apex with bulkification. Which c
text: A consultant needs to run flows in batches from Apex with bulkification. Which class should they use? Invocable.Action — it runs flows in batches with bulkification and references flows dynamically (string name, no referential integrity). Flow.Interview references flows statically (referential integrity) and cannot run in batches via bulkification.

title: Flow Version from Apex — A consultant starts a flow from Apex as a flow admin. Which version runs?
text: A consultant starts a flow from Apex as a flow admin. Which version runs? The latest version, regardless of activation status. (By contrast, REST API runs the active version.)

title: Marketing Sites vs Landing Pages Site — A consultant needs to host a code-view landing page. Which site should they use?
text: A consultant needs to host a code-view landing page. Which site should they use? A marketing site — it hosts code-view landing pages and forms. Component/template-based landing pages live on the auto-generated Marketing Landing Pages site.

title: Marketing Site Languages — A client wants to publish a landing page in French, but their site's default loc
text: A client wants to publish a landing page in French, but their site's default locale is English. What must the consultant do? Add French as a supported language on the Languages tab, then republish the site.

title: Marketing Site Security Tab — What does the Security tab of a marketing site control?
text: What does the Security tab of a marketing site control? CSP security level, trusted sites for scripts, clickjack protection, cookie policy, and Lightning Web Security — plus trusted domains for script hosts.

title: Marketing Site Integrations — Which integrations can be configured on a marketing site?
text: Which integrations can be configured on a marketing site? Data 360, Data 360 Web Tracking Consent Banner, Google Analytics 4, and Meta Pixel.

title: MCE Journey Association — A consultant wants to connect an MCE journey to a campaign. What are the constra
text: A consultant wants to connect an MCE journey to a campaign. What are the constraints? The journey cannot already be connected to a campaign, can be connected to only one campaign, must be in Draft/Running/Finishing/Paused/Stopped mode, and there is a limit of 20 journeys per campaign.

title: Journey Historical Reporting — A client connects a running journey to a campaign and sees analytics going back
text: A client connects a running journey to a campaign and sees analytics going back further than the connection date. Why? For a running journey, Salesforce attempts to associate historical send and engagement data to the newly-associated campaign — the amount depends on when data was brought into MC Next and Data 360.

title: Multi-Org Journey Scenarios — A client has multiple Marketing Cloud Engagement orgs. Org A associates a journe
text: A client has multiple Marketing Cloud Engagement orgs. Org A associates a journey with campaign A. Can org B relate the same journey to campaign B? No — the journey is not available for org B to relate to campaign B.

title: Marketing Calendar Customisation — A consultant wants to change the colour of the segment flows calendar on the Mar
text: A consultant wants to change the colour of the segment flows calendar on the Marketing Calendar. Is this possible? No — the default calendars (campaigns, campaign segment flows, segment flows) can be hidden but not deleted or customised. You can create a custom object calendar that is editable, deletable, and has personalised colours.

title: Flow as the Orchestration Engine — A consultant migrating from Marketing Cloud Engagement asks how outbound messagi
text: A consultant migrating from Marketing Cloud Engagement asks how outbound messaging is orchestrated in Marketing Cloud Next. What should they explain? In MC Next, Flow is the single orchestration engine for outbound messaging. These are called marketing flows (or high-scale flows), and they run off-core on a separate high-scale processing engine.

title: The Six Flow Types — A consultant is documenting the flow types available in Marketing Cloud Next. Wh
text: A consultant is documenting the flow types available in Marketing Cloud Next. Which types exist, and what triggers each? Audience flow (schedule or immediate) · Activation-triggered flow (a Data 360 activation publishes) · Automation event-triggered flow (a predefined event occurs) · On-demand flow (REST API call, targets an individual) · Broadcast flow (REST API call, targets all members of a dynamic segment) · Data Cloud-triggered flow (a DMO or Calculated Insight object record is created/updated).

title: Which Flows Can't Send Email — A consultant wants to send a promotional email from a Data Cloud-triggered flow.
text: A consultant wants to send a promotional email from a Data Cloud-triggered flow. Is this possible? No. Record-triggered flows and Data Cloud-triggered (Data 360-triggered) flows cannot send emails from Marketing Cloud Next.

title: Audience Flow Re-entry — A marketer configures a recurring audience flow and wants to control when an ind
text: A marketer configures a recurring audience flow and wants to control when an individual can rejoin. What options are available? Three re-entry options, mirroring Journey Builder's contact entry mode: no re-entry, re-entry at any time, and re-entry only after exiting.

title: Activation as Personalization Source — A client wants their back-in-stock email to include product details from a relat
text: A client wants their back-in-stock email to include product details from a related DMO without additional lookups at send time. How should the consultant configure this? Append the related attributes to the activation, then use the activation directly as the personalization source — email merge fields and repeaters can reference the enriched Data 360 activation attributes without additional lookups at send time.

title: On-Demand Flow API Requirements — A developer is triggering an on-demand flow via REST to send a one-time password
text: A developer is triggering an on-demand flow via REST to send a one-time password email. What values are required, and what are the rules about the individual ID? Both the email address and the individual ID are required. The individual ID does not need to correspond to an Individual record in Data 360 — it simply cannot be null. The request won't create an Individual DMO record, but the resulting engagement activity will still appear in the Email Engagement DMO.

title: Broadcast vs On-Demand Flow — A utility company needs to send an SMS alert to everyone in an affected area whe
text: A utility company needs to send an SMS alert to everyone in an affected area when an outage occurs. Which flow type applies, and what segment type is required? A broadcast flow — it targets all members of a dynamic segment. The segment must use the dynamic segment type, evaluated at execution time using variables passed into the flow.

title: The Eight Data Providers — A consultant is cataloguing the personalization data providers available in Mark
text: A consultant is cataloguing the personalization data providers available in Marketing Cloud Next. How many are there, and what are they? Eight: data graph, event, activation, Salesforce record, Apex class, personalization recommender, lookup graph, and offer.

title: Activation + Event Conflict — A marketer builds an email that needs both segment attributes from a Data 360 ac
text: A marketer builds an email that needs both segment attributes from a Data 360 activation and order details from the order-confirmation event that triggered the flow. They try to add both an activation data provider and an event data provider. What happens? The same message cannot use both an activation data provider and an event data provider. Each requires a specific flow orchestration pattern, so using both creates a conflict in how the data is bound to the message.

title: Event Data Provider Limitation — A consultant wants an order event to provide both Sales Order attributes and rel
text: A consultant wants an order event to provide both Sales Order attributes and related product details from the Sales Order Product DMO. Is this supported? No. Event data providers support direct attributes from the event DMO, but not related collections. An order event can provide attributes from the Sales Order DMO, but not related products from the Sales Order Product DMO.

title: Content Variables — A client needs an email to include an order number, delivery date, and tracking
text: A client needs an email to include an order number, delivery date, and tracking URL that are calculated during a flow and retrieved from an external order management system. Which mechanism applies? Content variables — custom placeholders defined within the email and populated at runtime from Salesforce Flow. They can be mapped to any data source available to Flow, including Salesforce data, MuleSoft integrations, and HTTP connectors.

title: Marketing Objects vs Data Extensions — A marketer wants to store a product catalogue and rewards balances for use in em
text: A marketer wants to store a product catalogue and rewards balances for use in emails, without asking an admin to create a Salesforce object or modify the Data 360 data model. What should the consultant recommend? A marketing object — a marketer-managed table of data that can be queried at runtime to personalize content. The closest MCE comparison is a data extension.

title: MCE vs MC Next Personalization — A consultant migrating from Marketing Cloud Engagement asks what changes about c
text: A consultant migrating from Marketing Cloud Engagement asks what changes about content personalization. What should they explain? MCE personalization relies primarily on data extensions (sendable or non-sendable). MC Next offers a broad range of options: data providers, content variables, and marketing objects.

title: Marketer vs Developer Personalization Methods — A client's marketing team wants point-and-click personalization, while their dev
text: A client's marketing team wants point-and-click personalization, while their developer wants scripting control. Which methods suit each? Marketer configuration: merge fields, repeaters, and dynamic content. Developer flexibility: Handlebars and AMPscript.

title: Merge Field Fallback — A marketer personalizes an email with the recipient's first name but some record
text: A marketer personalizes an email with the recipient's first name but some records have no first name. What should they configure? A fallback value on the merge field — for example, "Friend" — used when the customer's data is missing.

title: Audience Flow Sources — A marketer needs to send a promotional email to everyone who purchased in the la
text: A marketer needs to send a promotional email to everyone who purchased in the last 30 days, on a recurring schedule. Which audience flow source should they use, and how often can it run? A Segment source, running as often as every hour.

title: Audience Flow Re-entry — A marketer configures a recurring audience flow and wants to control when an ind
text: A marketer configures a recurring audience flow and wants to control when an individual can rejoin it. What must they configure, and what does it mirror? Re-entry conditions, which mirror Journey Builder's three contact entry modes: no re-entry, re-entry at any time, or re-entry only after exiting.

title: Segment Republish Before Run — A consultant configures a scheduled segment flow. Why should they republish the
text: A consultant configures a scheduled segment flow. Why should they republish the segment immediately before the flow runs? To ensure membership is as up-to-date as possible; otherwise the segment defaults to its defined publishing schedule.

title: Campaign vs Flow Cardinality — A consultant is designing a campaign with multiple email journeys. What is the c
text: A consultant is designing a campaign with multiple email journeys. What is the cardinality between campaigns and flows? One campaign can contain many flows, but each flow belongs to exactly one campaign.

title: Flow Status Reference — A marketer pauses a flow to make edits. Which status does a paused flow hold, an
text: A marketer pauses a flow to make edits. Which status does a paused flow hold, and what is the correct way to edit it? Paused flows are still considered active. To edit, deactivate (complete or cancel work), then Edit As New Version, then activate.

title: Decision Element Ordering — A consultant builds a Decision element with a broad condition first and a specif
text: A consultant builds a Decision element with a broad condition first and a specific condition second. What will happen, and how should they fix it? The broad condition will match first and the specific path may never trigger. Outcomes are evaluated in order with first-match-wins, so order most-specific to least-specific.

title: Flow Data Graph — A consultant adds a Decision element but can't see the fields they need. What is
text: A consultant adds a Decision element but can't see the fields they need. What is the most likely cause? The flow's data graph isn't connected — the flow data graph is separate from the org default data graph.

title: Path Experiment Winner Selection — A marketer runs a Path Experiment and wants the winner selected automatically. A
text: A marketer runs a Path Experiment and wants the winner selected automatically. At what confidence level does the system declare a winner? 95% confidence against all other paths, after which the delayed group is sent down the winning path automatically.

title: Distributed Marketing Template Limits — A marketer configures an approved Distributed Marketing template. What are the l
text: A marketer configures an approved Distributed Marketing template. What are the limits on approved images and phrases? Up to 30 approved images and 30 approved phrases, with only one default image. Only phrases can be marked required (locked).

title: Distributed Marketing Sender Permissions — A sales representative needs to send emails using an approved Distributed Market
text: A sales representative needs to send emails using an approved Distributed Marketing template. Which permission sets are required? Both the Send Distributed Marketing Messages permission set AND the Marketing Cloud Manager permission set.

title: Distributed Marketing Unschedule — A sales rep schedules an email from an approved template, then unschedules it. W
text: A sales rep schedules an email from an approved template, then unschedules it. What is the consequence? Unscheduling cancels the email — and any emails scheduled with it in the same campaign. To send on a new schedule, recreate it.

title: Dynamic From Address and DMARC — A client sends from an authenticated subdomain and wants a personalized From add
text: A client sends from an authenticated subdomain and wants a personalized From address. What should the consultant recommend? Use a static authenticated From address with a dynamic display name — a personal root-domain address would break DMARC alignment.

title: Dynamic Reply and RMM — A client wants auto-replies and out-of-office processing on replies. Should they
text: A client wants auto-replies and out-of-office processing on replies. Should they use direct reply or RMM routing? RMM routing — direct reply bypasses RMM, so there's no auto-reply management, out-of-office handling, or unsubscribe processing.

title: Dynamic Reply Domain Authorization — A marketer configures a dynamic reply address, but the resolved domain isn't aut
text: A marketer configures a dynamic reply address, but the resolved domain isn't authorized. What happens? The fallback address is used — reply domains must be authorized, or MC Next falls back.

title: Promotional vs Transactional Purpose — A marketer builds an email for a password reset. Which message purpose should th
text: A marketer builds an email for a password reset. Which message purpose should they select, and why does it matter? Transactional — it relates to something the customer did and does not require a promotional subscription. The choice changes compliance elements and consent rules.

title: Linking vs Cloning Personalization Points — A marketer wants the same personalization rules to apply to a heading, hero imag
text: A marketer wants the same personalization rules to apply to a heading, hero image, and CTA button. Should they link or clone the personalization point? Link — linking shares one point so all components update together; cloning creates a separate copy with its own rules.

title: Engagement Signal Identifiers — A consultant configures an engagement signal for a custom recommender objective.
text: A consultant configures an engagement signal for a custom recommender objective. Which identifier is required, and what are the four identifier types? The item identifier is required for custom objective-based recommenders. The four types are User, Timestamp, Item, and Event identifiers.

title: Engagement Signal DMO Category — A consultant tries to configure an engagement signal but can't select their pref
text: A consultant tries to configure an engagement signal but can't select their preferred DMO. What is the most likely cause? The DMO isn't categorized as Engagement — engagement signals can only use Engagement-category DMOs that are mapped.

title: Flow Sharing on Campaign Delete — A consultant deletes a campaign that had several related flows. What happens to
text: A consultant deletes a campaign that had several related flows. What happens to the flows' sharing settings? Sharing reverts to each flow's own defined rules; if none are defined, the flow becomes private.

title: Standalone Flow Sharing — A consultant creates a standalone flow and expects the marketing team to see it,
text: A consultant creates a standalone flow and expects the marketing team to see it, but they can't. Why? Standalone flows are private by default — they must be shared explicitly, either dynamically (categories + sharing rules) or manually (per user/group).

title: Repeater Layout Change — A designer changes the layout of a repeater that already has content and styling
text: A designer changes the layout of a repeater that already has content and styling. What happens? The content, data, and style settings within the repeater are removed.

title: Recommender Data Placement — A marketer wants to show personalized product recommendations in an email. Where
text: A marketer wants to show personalized product recommendations in an email. Where must recommender data be placed? Inside a repeater component — recommender data only works in a repeater and its merge fields.

title: Recommender Training Requirement — A marketer adds a new recommender but it isn't selectable in the email. What is
text: A marketer adds a new recommender but it isn't selectable in the email. What is the most likely cause? The recommender hasn't completed its training period with at least one successful refresh.

title: Campaign Stage Derivation — A campaign has five flows; four completed successfully and one errored. What doe
text: A campaign has five flows; four completed successfully and one errored. What does the Campaign Stage field show? Error — the Campaign Stage is derived from all flows, and one Error flow makes the whole campaign Error.

title: Marketing Calendar Permissions — A sales user needs to view the Marketing Calendar but isn't a marketer. Which pe
text: A sales user needs to view the Marketing Calendar but isn't a marketer. Which permission grants access? The Access Marketing Calendar user permission — in addition to Marketing Cloud Admin or Marketing Cloud Manager.

title: NotSentReason Mapping — A consultant wants to understand why emails weren't sent. Which field should the
text: A consultant wants to understand why emails weren't sent. Which field should they inspect, and what does it map to? The NotSentReason field, which maps to the Engagement Action Reason field of the Email Engagement DMO.

title: Campaign Flow Cardinality — A consultant needs to relate a flow to a campaign for reporting. What is the cor
text: A consultant needs to relate a flow to a campaign for reporting. What is the correct relationship? Each flow relates to exactly one campaign, while a campaign can relate to many flows.

title: Saved Expressions — A marketer wants to show a customer's most recent purchase across multiple email
text: A marketer wants to show a customer's most recent purchase across multiple emails. What should they create? A saved expression — it defines which single value to return when multiple are possible, using filters and sorting, and is reusable across emails and channels.

title: Engagement Signal Counting — A consultant wants to count unique email clicks rather than total clicks. How sh
text: A consultant wants to count unique email clicks rather than total clicks. How should they configure the engagement signal? Group repeat events using added fields (e.g., individual ID + bulk message ID + click event) and count them as one signal.

title: Flow Sharing Categories — A consultant configures dynamic sharing for a standalone flow using the Equals o
text: A consultant configures dynamic sharing for a standalone flow using the Equals operator. What must be true for the sharing rule to apply? The category/subcategory entered on the flow must match the sharing rule's value exactly.

title: Marketing Agents — A marketer wants to turn a written campaign brief into a campaign with a flow an
text: A marketer wants to turn a written campaign brief into a campaign with a flow and multichannel content. Which agent should the consultant recommend? The Campaign Creation agent — it drafts a brief, creates a campaign from a brief, summarizes, and generates insights.

title: Einstein Segments — A client wants to create segments using natural language. What prerequisite must
text: A client wants to create segments using natural language. What prerequisite must be met? A Unified Individual DMO with at least 10 records.

title: Einstein Data Prism — A consultant is configuring Einstein Segments and needs to validate which metada
text: A consultant is configuring Einstein Segments and needs to validate which metadata the model can use. Which tool should they use? Metadata Studio — it validates and excludes metadata. Einstein Data Prism is the grounding layer that scans metadata, auto-generates descriptions, and uses a vector database.

title: Einstein Segment Filtering — A client notices that Einstein Segments excluded several attributes they expecte
