text: A client notices that Einstein Segments excluded several attributes they expected to use. Why? Einstein Segments strips demographic attributes and attributes that would return fewer than 10 results.

title: Channel vs Agent — A consultant is explaining conversational messaging architecture. What is the di
text: A consultant is explaining conversational messaging architecture. What is the difference between a channel and an agent? Channel = pipe (delivery); Agent = brain (LLM + Data 360).

title: Conversational Ecosystem — What four components make up the conversational messaging ecosystem?
text: What four components make up the conversational messaging ecosystem? Channel + Flow + Agent + Data 360.

title: Subagents vs Actions — A consultant needs to define what a conversational agent is allowed to do versus
text: A consultant needs to define what a conversational agent is allowed to do versus what tools it can use. How should they model this? Subagents = job description (boundaries); Actions = tools (get info / update records).

title: Conversational Lifecycle — What are the four stages of the conversational lifecycle?
text: What are the four stages of the conversational lifecycle? Trigger → Routing/intent → Execution → Handoff/resolution.

title: Conversational KPIs — A client wants to measure the success of their conversational agent. Which KPIs
text: A client wants to measure the success of their conversational agent. Which KPIs should the consultant recommend? Deflection, engagement, and conversion.

title: Predictive AI Edition Gates — A client on the Growth tier wants to use Engagement Scoring. Is this possible?
text: A client on the Growth tier wants to use Engagement Scoring. Is this possible? No — Engagement Scoring is Advanced only. STO is Growth (global model) / Advanced; Metrics Guard is Growth + Advanced; Engagement Frequency is Advanced only.

title: Metrics Guard Score — A client sees a Metrics Guard score of 0.2 on a send and assumes it performed po
text: A client sees a Metrics Guard score of 0.2 on a send and assumes it performed poorly. What should the consultant explain? The Metrics Guard score is counterintuitive — lower means more likely real (less likely to be a bot).

title: Predictive AI Prerequisite — A consultant is enabling Send Time Optimization, Engagement Scoring, and Engagem
text: A consultant is enabling Send Time Optimization, Engagement Scoring, and Engagement Frequency. What shared prerequisite must be in place? An identity resolution ruleset with Individual as the primary object.

title: Scoring Models — A client wants to score both individuals and accounts. What should the consultan
text: A client wants to score both individuals and accounts. What should the consultant explain about scoring models and editions? The three scoring models are Engagement, Fit, and Overall, scored 0–100. Account scoring is Advanced only.

title: Scoring Frequency Cost — A client wants to increase scoring frequency to daily. What is the cost implicat
text: A client wants to increase scoring frequency to daily. What is the cost implication? More frequent scoring consumes more credits.

title: Einstein Trust Layer — A client's legal team asks how Salesforce prevents AI hallucination and protects
text: A client's legal team asks how Salesforce prevents AI hallucination and protects sensitive data. Which framework should the consultant describe? The Einstein Trust Layer — toxicity detection, dynamic grounding (anti-hallucination), PII masking, zero data retention, encryption, audit trail, and human escalation.

title: Dynamic Grounding — What does dynamic grounding do in the Einstein Trust Layer?
text: What does dynamic grounding do in the Einstein Trust Layer? It grounds AI responses in real data to prevent hallucination.

title: Zero Data Retention — A client asks whether their prompts are stored by the LLM provider. What should
text: A client asks whether their prompts are stored by the LLM provider. What should the consultant explain? Zero data retention means prompts and responses are not retained by the LLM provider.

title: Agentic Marketing Waves — A consultant is explaining the evolution of marketing automation. What are the t
text: A consultant is explaining the evolution of marketing automation. What are the three waves? Automation → Real-Time → Agentic.

title: Agentic Marketing Definition — What is the defining characteristic of agentic marketing?
text: What is the defining characteristic of agentic marketing? The marketer states the strategy and AI agents execute it.

title: AI Campaign Insights Scope — A client runs Generate Campaign Insights on a campaign with three flows. Which f
text: A client runs Generate Campaign Insights on a campaign with three flows. Which flow is analysed? The first flow.

title: The Five Out-of-the-Box Agents — A consultant is mapping Marketing Cloud Next's AI agents to a client's workflow
text: A consultant is mapping Marketing Cloud Next's AI agents to a client's workflow stages. Which agents are available, and what does each do? Segment Creation (natural language → editable segment criteria) · Campaign Creation (campaign briefs, flows, and multi-channel content) · Content Creation (drafts and refines email, landing page, and SMS content) · Journey Decisioning (selects the most appropriate journey or flow and creates personalized content) · Account Discovery (account insights and potential buying group members).

title: Account Discovery Agent — A B2B client wants to identify potential buying group members at target accounts
text: A B2B client wants to identify potential buying group members at target accounts and guide follow-up activities. Which agent applies? The Account Discovery agent — it provides account insights and identifies potential buying group members.

title: Draft with Agentforce — A marketer wants to turn a campaign objective into a complete brief and campaign
text: A marketer wants to turn a campaign objective into a complete brief and campaign. What is the workflow? Marketing Home → New Campaign → Draft with Agentforce → describe the campaign objective → choose to draft a brief → ask Agentforce to generate a campaign → review the campaign preview (flow and content) → save as a new campaign.

title: Engagement Frequency Classifications — A client wants to reduce email fatigue. Which predictive AI feature applies, and
text: A client wants to reduce email fatigue. Which predictive AI feature applies, and what classifications does it produce? Engagement Frequency — it determines how often each contact should receive an email. The Email Engagement Classification field in the Email Engagement Frequency DMO assigns each individual to one of four categories: Saturated, Almost Saturated, On Target, or Under Saturated.

title: Engagement Scoring Personas — A client wants to tailor campaign strategy by recipient behaviour. Which predict
text: A client wants to tailor campaign strategy by recipient behaviour. Which predictive AI feature provides personas, and what are they? Engagement Scoring — it assigns individuals to four personas based on predicted likelihood to open and click: Loyalists (high open, high click), Selective Subscribers (low open, high click), Window Shoppers (high open, low click), and Win Back/Dormant (low open, low click).

title: Using Engagement Scoring Personas — A client has a large group of "Selective Subscribers" (low open, high click) and
text: A client has a large group of "Selective Subscribers" (low open, high click) and "Window Shoppers" (high open, low click). How should the consultant advise them to act? Send surveys to better understand Selective Subscribers, and engage Window Shoppers through alternative channels. Place dormant subscribers into a dedicated win-back campaign.

title: Send Time Optimization Setup — A consultant enables Send Time Optimization. What configuration is required for
text: A consultant enables Send Time Optimization. What configuration is required for it to work in a Send Email Message element? Add the Send Time Optimization DMO to the data graph using the required structure, then select the Hourly Scores by Week field. The Send Email Message element uses this field to determine each recipient's optimal send time.

title: STO Optimization Window — A marketer enables Send Time Optimization on a Send Email Message element. What
text: A marketer enables Send Time Optimization on a Send Email Message element. What window can they define, and what happens within it? An optimization window ranging from 2 hours up to 1 week. MC Next sends the message to each recipient at their predicted optimal time within that window.

title: Predictive AI Edition Gates — A client on the Growth edition wants to use Engagement Frequency and Engagement
text: A client on the Growth edition wants to use Engagement Frequency and Engagement Scoring. What should the consultant advise? Both are Advanced-only. Only Send Time Optimization is available in Growth (and Advanced).

title: Using Predictive AI Insights — A consultant wants to branch a flow based on a contact's engagement score. What
text: A consultant wants to branch a flow based on a contact's engagement score. What configuration is required? Configure the required data graph first, then use fields such as Email Engagement Frequency or Engagement Score to create branches with a Decision element. Alternatively, use those DMO fields as segment criteria.

title: Dashboard Selection — A client reports that a large number of emails are failing to reach inboxes and
text: A client reports that a large number of emails are failing to reach inboxes and wants to understand why. Which pre-built dashboard should the consultant recommend? The Deliverability dashboard — it shows email delivery and failure reasons.

title: Campaign Performance Dashboard — A client wants to compare performance across individual campaigns. Which dashboa
text: A client wants to compare performance across individual campaigns. Which dashboard applies? The Campaign Performance dashboard — aggregated and individual campaign KPIs.

title: Content Performance Dashboard — A client wants to compare how different content variations performed across chan
text: A client wants to compare how different content variations performed across channels. Which dashboard applies? The Content Performance dashboard — cross-channel and variation data.

title: Channel-Specific Dashboards — A client wants to analyse landing page engagement specifically. Which dashboard
text: A client wants to analyse landing page engagement specifically. Which dashboard applies? The SMS / Forms / Landing Page Engagement dashboards (channel-specific).

title: B2B Analytics — A client wants to understand how marketing influenced closed revenue. Which dash
text: A client wants to understand how marketing influenced closed revenue. Which dashboards apply? B2B Analytics — Account-Based Marketing, Pipeline, Marketing Manager, and B2B Attribution — focused on revenue attribution.

title: Open Rate Formula — A campaign sent 10,000 emails, had 200 bounces, and 3,000 unique opens. What is
text: A campaign sent 10,000 emails, had 200 bounces, and 3,000 unique opens. What is the Open Rate? 3,000 ÷ (10,000 − 200) = 30.6%.

title: Click Rate vs CTR — A client is confused about the difference between Click Rate and CTR. How should
text: A client is confused about the difference between Click Rate and CTR. How should the consultant explain it? Click Rate = unique clicks ÷ (sends − bounces). CTR = unique clicks ÷ unique opens.

title: Bounce and Delivery Rate — A campaign sent 10,000 emails with 200 bounces. What are the Bounce Rate and Del
text: A campaign sent 10,000 emails with 200 bounces. What are the Bounce Rate and Delivery Rate? Bounce Rate = 200 ÷ 10,000 = 2%. Delivery Rate = (10,000 − 200) ÷ 10,000 = 98%.

title: Opt-Out Rate — A campaign sent 10,000 emails, had 200 bounces, and 50 unsubscribes. What is the
text: A campaign sent 10,000 emails, had 200 bounces, and 50 unsubscribes. What is the Opt-Out Rate? 50 ÷ (10,000 − 200) = 0.51%.

title: Marketing Performance — A consultant is installing Marketing Performance. Which permission sets are requ
text: A consultant is installing Marketing Performance. Which permission sets are required, and what is needed to view it? Installation needs both the Data Cloud admin and Marketing Cloud Admin permission sets. Viewing needs Tableau Next Included App Business User.

title: Opportunity Influence — A client wants to attribute closed revenue to email and SMS clicks. What is the
text: A client wants to attribute closed revenue to email and SMS clicks. What is the attribution window? A 30-day-before window to Closed/Won.

title: Attribution Models — A client wants to credit the campaign that first introduced a customer. Which at
text: A client wants to credit the campaign that first introduced a customer. Which attribution model applies? First-touch (as opposed to last-touch).

title: Sharing Dashboards — A consultant shares a dashboard folder with the marketing team, but the team rep
text: A consultant shares a dashboard folder with the marketing team, but the team reports they cannot see it. Why? Sharing folders or dashboards alone does not make them appear to users — sharing does not grant visibility.

title: On-Canvas Analytics Cost — A consultant opens element details in on-canvas analytics to investigate a flow
text: A consultant opens element details in on-canvas analytics to investigate a flow run. What is the cost implication? Opening element details consumes Data Cloud credits.

title: NotSentReason — A client wants to report on why emails were not sent. Which field and DMO should
text: A client wants to report on why emails were not sent. Which field and DMO should the consultant use? The NotSentReason field, which maps to Engagement Action Reason on the Email Engagement DMO.

title: Campaign Stage — A campaign has four completed flows and one errored flow. What does the Campaign
text: A campaign has four completed flows and one errored flow. What does the Campaign Stage show? Error — one Error flow makes the whole campaign Error.

title: Marketing Calendar — A client wants to see all their scheduled marketing activity in one view. Which
text: A client wants to see all their scheduled marketing activity in one view. Which flows will appear? Campaigns + Campaign Segment Flows + Segment Flows appear by default. Event-triggered and form-triggered flows do not appear.

title: Dashboard Selection Drill — A client asks which dashboard to use for each of these: (a) comparing content va
text: A client asks which dashboard to use for each of these: (a) comparing content variations, (b) diagnosing delivery failures, (c) attributing closed revenue. What should the consultant recommend? (a) Content Performance · (b) Deliverability · (c) B2B Analytics (B2B Attribution).

title: Metric Formula Drill — A campaign sent 50,000 emails, had 1,000 bounces, 10,000 unique opens, 2,000 uni
text: A campaign sent 50,000 emails, had 1,000 bounces, 10,000 unique opens, 2,000 unique clicks, and 100 unsubscribes. Calculate Open Rate, Click Rate, CTR, Bounce Rate, Delivery Rate, and Opt-Out Rate. - Open Rate = 10,000 ÷ 49,000 = 20.4% - Click Rate = 2,000 ÷ 49,000 = 4.1% - CTR = 2,000 ÷ 10,000 = 20.0% - Bounce Rate = 1,000 ÷ 50,000 = 2.0% - Delivery Rate = 49,000 ÷ 50,000 = 98.0% - Opt-Out Rate = 100 ÷ 49,000 = 0.2%

title: The Three Reporting Capabilities — A consultant is documenting the reporting capabilities included with Marketing C
text: A consultant is documenting the reporting capabilities included with Marketing Cloud Next. How many are there out of the box, and what does each provide? Three, all included with no additional license or SKU: the Campaign Performance Dashboard (end-to-end view of an individual campaign — sends, opens, clicks, bounces, contact progression), the Marketing Performance Dashboard (broader cross-channel view over time — audience growth and program-level engagement trends), and the Semantic Data Model (a consistent business layer for custom reports, stakeholder sharing, and external tool connections)

title: Marketing Performance Dashboard Location — A marketer wants a consolidated view of performance across campaigns, channels,
text: A marketer wants a consolidated view of performance across campaigns, channels, content, and audience segments. Where do they find it, and what does it cover? The Marketing Performance dashboards, available from the Marketing Analytics tab. They bring together activity across web, email, SMS, WhatsApp, and mobile — and the same dashboards are embedded directly in each campaign record.

title: Content Performance Dashboard Access — A marketer wants to see how a specific email element is performing within an act
text: A marketer wants to see how a specific email element is performing within an active flow. How do they access content performance insights? Select the corresponding element in the active flow (such as a Send Email Message element), then from the Analytics tab click the Details button to review pulse card metrics for the content type plus row-level data.

title: Deliverability Dashboards — A client reports that some SMS and WhatsApp messages aren't reaching recipients.
text: A client reports that some SMS and WhatsApp messages aren't reaching recipients. Which dashboard helps, and what does it show? The deliverability dashboards for SMS, WhatsApp, and mobile app messaging. They provide visibility into message delivery health and campaign performance, and help you understand why a particular message failed to reach specific recipients.

title: Semantic Data Model — A client wants to build custom reports, share marketing data with stakeholders o
text: A client wants to build custom reports, share marketing data with stakeholders outside Salesforce CRM, and connect an external BI tool. What should the consultant recommend? The semantic data model — powered by Tableau Next, it provides the foundation for reports and dashboards in Marketing Cloud Next and is available from the Analytics tab.

title: Customising Standard Dashboards — A client wants to adjust the standard dashboards to show different metrics and l
text: A client wants to adjust the standard dashboards to show different metrics and layouts. What can they change? Standard dashboards can be used as provided or customised by changing their widgets, labels, layouts, and filters.

title: Unified Engagement History — A sales team wants visibility into which contacts at an account are most engaged
text: A sales team wants visibility into which contacts at an account are most engaged with marketing. What should the consultant recommend, and how is it deployed? The Unified Engagement History dashboard — a pre-built dashboard giving sales and marketing a shared view of activities performed by the leads and contacts associated with an account. Embed it by adding the Unified Engagement History dashboard component to the account, lead, and contact page layouts.

title: What is the defining difference between traditional automation and agentic marketing?
text: What is the defining difference between traditional automation and agentic marketing? Automation follows a fixed, human-configured path; agentic marketing lets the marketer state a strategy while AI agents create content, build audiences, personalize, optimize, and orchestrate handoffs autonomously.

title: What three pillars set Marketing Cloud Next apart from retrofitted-AI platforms?
text: What three pillars set Marketing Cloud Next apart from retrofitted-AI platforms? (1) Actionable data (one unified dataset), (2) cross-departmental workflows (Sales/Service/Commerce), (3) autonomous Agentforce-native AI agents.

title: Name the three waves of Marketing Cloud evolution.
text: Name the three waves of Marketing Cloud evolution. Wave 1 Automation → Wave 2 Real-Time → Wave 3 Agentic.

title: What does "zero copy data access" mean?
text: What does "zero copy data access" mean? Connecting directly to an external data platform (Snowflake, BigQuery) and reading data in place without physically moving/copying it.

title: What is the "pipe vs. brain" distinction in conversational marketing?
text: What is the "pipe vs. brain" distinction in conversational marketing? The channel (SMS/WhatsApp/email) is the pipe that delivers messages and receives replies; the agent (Agentforce) is the brain that analyzes text with LLMs + Data 360.

title: What are the four components of the conversational ecosystem?
text: What are the four components of the conversational ecosystem? Channel (interface), Flow (traffic controller), Agent (intelligence), Data 360 (memory).

title: What's the difference between a subagent and an action?
text: What's the difference between a subagent and an action? A subagent defines the boundaries of what the agent may discuss (the "job description"); an action is a tool to actually do things (Get Information or Update Records).

title: What are the four stages of a conversation's lifecycle?
text: What are the four stages of a conversation's lifecycle? (1) Trigger, (2) Routing & engagement (intent recognition), (3) Execution (retrieve/update via actions), (4) Handoff or resolution.

title: Name the three core KPIs for conversational marketing.
text: Name the three core KPIs for conversational marketing. Deflection rate (no human intervention), engagement rate (replies vs. clicks), conversion rate (sale/booking).

title: Name four mechanisms of the Einstein Trust Layer.
text: Name four mechanisms of the Einstein Trust Layer. Toxicity detection, dynamic grounding (anti-hallucination), PII data masking, zero data retention, encryption, audit trail, human escalation (any four).

title: How does the Trust Layer protect PII sent to an LLM?
text: How does the Trust Layer protect PII sent to an LLM? It detects PII (credit cards, phones, addresses), replaces it with anonymized placeholders before the prompt reaches the LLM, then unmasks the response.

title: What are DLO, DMO, and Unified Individual, in order?
text: What are DLO, DMO, and Unified Individual, in order? DLO (raw data lake object, "intake"), DMO (standardized data model object), Unified Individual (identity-resolved single profile).

title: What primary object does Marketing Cloud Next require for a data graph?
text: What primary object does Marketing Cloud Next require for a data graph? Unified Individual (the segment driving the flow must also be built on Unified Individual).

title: Why doesn't data automatically become available just because it's in Data 360?
text: Why doesn't data automatically become available just because it's in Data 360? A field must be explicitly included in the data graph before Marketing Cloud Next can access it for personalization/decisioning.

title: What three decisions must an admin make before building a data graph?
text: What three decisions must an admin make before building a data graph? Which objects to include, which fields are needed (can't be removed after save), and refresh frequency.

title: Which flow element draws data from Salesforce Core directly (bypassing Data 360)?
text: Which flow element draws data from Salesforce Core directly (bypassing Data 360)? The Get Records element (e.g., Contacts, Leads, Accounts).

title: Name the five stages of the data ingestion workflow.
text: Name the five stages of the data ingestion workflow. (1) Data stream → DLO, (2) DMO mapping, (3) identity resolution → Unified Individual, (4) segment refresh, (5) data graph refresh.

title: How often does identity resolution run by default, and why is it the least predictable sta
text: How often does identity resolution run by default, and why is it the least predictable stage? Once per day (more often for smaller change sets); depends on schedule and change volume, so a few hours up to 24 hours.

title: How do the CRM connector's streaming vs. batch ingestion differ in latency?
text: How do the CRM connector's streaming vs. batch ingestion differ in latency? CDC streaming lands in the DLO in 3 minutes; batch fallback (unsupported CDC or formula fields) checks every 10 minutes.

title: How does a Decision element evaluate outcomes?
text: How does a Decision element evaluate outcomes? Outcomes are evaluated in order and the first match wins; unmatched contacts follow the default (catch-all) outcome.

title: What are the three parts of a decision condition?
text: What are the three parts of a decision condition? Resource (data-graph attribute), Operator (Equals/Greater Than/etc.), Value (typed entry or field reference).

title: How does the flow data graph differ from the org default data graph?
text: How does the flow data graph differ from the org default data graph? The org default populates message personalization; the flow data graph determines what the flow can evaluate for decisioning.

title: What two capabilities does a Path Experiment combine?
text: What two capabilities does a Path Experiment combine? Random Split (distribute contacts across paths) and Path Optimizer (evaluate which path performs best).

title: At what confidence level does automatic Path Experiment selection declare a winner?
text: At what confidence level does automatic Path Experiment selection declare a winner? 95% confidence against all other paths; the delayed group then follows the winning path.

title: Which edition includes Path Experiments, and what permission is required?
text: Which edition includes Path Experiments, and what permission is required? Advanced Edition only; requires Marketing Cloud Manager or Admin permission set + personalization features.

title: What is a formula resource used for in a flow?
text: What is a formula resource used for in a flow? A computed value (e.g., Today()-30 ) that a Decision element can reference, such as testing recency.

title: What's the difference between promotional and transactional message purpose?
text: What's the difference between promotional and transactional message purpose? Promotional = marketing content, requires opt-in consent; transactional = related to a customer action (receipt, reset), no subscription needed.

title: What are the three core parts of the email editor?
text: What are the three core parts of the email editor? Canvas (structure), components panel (elements), properties sidebar (per-component settings).

title: How often is personalization tracking setup performed?
text: How often is personalization tracking setup performed? Once per org (Customer Engagement → Personalization Setup).

title: What's the difference between linking and cloning a personalization point?
text: What's the difference between linking and cloning a personalization point? Linking shares one personalization point across components (updates apply everywhere); cloning creates a separate copy with its own rules.

title: What does a saved expression do?
text: What does a saved expression do? Defines which single value to return from data when multiple are possible, using filters/sorting (e.g., most recent purchase); reusable across emails/channels.

title: What three parts make up the consent composite key?
text: What three parts make up the consent composite key? Communication Subscription (topic) + Contact Point (email/phone) + Engagement Channel Type (Email/SMS/WhatsApp).

title: What does Marketing Cloud Next's strict opt-in rule mean?
text: What does Marketing Cloud Next's strict opt-in rule mean? If no consent record exists for a recipient on a subscription, the system treats them as opted out and blocks the send (absence of "Yes" = "No").

title: Does "Unsubscribe from all" persist as a permanent block?
text: Does "Unsubscribe from all" persist as a permanent block? No — it removes the contact from all existing subscriptions but doesn't prevent a future opt-in on a newly created subscription.

title: What is SMS opt-out scope?
text: What is SMS opt-out scope? Per sender code — opting out of one code doesn't affect other codes from the same brand (not global per phone number).

title: Why must you never delete a Communication Subscription?
text: Why must you never delete a Communication Subscription? Deleting it cascades and permanently destroys all related historical consent data (the audit trail). Instead, remove it from Preference Pages.

title: What flow actions write consent, and which must be avoided?
text: What flow actions write consent, and which must be avoided? Use Create Consent (Data Cloud Record-Triggered) or Consent Request (Automation Event/On-Demand); avoid MessagingConsent / MessagingConsentV2 .

title: What are the five steps of a double opt-in flow?
text: What are the five steps of a double opt-in flow? (1) Data capture, (2) transactional confirmation email, (3) click verification link, (4) Consent Request action writes OPT IN, (5) verified subscriber.

title: What four pieces establish a trusted sending identity?
text: What four pieces establish a trusted sending identity? Physical address, authenticated sending domain (DKIM/SPF/DMARC), authenticated from addresses, branded tracking domain.

title: What three functions does Reply Mail Management perform?
text: What three functions does Reply Mail Management perform? Delete auto-responses, optional auto-response acknowledgment, routing to a monitored inbox (plus opt-out keyword processing).

title: What does Einstein Metrics Guard do?
text: What does Einstein Metrics Guard do? Uses AI to filter non-human activity (bot scans, security checks) so open/click rates reflect real engagement.

title: What happens when you copy an email that includes personalization?
text: What happens when you copy an email that includes personalization? Only the default variations of dynamic content components are copied — other variations and personalization rules aren't. A Personalization recommender isn't copied either (but its merge fields and repeaters are).

title: What does converting an email to code remove, and can you undo it?
text: What does converting an email to code remove, and can you undo it? It removes dynamic content — repeaters, conditional logic, and content variants — and you lose drag-and-drop components and Style tab styling. You can't undo the conversion.

title: How long does a View as Web Page link work, and what does it re-render?
text: How long does a View as Web Page link work, and what does it re-render? It becomes active when sent and works for 90 days. It reflects the published version at send time, but personalized values re-render against the recipient's current profile each time the link is opened.

title: What happens when you manually edit an email's plain text version?
text: What happens when you manually edit an email's plain text version? It's no longer in sync with the original — future changes to the original aren't included. Restore discards plain-text edits.

title: How many test recipients can you send to, and what do test sends count toward?
text: How many test recipients can you send to, and what do test sends count toward? Up to five comma-separated addresses; test sends count toward message credits. The From name must be from an authenticated domain.

title: What file type and size limit apply to email attachments?
text: What file type and size limit apply to email attachments? PDF files from Salesforce CMS, up to 5 MB.

title: What are the three opt-out link options for promotional emails?
text: What are the three opt-out link options for promotional emails? Unsubscribe (immediate unsubscribe from the email's subscription + confirmation page), Preference Manager (manage individual email preferences), or a custom preference page URL.

title: How does locking work for email template content?
text: How does locking work for email template content? Template-wide settings and components are locked by default; nested components mirror the parent (locking/unlocking cascades). Unlock via Settings (template-wide), lock icons (subject/preheader), Data Sources tab, or per-component "Allow users to modify this component".

title: When should you use a static vs. dynamic From address?
text: When should you use a static vs. dynamic From address? Static From + dynamic display name when sending from an authenticated subdomain (avoids DMARC alignment failures); dynamic From when you authenticate the root domain (personal addresses align with the sending domain).

title: What does a dynamic reply address require, and what happens if the domain isn't authorized
text: What does a dynamic reply address require, and what happens if the domain isn't authorized? It requires an authorized email domain. MC Next validates each resolved reply address's domain; if not authorized, it uses the fallback address.

title: How does a dynamic reply address interact with Reply Mail Management?
text: How does a dynamic reply address interact with Reply Mail Management? Direct reply bypasses RMM (no auto-reply/out-of-office/unsubscribe processing); RMM routing forwards replies to conversational agents, shared inboxes, or Sales/Service Cloud routing rules.

title: What happens when a dynamic From/reply value is missing at send time?
text: What happens when a dynamic From/reply value is missing at send time? MC Next uses the configured fallback — always configure a verified, authenticated address as the fallback to maintain deliverability.

title: What are the two ways to source a dynamic email address?
text: What are the two ways to source a dynamic email address? From an associated user (contact owner, account manager, customer success manager) or from a custom field (brand, publication, or region address).

title: What enforces data isolation between business units?
text: What enforces data isolation between business units? A one-to-one mapping between a business unit and a data space (each business unit → exactly one data space, not shared).

title: What are the two business unit member roles and their key difference?
text: What are the two business unit member roles and their key difference? Marketer-Standard (can activate flows) vs. Marketer-ReadOnly (can't activate; can send messages + view dashboards).

title: How many business units can you create, and can you deactivate the last one?
text: How many business units can you create, and can you deactivate the last one? Up to 150; you can't deactivate the last remaining business unit (and deactivation is permanent).

title: Which Einstein feature is NOT supported with business units?
text: Which Einstein feature is NOT supported with business units? Einstein Metrics Guard.

title: What's the cardinality between campaigns and flows?
text: What's the cardinality between campaigns and flows? One campaign can contain multiple flows; each flow relates to only one campaign.

title: Name three marketing-oriented flow types and their triggers.
text: Name three marketing-oriented flow types and their triggers. Audience Flow (schedule/segment), Automation Event-Triggered Flow (event), Activation-Triggered Flow (activation publish), Broadcast/On-Demand (API call).

title: How does a Decision element evaluate outcomes?
text: How does a Decision element evaluate outcomes? Like IF/ELSE — outcomes evaluated in order, first match wins, unmatched records follow the default path.

title: What happens to a Wait element when you pause a flow?
text: What happens to a Wait element when you pause a flow? Pause duration counts toward total wait time; past-due tasks complete immediately on resume.

title: How many exit rules can a flow have, and when are they evaluated?
text: How many exit rules can a flow have, and when are they evaluated? Up to 10; evaluated each time a user starts or resumes a flow.

title: What three Salesforce Personalization concepts power dynamic content?
text: What three Salesforce Personalization concepts power dynamic content? Personalization point, decision, and targeting rule.

title: Max personalization points per content item and variations per component?
text: Max personalization points per content item and variations per component? 25 personalization points per item; 15 variations per component.

title: What are the GSM-7 vs UCS-2 SMS character limits?
text: What are the GSM-7 vs UCS-2 SMS character limits? GSM-7 = 160 chars; UCS-2 (Unicode/emoji) = 70 chars; segmented messages add a header (153/67).

title: Which five SMS opt-out keywords are always reserved?
text: Which five SMS opt-out keywords are always reserved? STOP, QUIT, CANCEL, END, UNSUBSCRIBE.

title: What does "published" mean for an email (vs. sent)?
text: What does "published" mean for an email (vs. sent)? Published = ready to send in a flow; customers see it only when the campaign/flow is activated.

title: Key difference between a prospect and a lead?
text: Key difference between a prospect and a lead? Prospect is unqualified (marketing-owned, top of funnel); lead is qualified (sales-owned, middle of funnel).

title: Can you create a Unified Individual record manually?
text: Can you create a Unified Individual record manually? No — created only by syncing + identity resolution harmonization.

title: What happens when converting a prospect to an existing lead with empty fields?
text: What happens when converting a prospect to an existing lead with empty fields? Only empty fields in the existing lead are overwritten by prospect values.

title: Name three product-related marketing triggers.
text: Name three product-related marketing triggers. Product Back In Stock, Product Low Inventory, Product Price Drop (also Abandoned Cart/Page/Browse).

title: Difference between Inactivity Period and Job Frequency in a trigger?
text: Difference between Inactivity Period and Job Frequency in a trigger? Inactivity = wait after last interaction; Job Frequency = how often the trigger job evaluates customers.

title: What permission set configures marketing triggers?
text: What permission set configures marketing triggers? Marketing Triggers Admin.

title: What engagement types does Opportunity Influence use for attribution?
text: What engagement types does Opportunity Influence use for attribution? Email and SMS click activities (not opens, not external sites).

title: What's the attribution window for Opportunity Influence?
text: What's the attribution window for Opportunity Influence? 30 days before opportunity creation to the date it's Closed/Won.

title: Difference between first-touch and last-touch attribution?
text: Difference between first-touch and last-touch attribution? First-touch credits the first campaign engaged; last-touch credits the last campaign before close.

title: Name the four B2B Analytics dashboards.
text: Name the four B2B Analytics dashboards. Account-Based Marketing, Pipeline, Marketing Manager, B2B Attribution.

title: What's the Campaign ROI% formula?
text: What's the Campaign ROI% formula? (Revenue − Cost) / Cost.

title: Max approved images/phrases, and which can be "required"?
text: Max approved images/phrases, and which can be "required"? 30 images + 30 phrases; only phrases can be required (locked), one default image.

title: What two permission sets does a non-marketing sender need?
text: What two permission sets does a non-marketing sender need? Send Distributed Marketing Messages + Marketing Cloud Manager.

title: Difference between Click Rate and Click-Through Rate (CTR)?
text: Difference between Click Rate and Click-Through Rate (CTR)? Click Rate = clicks/sends; CTR = clicks/opens (different denominators).

title: What's the email delivery rate formula?
text: What's the email delivery rate formula? (sends − bounces) / sends.

title: What's the push open rate denominator?
text: What's the push open rate denominator? Opened / Delivered (not sent).

title: What are the three marketing object data types and their limits?
text: What are the three marketing object data types and their limits? Text (up to 255 chars), Number (integer up to 18 digits), Decimal (decimal up to 18 digits). Max length can't be changed after creation.

title: What are the Growth vs. Advanced allocations for marketing object storage and count?
text: What are the Growth vs. Advanced allocations for marketing object storage and count? Growth = 10 GB / 25 objects; Advanced = 40 GB / 100 objects; 100 columns per object (both).

title: What identifier suffix marks a marketing object vs. a field vs. a data graph field?
text: What identifier suffix marks a marketing object vs. a field vs. a data graph field? Object = API name + mo ; field = API name + c ; data graph field = $dataGraph.<Field .

title: What function/helper reads marketing object data in AMPscript vs. Handlebars?
text: What function/helper reads marketing object data in AMPscript vs. Handlebars? AMPscript uses Lookup() (e.g., %=v(@points)=% ); Handlebars uses queryFirst type="MO" .

title: How does an actionable list differ from a segment?
text: How does an actionable list differ from a segment? Actionable list = fixed/static collection (leads OR contacts, not both); segment = dynamic, rule-based.

title: Who can manually remove members from an actionable list record page?
text: Who can manually remove members from an actionable list record page? Only the list's creator (flow automation can also remove members).

title: How do you create a marketing object, and what happens to the data types?
text: How do you create a marketing object, and what happens to the data types? Import a CSV file (Data Management → Marketing Objects → New → From File). The object contains only the CSV's columns; MC Next infers each column's data type from the file.

title: Can a marketing object have multiple primary key fields or composite keys?
text: Can a marketing object have multiple primary key fields or composite keys? You can select more than one primary key field, but marketing objects don't support composite keys.

title: What does a Full Refresh do to a marketing object, and what must the CSV match?
text: What does a Full Refresh do to a marketing object, and what must the CSV match? It deletes the object's data and replaces it with the CSV's data. The file must have the same columns as the marketing object. Needs Manage Marketing Objects + Modify All Marketing Object Records.

title: Which marketing object field properties can't be changed after creation?
text: Which marketing object field properties can't be changed after creation? Field API name, data type, and primary key designation. To change them, delete the field and recreate it — which permanently removes all data in that field.

title: What happens while a marketing object schema change is processing?
text: What happens while a marketing object schema change is processing? It typically completes in a few seconds; you can't make additional schema changes during processing (fields show a "Read Only" indicator), but the object remains available for queries and record creation.

title: When can't you delete a marketing object, and what happens when you do?
text: When can't you delete a marketing object, and what happens when you do? You can't delete it if any other object refers to its data (remove references from content, campaigns, briefs, flows first). Deleting removes all contained data permanently — it can't be restored.

title: What do ViewAllMarketingObjectRecords vs. ManageMarketingObjects grant?
text: What do ViewAllMarketingObjectRecords vs. ManageMarketingObjects grant? ViewAllMarketingObjectRecords = view records from any marketing object. ManageMarketingObjects = view records + create and delete marketing objects.

title: How do you make the Data Management tab appear for marketing users?
text: How do you make the Data Management tab appear for marketing users? Setup → Profiles → Marketing User → Edit → Tab Settings → Data Management → Default On. Users can also add/rearrange it in the tab bar.

title: When should you insert records manually vs. import a CSV?
text: When should you insert records manually vs. import a CSV? Use Add Records (Data Explorer) for a small number of manual entries; use CSV import for larger data loads.

title: In a workspace share chain (A→B→C), why might an asset fail to publish to C?
text: In a workspace share chain (A→B→C), why might an asset fail to publish to C? Sharing is not transitive — publishing to C doesn't publish A's assets; you must share the original source A directly to each target.

title: How does engagement differ between a prospect and a lead?
text: How does engagement differ between a prospect and a lead? A prospect may have interacted only once; a lead is actively engaging with sales or marketing content.

title: What's the conversion potential of a prospect vs. a lead?
text: What's the conversion potential of a prospect vs. a lead? Prospect = low to medium; lead = medium to high.

title: What's required to create a contact, and what happens when converting to an existing conta
text: What's required to create a contact, and what happens when converting to an existing contact? An account is required for creating a contact; when converting a prospect to an existing contact, creating a new account is disabled.

title: Can prospects be added to campaigns, and how?
text: Can prospects be added to campaigns, and how? Yes — prospects are treated as unified individuals, so you can create a unified individual segment, define rules for prospects, and add them to campaigns.

title: What must the Consent Status column include when importing prospects via CSV?
text: What must the Consent Status column include when importing prospects via CSV? Opt-in values, if you plan to send marketing emails.

title: What's the minimum information needed to add a prospect manually?
text: What's the minimum information needed to add a prospect manually? At least last name, email, or phone number.

title: Which flow type converts prospects to leads on engagement score, and how?
text: Which flow type converts prospects to leads on engagement score, and how? A Data 360-Triggered Flow — Start element = engagement score object, condition = engagement score greater than a value → convert to lead.

title: Which flow type converts prospects to contacts, and what's the example condition?
text: Which flow type converts prospects to contacts, and what's the example condition? A Record-Triggered Flow on Prospect (created or updated) with the Convert Prospect action; e.g., if ProspectStatus equals Qualified → convert to contact. Data 360-triggered and form-triggered flows can also convert.

title: What inputs does the Convert Prospect flow action require?
text: What inputs does the Convert Prospect flow action require? Prospect ID; Converted Status (valid picklist option + Converted checkbox selected); Existing/New Contact; Existing/New Account; optional Existing/New Opportunity.

title: How does Multi-Currency affect prospect → lead conversion?
text: How does Multi-Currency affect prospect → lead conversion? If the lead's annual revenue is empty but the prospect's is populated, the prospect's Currency ISO code + annual revenue replace the lead's. Different currency codes → the prospect's currency code wins to avoid conversion problems.

title: What's the Title length gotcha when converting a prospect?
text: What's the Title length gotcha when converting a prospect? Prospect Title allows up to 128 characters, but conversion fails if the lead's Title field would contain more than 80 characters.

title: How do prospect address fields map to Contact and Account?
text: How do prospect address fields map to Contact and Account? City → Mailing City / Billing City; Country → Mailing Country / Mailing Country; State/Province → Mailing State/Province / Billing State/Province; Zip → Mailing Zip / Billing Zip.

title: How does the prospect Company field map on conversion?
text: How does the prospect Company field map on conversion? Lead: Company; Contact: Account Name; Account: Account Name.

title: How does Prospect Currency map on conversion?
text: How does Prospect Currency map on conversion? Lead: Lead Currency; Contact: Contact Currency; Account: Account Currency.

title: What do Lead Assignment Rules determine, and what does each rule entry specify?
text: What do Lead Assignment Rules determine, and what does each rule entry specify? They determine the record owner after a prospect converts to a lead. Each rule entry specifies: processing order, the condition the lead must match, and the user assigned.

title: Which restrictions apply to prospects?
text: Which restrictions apply to prospects? Can't add a prospect as a campaign member; not supported in Data Import Wizard; can't clone or bulk delete prospects; converted prospects don't show in list view; status values = lead status values.

title: What's the difference between default and required content in a Distributed Marketing temp
text: What's the difference between default and required content in a Distributed Marketing template? A default appears automatically but the user can edit/remove it (only one default image); a required phrase is locked and can't be edited. If neither, the section shows as a blank placeholder.

title: How do you force non-marketers to choose only approved subject lines/preheaders?
text: How do you force non-marketers to choose only approved subject lines/preheaders? Lock the subject line/preheader field — if unlocked, users can enter custom text even when approved options are available.

title: What flow elements make an approved template available and prevent canceled sends?
text: What flow elements make an approved template available and prevent canceled sends? An event-triggered flow with the Distributed Marketing and Alerts Message event; Wait Until Date (scheduled sends), Get Records (List Email), Decision (Status = Scheduled), and Send Email Message on the scheduled branch. Canceled emails go down the alternate path and aren't sent.

title: What happens when you unschedule a Distributed Marketing email?
text: What happens when you unschedule a Distributed Marketing email? It cancels the email so it isn't sent — and if it was scheduled with other emails in a campaign, those are canceled too. To send on a new schedule, recreate it.

title: What are the three views of the Distributed Sends dashboard?
text: What are the three views of the Distributed Sends dashboard? Individual Email (Total Recipients = 1–1), Bulk Email (Total Recipients 1), and Bulk Email Recipient Activity (per-recipient engagement). You only see your own sends.

title: What is Conversational Email, and what does it integrate with?
text: What is Conversational Email, and what does it integrate with? Two-way email engagement directly from MC Next — messages support replies. It integrates with Agentforce, Digital Engagement, and Data 360: replies are analyzed for intent, can trigger flows, route to agents or human reps, and update data in real time.

title: Name three Conversational Email use cases.
text: Name three Conversational Email use cases. Drive event registrations, recover abandoned carts, personalize post-purchase journeys, enhance transactional emails, service scheduling, order management, loyalty engagement, product recommendations, account engagement (any three).

title: What's the relationship between campaigns and flows?
text: What's the relationship between campaigns and flows? A campaign can relate to multiple flows, but each flow relates to only one campaign. Changing an active flow's campaign causes reporting and data stream issues.

title: What are the three ways to create the first flow in a campaign?
text: What are the three ways to create the first flow in a campaign? Flow trigger (Build Your Own → pick a trigger), flow template (goal-driven preconfigured flow), or Quick Start (common use case with preconfigured flow + CMS content).

title: What does the signup form flow template automatically create?
text: What does the signup form flow template automatically create? A flow, a form, and (optionally) a landing page — all related to the campaign. Lead is the default record type created on submit.

title: What must you do before sending to a segment or previewing membership?
text: What must you do before sending to a segment or previewing membership? Publish the segment first (republish if stale). For the freshest data, republish the segment immediately before running the flow.

title: How does pausing a flow affect Wait elements?
text: How does pausing a flow affect Wait elements? The pause duration counts toward the total wait time; past-due tasks complete immediately after resume.

title: What are the steps to edit a paused flow?
text: What are the steps to edit a paused flow? Deactivate (choose "Deactivate and cancel work" or "Deactivate and complete work") → Edit As New Version → Activate. The version number is appended to the flow name.

title: How many exit rules can a flow have, and when are they evaluated?
text: How many exit rules can a flow have, and when are they evaluated? Up to 10; evaluated each time a user starts or resumes a flow. Numeric attributes support aggregation functions (Average, Sum, Max, Min).

title: What are the two Decision element logic methods, and how do they differ?
text: What are the two Decision element logic methods, and how do they differ? Define Manually (outcomes evaluated in order — first match wins) vs. Define with AI (Advanced; all outcomes evaluated simultaneously — order has no impact). AI Decision isn't supported for Marketing Cloud flows.

title: How does automated Path Experiment selection declare a winner?
text: How does automated Path Experiment selection declare a winner? Bayesian prediction; a path wins at ≥95% confidence to beat all others, otherwise fallback behavior. Percentages are targets, not exact counts (probability-based assignment).

title: How do you manually select a winning path, and does it require a new version?
text: How do you manually select a winning path, and does it require a new version? Winning Path dropdown on the activated flow — sends all new/remaining/delayed members down that path. It doesn't require saving a new flow version.

title: What are the Subflow element restrictions?
text: What are the Subflow element restrictions? Can't call flows that contain wait elements; variable API names ≤ 40 characters; only flow admins can run inactive flows (others fail at run time if no active version).

title: Which version does a Subflow call by default (API 61.0+)?
text: Which version does a Subflow call by default (API 61.0+)? The active version; if none, the latest version. Run latest via Debug option or appending ?latestSub=true to the parent flow URL.

title: What's required for flows with Wait elements?
text: What's required for flows with Wait elements? They must be autolaunched, and can't be combined with screens, choice, or choice sets.

title: What happens if you don't set a resume time/time zone on Wait Until Date?
text: What happens if you don't set a resume time/time zone on Wait Until Date? The flow resumes at 12 AM in your org's time zone. A past or missing attribute value → pauses then resumes immediately.

title: Where must the Wait Until Event element be placed, and what's unsupported?
text: Where must the Wait Until Event element be placed, and what's unsupported? Immediately after the element being monitored. Dynamic links and links with merge fields are unsupported — use the Any Link option instead.

title: What DMO rules apply to engagement signals?
text: What DMO rules apply to engagement signals? Only DMOs categorized as Engagement; only mapped DMOs/fields; related DMOs must be 1:1 or many-to-one; only one related DMO; item identifier required for custom objective-based recommenders.

title: What are the four engagement signal identifiers?
text: What are the four engagement signal identifiers? User Identifier, Timestamp Identifier, Item Identifier, Event Identifier. A count-based metric is created by default.

title: How can engagement events be counted?
text: How can engagement events be counted? As discrete events (each occurrence, e.g., total email clicks) or grouped repeat events via added fields counted as one signal (e.g., unique click = individual ID + bulk message ID + click event).

title: What are the key inputs of the Send Email Message element?
text: What are the key inputs of the Send Email Message element? Email content, Einstein STO, Einstein Metrics Guard, Sender (Organization-Wide Addresses), CC/BCC, Archive Emails, Track Clicks/Opens, Communication Subscription. Emails don't include My Email Settings signatures.

title: What are the RCS Messaging Session Window options?
text: What are the RCS Messaging Session Window options? Any Time (send regardless), Not During Active Sessions (skip while Active), Not During Open Sessions (skip unless status is Error or Ended).

title: What's the default in-app message expiration?
text: What's the default in-app message expiration? 180 days after you activate the flow (or Custom/Dynamic timeframes).

title: What journeys does the Send to Journey element support?
text: What journeys does the Send to Journey element support? Only journeys with status Running that use an API event entry source; the MCE business unit must be linked to the same data space as the flow. Individual ID → SubscriberKey; contact point email → journey's default email.

title: What are the Get Records storage options and record limit?
text: What are the Get Records storage options and record limit? Only the first record; all records; or all records up to a limit between 2 and 20,000. Store all fields, choose fields, or choose fields + assign variables (advanced).

title: What's required to use a Data Cloud object in Get Records?
text: What's required to use a Data Cloud object in Get Records? A data mapping relating DLO fields to DMO fields must exist in the org.

title: What happens if Update Records has no filter conditions?
text: What happens if Update Records has no filter conditions? The flow updates ALL records for the object. Also, the element doesn't know which fields are required.

title: What are the Delete Records warnings?
text: What are the Delete Records warnings? Even an inactive flow triggers deletes when tested; records are deleted the moment the element runs; Recycle Bin holds them 15 days; flows can delete records pending approval.

title: When are records actually created/deleted in a flow?
text: When are records actually created/deleted in a flow? Not until the interview's transaction completes — when the interview finishes or runs a Screen, Local Action, or Wait element.

title: What are the Collection Filter condition requirements?
text: What are the Collection Filter condition requirements? All Conditions Are Met, Any Condition Is Met, Custom Condition Logic Is Met (e.g., 1 AND (2 OR 3)), or Formula Evaluates to True. Output is null until the filter runs; source collection unchanged.

title: How many sort fields can Collection Sort use?
text: How many sort fields can Collection Sort use? Up to 3 fields (greater to lesser priority). Changes are made directly in the selected collection variable.

title: What are the Transform element limits?
text: What are the Transform element limits? Up to 1 nested collection; formula ≤ 255 characters (use a formula resource for longer); debug shows up to 20 records; data graphs aren't supported for joins.

title: Which operators are limited to Create/Get/Update Records, and which aren't filter conditio
text: Which operators are limited to Create/Get/Update Records, and which aren't filter conditions? In and Not In are available only in Create Records, Get Records, and Update Records. Contains and Is Changed aren't available as filter conditions.

title: Why is filtering on multi-select picklists fragile, and what's the fix?
text: Why is filtering on multi-select picklists fragile, and what's the fix? Semicolon spacing and item order cause mismatches (e.g., "red; green; blue" vs "red;green;blue"). Use the INCLUDES function in a flow formula.

title: What drives the Campaign Stage field?
text: What drives the Campaign Stage field? The statuses of all flows in the campaign (In Planning, In Progress, Completed, Error, Canceled, Paused). One Error flow can make the whole campaign Error.

title: Who can access the Marketing Calendar, and which calendars are default?
text: Who can access the Marketing Calendar, and which calendars are default? Marketing Cloud Admin, Marketing Cloud Manager, or Access Marketing Calendar user permission (Sales). Defaults: Campaigns, Campaign Segment Flows, Segment Flows. Event/form-triggered flows don't appear.

title: What does the NotSentReason field map to?
text: What does the NotSentReason field map to? The Engagement Action Reason field of the Email Engagement DMO. Common reasons: no consent, no opt-in, unauthorized From address, hard bounce, TTL exceeded.

title: How does Agentforce generate campaigns, and what's the "Forward to Agent" step?
text: How does Agentforce generate campaigns, and what's the "Forward to Agent" step? Draft with Agentforce → describe the objective → the agent generates a brief + campaign preview (name, flow, multichannel content). Conversational campaigns add a "Forward to Agent" final step to handle email responses. After saving, preview steps can't be refined.

title: Which agent actions are powered by Salesforce Flow?
text: Which agent actions are powered by Salesforce Flow? Create a Campaign from a Brief, Draft a Campaign Brief, Save Campaign Brief, and Save Campaign. Required custom campaign fields need these flows updated.

title: Which add-on does each non-email channel require?
text: Which add-on does each non-email channel require? SMS → Message Credits - SMS; WhatsApp → Message Credits - WhatsApp; Mobile App → Message Credits - Mobile App Regional (Advanced only).

title: Do US/Canadian short codes require brand/campaign?
text: Do US/Canadian short codes require brand/campaign? No — short codes don't require associated brands or campaigns (long codes do).

title: Which regions host Mobile App Messaging?
text: Which regions host Mobile App Messaging? Germany and United States only.

title: What push services are configured for iOS and Android?
text: What push services are configured for iOS and Android? iOS → APNs (Apple Push Notification service); Android → FCM (Firebase Cloud Messaging).

title: What can't you do after activating a custom mobile app event?
text: What can't you do after activating a custom mobile app event? Delete its attributes (you can deactivate the event, but not delete active events or activated attributes).

title: When do preference page changes go live?
text: When do preference page changes go live? Immediately upon save (published instantly to subscribers).

title: What are the first two columns of a consent import CSV?
text: What are the first two columns of a consent import CSV? Contact point (email or phone) as column 1, consent date as column 2.

title: What happens if you import a consent date earlier than the existing date?
text: What happens if you import a consent date earlier than the existing date? It's ignored (the importer ignores incoming dates before existing consent dates).

title: Why would Lyn need 4 import files for SMS + email consent?
text: Why would Lyn need 4 import files for SMS + email consent? One per channel+status: opted-in email, opted-out email, opted-in SMS, opted-out SMS.

title: Why isn't the first page view recorded when consent banner is required?
text: Why isn't the first page view recorded when consent banner is required? It occurs before the visitor provides consent.

title: What two integration tiles are needed for landing pages with consent banner?
text: What two integration tiles are needed for landing pages with consent banner? Data Cloud integration + Data Cloud Web Tracking Consent Banner integration.

title: What are the four main analytics packages?
text: What are the four main analytics packages? Marketing Engagement Analytics, Flow Reports Analytics, SMS Analytics, Landing Pages and Forms Analytics.

title: What permission sets install vs. view Marketing Performance?
text: What permission sets install vs. view Marketing Performance? Install = Data Cloud admin + Marketing Cloud Admin; View = Tableau Next Included App Business User.

title: What license limit can block Marketing Analytics package install?
text: What license limit can block Marketing Analytics package install? Requires ≥2 available dynamic dashboard licenses.

title: What's the scoring frequency range?
text: What's the scoring frequency range? Every 1 hour to every 24 hours (4 options); more frequent = more credits.

title: Max engagement/fit rules, conditions per rule, and models per edition?
text: Max engagement/fit rules, conditions per rule, and models per edition? 30 engagement + 30 fit rules, 10 conditions/rule, 1 model (Growth) / 2 models (Advanced).

title: What are the point values for form-submit, page-view, and UNSUBSCRIBE (people)?
text: What are the point values for form-submit, page-view, and UNSUBSCRIBE (people)? form-submit +10, page-view +1, UNSUBSCRIBE -5.

title: What's the default account fit rule?
text: What's the default account fit rule? Account Type = Prospect → +30.

title: What prerequisite do STO, Engagement Scoring, and Frequency share?
text: What prerequisite do STO, Engagement Scoring, and Frequency share? Identity resolution ruleset with Individual as primary DMO (must be one of first two rulesets).

title: How much engagement history does Send Time Optimization analyze?
text: How much engagement history does Send Time Optimization analyze? Past 90 days.

title: Which domain is NOT provided by default?
text: Which domain is NOT provided by default? Email sending domains (must be authenticated yourself).

title: What is the tracker domain / link rewriting?
text: What is the tracker domain / link rewriting? URLs are rewritten with the tracker domain, engagement is captured, then forwarded to the target URL.

title: What are the Measure field values for the three scores?
text: What are the Measure field values for the three scores? Engagement → Engagement Score c; Fit → Fit Score c; Overall → People Score c.

title: At send time, what is the actual source of truth for consent in Marketing Cloud Next?
text: At send time, what is the actual source of truth for consent in Marketing Cloud Next? A cache, not the DMO directly. MC Next checks the cache for a Consent Record matching the recipient's email address; only on a miss does it query the Communication Subscription Consent and populate the cache.

title: What happens on a consent cache miss?
text: What happens on a consent cache miss? The Communication Subscription Consent is queried and the cache populated with that recipient's consent value.

title: How long is a consent cache value used for?
text: How long is a consent cache value used for? 90 days, unless it is updated through a supported path that refreshes the cache.

title: Which consent update methods refresh the consent cache?
text: Which consent update methods refresh the consent cache? Manual update from Lead/Contact layouts (Privacy Consent Status LWC), Unsubscribe link / Preference Center, CSV import, and the Create Consent flow activity (official).

title: Which Flow activity officially refreshes the consent cache, and which one is not guarantee
text: Which Flow activity officially refreshes the consent cache, and which one is not guaranteed? Create Consent is the only officially supported one. MessagingConsentV2.MessagingConsent 'seems' to work but has no official guarantee.

title: What happens if you write consent directly into the Communication Subscription Consent DMO
text: What happens if you write consent directly into the Communication Subscription Consent DMO (e.g., via a mapped DLO)? The write does not update the cache, so the new consent can be ignored at send time (stale consent up to the 90-day expiry).

title: What is the symptom of a stale consent cache?
text: What is the symptom of a stale consent cache? A recipient can keep receiving email even though the CSC DMO shows Opted Out (or a new Opt In may not be honored) until the cache entry is refreshed or expires.

title: How is the primary Id of the Communication Subscription Consent DMO formed?
text: How is the primary Id of the Communication Subscription Consent DMO formed? Forged from the Contact Point and the Comm Subscription Channel Type (e.g., contact+002@bamsoo.com#0eBbF00000000HlUAI).

title: What is MC Next's consent default when no record is found for a Contact Point / Subscripti
text: What is MC Next's consent default when no record is found for a Contact Point / Subscription / Channel? Implicit Opt Out — the recipient is assumed opted out.

title: Which DMO stores the mapping of a Subscription to its Engagement Channels, and how is the
text: Which DMO stores the mapping of a Subscription to its Engagement Channels, and how is the combination identified? Communication Subscription Channel Type DMO (CommSubscriptionChannelType Home DSO); each row is a subscription + engagement channel combination, uniquely identified by Comm Subscription Channel Type Id.

title: Which DMO defines Engagement Channels themselves, and what do its record IDs start with?
text: Which DMO defines Engagement Channels themselves, and what do its record IDs start with? Engagement Channel Type DMO (EngagementChannelType Home DSO); records start with 0eF .

title: After Summer '25, why might a Contact Point show 2 consent records for the same Subscripti
text: After Summer '25, why might a Contact Point show 2 consent records for the same Subscription + Channel? The CSC DMO can map to both MessagingConsent and MessagingConsentV2 DSOs. Since Summer '25 only the V2 DSO is written; instances created earlier can have two records, each with a distinct Data Source.

title: When you modify consent and the existing record was created via the V1 system, what happen
text: When you modify consent and the existing record was created via the V1 system, what happens? The existing V1 record is not updated; a new record is created with V2 as the Data Source. MC Next always uses the latest record as the current Consent Status.

title: What is dummyCsctToken used for?
text: What is dummyCsctToken used for? Unsubscribing from a Test Email — it is a placeholder Comm Subscription Channel Type.

title: How does the Privacy Consent Status component determine what to display?
text: How does the Privacy Consent Status component determine what to display? For each Subscription, it checks the CSC DMO for a related record (same Email Address + Subscription, Email Engagement Channel 0eB… ); displays the latest record's status, or Opted Out if none exists (implicit).

title: Name the five ways to modify the Consent Status.
text: Name the five ways to modify the Consent Status. 1) Manual (Privacy Consent Status component dropdown) 2) Unsubscribe link in email 3) Preference Center in email 4) Import (CSV, Consent menu) 5) Flow (Segment Triggered or Automation Triggered; e.g., 2-step DOI).

title: What does every Promotional Email require, and is there two-click unsubscribe?
text: What does every Promotional Email require, and is there two-click unsubscribe? At least one Unsubscribe link (or alternatively a Preference Center link), and clicking immediately opts out — there is no two-click unsubscribe in MCG/A so far.

title: A Unified Individual has several email addresses — how is their per-subscription consent s
text: A Unified Individual has several email addresses — how is their per-subscription consent status determined? There is no single correct answer; it's a business choice. A clarifying pattern is to build a new DMO related to Unified Individual holding every address + its current status per subscription, surfaced via Data Cloud Profile Related Records on Lead/Contact layouts.

title: Which DLO stores consent history, and is it mapped to a DMO?
text: Which DLO stores consent history, and is it mapped to a DMO? ConsentAuditTrailV2-ConsentAuditTrail (previously the non-V2 version, unused since Summer '25); it is NOT mapped to any DMO and acts as append-only history, while the CSC DMO is upsert (current state).

title: Where is Marketing Cloud Next consent data stored?
text: Where is Marketing Cloud Next consent data stored? In Data Cloud, in the Communication Subscription Consent (CSC) Data Model Object (DMO).

title: What two things does Marketing Cloud Next consent key on?
text: What two things does Marketing Cloud Next consent key on? The Contact Point value (email/phone/device ID) + the Communication Subscription Channel Type (CSCT) ID.

title: Why is consent intentionally agnostic of PartyID?
text: Why is consent intentionally agnostic of PartyID? A single email/phone can map to multiple individuals (shared household, merges). Keying on the individual would require resolving whose preference "wins"; keying on the address is conservative and regulator-friendly (any opt-out on the address = address opted out).

title: What happens when two people share one email and one opts out?
text: What happens when two people share one email and one opts out? The opt-out affects all of them — there's no way to send to some and suppress others sharing the same address.

title: What's the key difference between the Consent Audit Trail and the CSC DMO?
text: What's the key difference between the Consent Audit Trail and the CSC DMO? The Audit Trail is append-only (historical record of every change); the CSC DMO stores current status and is updated in place.

title: Why is PartyId blank in audit trail rows?
text: Why is PartyId blank in audit trail rows? Consent is keyed on Contact Point value + CSCT ID, so PartyId is written blank by design — even for Lead/Contact records.

title: How do you attribute "who" made a consent change?
text: How do you attribute "who" made a consent change? There's no UserId/ActorId field. Use caller-provided source attribution (ConsentCapturedSourceType, ConsentCapturedSourceName, ConsentCapturedSourceDetails, SenderId).

title: How do you delete audit trail rows for GDPR?
text: How do you delete audit trail rows for GDPR? Use the Consent API "ShouldForget" endpoint on the Individual — flags the individual, async deletion across DMOs, reprocessed at 30/60/90 days, permanent. No UI for bulk deletion (engage Support).

title: What are three common causes of rejected audit rows?
text: What are three common causes of rejected audit rows? Wrong object mapping, date-format issues, and status case mismatch ("OptIn" instead of "OPT IN").

title: What are the four input parameters of the Create Consent action?
text: What are the four input parameters of the Create Consent action? Consent Status, Contact Point, Channel, and Communication Subscription.

title: In which three flow types is Create Consent/Consent Request available?
text: In which three flow types is Create Consent/Consent Request available? Data Cloud-Triggered Flows, Automation Event-Triggered Flows, and On-Demand Flows.

title: Name the unsupported consent write paths.
text: Name the unsupported consent write paths. Data Stream mapped to Consent DLO; Bulk Ingestion API to Consent DMO; Batch Data Transform to a DLO mapped to CSC DMO; legacy MessagingConsent/MessagingConsentV2 actions.

title: What's the recommended 2-step process for consent at scale (millions of records)?
text: What's the recommended 2-step process for consent at scale (millions of records)? 1) Initial data load into Data Cloud (Batch Data Transform creates records in the consent DLO). 2) Data Cloud-Triggered Flow with Create Consent to write consent so it's honored at send time.

title: What's the CSV consent import limit and purpose?
text: What's the CSV consent import limit and purpose? 50,000 rows per file, intended for one-time loads — not sustained high-volume sync.

title: What does "contactPointValue provided value cannot be formatted" mean?
text: What does "contactPointValue provided value cannot be formatted" mean? The Contact Point field must reference a contact point value (e.g., an email address), not a contact point ID (e.g., Contact Point Email ID).

title: What are the two steps of double opt-in?
text: What are the two steps of double opt-in? 1) Submit sign-up form + receive transactional confirmation email. 2) Click the confirmation link to verify intent — only then is consent recorded.

title: Why must the DOI confirmation email be Transactional?
text: Why must the DOI confirmation email be Transactional? Only Transactional emails can be sent to contacts without confirmed consent; Promotional would fail delivery for unconfirmed contacts.

title: What does the Wait Until Event step monitor in a DOI flow?
text: What does the Wait Until Event step monitor in a DOI flow? The transactional confirmation email (flow action to monitor) and the opt-in confirmation link/CTA (link to monitor).

title: Why might Email Opt-Out Rate look lower than expected?
text: Why might Email Opt-Out Rate look lower than expected? Preference Page unsubscribes are processed as consent updates, not Email Engagement Unsubscribe events — so they're not included in the Email Opt-Out Rate.

title: What are the customization limits of out-of-the-box preference pages?
text: What are the customization limits of out-of-the-box preference pages? Limited branding; no URL-parameter pre-population; limited thank-you page customization; no multi-channel per page; no coding languages (AMPscript/Apex); can't revert a published custom page.

title: How do you localize a Preference Page?
text: How do you localize a Preference Page? Use multiple Preference Pages (one per language) with dynamic rules to surface the right URL based on a language-preference field in Data Cloud.

title: Does the Contact/Lead Email Opt Out field (HasOptedOutOfEmail) auto-sync with MC Next cons
text: Does the Contact/Lead Email Opt Out field (HasOptedOutOfEmail) auto-sync with MC Next consent? No — you need a two-Flow bridge: Flow 1 (Automation Event-Triggered, CRM→MC Next) and Flow 2 (Data Cloud-Triggered, MC Next→CRM).

title: What event does Flow 1 (CRM→MC Next consent sync) use?
text: What event does Flow 1 (CRM→MC Next consent sync) use? The "Prospect, Lead, Contact or Related Record Change" event in an Automation Event-Triggered Flow, with a Consent Request Action.

title: What tool synchronizes consent between Marketing Cloud Engagement and MC Next?
text: What tool synchronizes consent between Marketing Cloud Engagement and MC Next? The Consent Mapping tool (Email and SMS available today).

title: When is consent evaluated for transactional emails?
text: When is consent evaluated for transactional emails? The transactional consent check is off by default, but if a Communication Subscription is populated at send time, consent is evaluated even when the global setting is disabled.

title: Does transactional SMS (OTP, 2FA) require consent?
text: Does transactional SMS (OTP, 2FA) require consent? Yes — under TCPA and most carrier rules, transactional SMS still requires consent.

title: At what level does MC Next record opt-outs?
text: At what level does MC Next record opt-outs? Communication Subscription level — there's no account-level or channel-level opt-out today.

title: How do spam complaints (FBL) and Reply Mail Management affect consent?
text: How do spam complaints (FBL) and Reply Mail Management affect consent? They opt the recipient out of all of their current subscriptions (subscription level, individually).

title: How do you segment on consent data?
