text: How do you segment on consent data? Direct segmentation isn't supported — build a Calculated Insight on consent data and use it in the segment filter (metered, consumes credits).

title: What two prerequisites must be met before the consent package installs cleanly?
text: What two prerequisites must be met before the consent package installs cleanly? Data Protection enabled, and Data Cloud Salesforce Connector permissions (Read + View All Records) on Communication Subscription, Communication Subscription Channel Type, and Engagement Channel Type.

title: Why do consent data streams fail to ingest on new sandboxes?
text: Why do consent data streams fail to ingest on new sandboxes? They're in NEEDS ACTIVATION state because connections aren't activated by default — activate each stream in Data Cloud Setup.

title: Does ingesting consent via the internal Salesforce connector consume credits?
text: Does ingesting consent via the internal Salesforce connector consume credits? No — as of Aug 7, 2025, it's included with Data 360. External-source ingestion (Snowflake, S3) does consume credits.

title: Can you deploy Communication Subscriptions between orgs?
text: Can you deploy Communication Subscriptions between orgs? No — they're stored as data in the Communication Subscription DMO, and only metadata deploys to a sandbox.

title: What's the first step of consent troubleshooting?
text: What's the first step of consent troubleshooting? Confirm the consent record in the CSC DMO (Data Cloud Data Explorer Communication Subscription Consent DMO), filtered by contact point value and CSCT ID.

title: How do you repair consent by volume?
text: How do you repair consent by volume? Single/small set → Consent Status LWC; ≤50k rows → Consent Import CSV; 50k rows → stage into a custom DMO then run a Data Cloud-Triggered Flow calling Create Consent.

title: What are the four levels of the Salesforce consent data model?
text: What are the four levels of the Salesforce consent data model? Global Consent (Individual), Engagement Channel Consent (ContactPointTypeConsent), Contact Point Consent (ContactPointConsent), Data Use Purpose (DataUsePurpose). Brand (BusinessBrand) is not a consent object but distinguishes brands.

title: Why can't you map external consent data directly into the Communication Subscription Conse
text: Why can't you map external consent data directly into the Communication Subscription Consent DMO? Although the data appears to save successfully, MC Next ignores it during message sends — the transactional consent service never registers the change, causing silent dropouts, compliance violations, and UI misalignment.

title: What three flows keep CRM, Data 360 and MC Next consent in sync?
text: What three flows keep CRM, Data 360 and MC Next consent in sync? 1) New Registration Automation (Data Cloud-Triggered) establishes baseline consent; 2) MC Next → CRM mirrors preference page/unsubscribe changes; 3) CRM → MC Next pushes back-office CommSubscriptionConsent edits upstream.

title: What triggers Flow 1 (New Registration Automation) and what does its Decision evaluate?
text: What triggers Flow 1 (New Registration Automation) and what does its Decision evaluate? A created ssot Individual dlm record in Data Cloud; the Decision evaluates the related CRM CommSubscriptionConsent's Privacy Consent Status to branch the Create Consent action.

title: Why must Flow 1 map the contact point dynamically from the retrieved email record?
text: Why must Flow 1 map the contact point dynamically from the retrieved email record? MC Next consent is bound to the contact point (email value), not the Lead/Contact record — so the Create Consent action needs the retrieved email address, never a hard-coded ID.

title: Which action does Flow 2 (MC Next → CRM) use, and what values does it write?
text: Which action does Flow 2 (MC Next → CRM) use, and what values does it write? A standard Update Records action on the CRM core object: sets Privacy Consent Status to Opt In when Data Cloud Consent Status is True, and Opt Out when False.

title: What triggers Flow 2?
text: What triggers Flow 2? An updated ssot CommunicationSubscriptionConsent dlm record in Data Cloud — caused by a preference page submission or an unsubscribe URL click in an email campaign.

title: What triggers Flow 3 and where is the object anchor set?
text: What triggers Flow 3 and where is the object anchor set? An updated CRM CommSubscriptionConsent record; Automation Event-Triggered Flow with the anchor set to Consent Giver ID (Contact).

title: How does Flow 3 stop future sends after a back-office opt-out?
text: How does Flow 3 stop future sends after a back-office opt-out? The Create Consent action sets Opt Out, telling the transactional engine to treat the contact point as suppressed, immediately preventing future campaign deployment.

title: What's the only supported route for consent updates into MC Next?
text: What's the only supported route for consent updates into MC Next? Native Create Consent Flow Actions inside Data Cloud-Triggered Flows or Automation Event-Triggered Flows — never direct DMO field mapping via data streams or batch transforms.

title: What three rules explain almost everything about consent in Marketing Cloud Next?
text: What three rules explain almost everything about consent in Marketing Cloud Next? 1) Consent attaches to a contact point value , not a person. 2) No consent record means opted out . 3) At send time the source of truth is a cache , not the record.

title: What does consent attach to in MC Next, and what does it NOT attach to?
text: What does consent attach to in MC Next, and what does it NOT attach to? It attaches to a Contact Point Value (email address, or phone in E.164). It does not attach to an Individual, Unified Individual, or CRM Prospect/Lead/Contact — and it isn't duplicated in CRM.

title: Why does Salesforce key consent on the address rather than the person?
text: Why does Salesforce key consent on the address rather than the person? When several individuals share a contact point (e.g. office@acme.com ), keying on the person forces the platform to decide whose preference wins. Keying on the address gives the more restrictive default — an opt-out is binding for everyone behind it, which is how regulators look at it.

title: What happens to consent when someone changes their email address?
text: What happens to consent when someone changes their email address? Their consent is stranded on the old address . The new address has no record, which means opted out .

title: What happens to the consent record when you delete the Contact?
text: What happens to the consent record when you delete the Contact? The consent record stays in Data 360 , keyed to an address that no longer appears anywhere in your CRM.

title: On the day you switch Marketing Cloud Next on, what is the consent state of your existing
text: On the day you switch Marketing Cloud Next on, what is the consent state of your existing database? Entirely opted out — no consent record means opt-out, so the whole base starts suppressed until you import consent.

title: Can you drive commercial sends from custom flag fields on Contact or Lead?
text: Can you drive commercial sends from custom flag fields on Contact or Lead? No. There is no supported path. Custom flags can feed the standard model through a flow, but they cannot replace it — updating those objects alone does nothing at send time.

title: How many CSV files do you need for two subscriptions across email and SMS, with both opt-i
text: How many CSV files do you need for two subscriptions across email and SMS, with both opt-in and opt-out? Eight — each file covers exactly one channel, one subscription and one status (2 subscriptions × 2 channels × 2 statuses).

title: What happens if you import a consent date earlier than the one already on the record?
text: What happens if you import a consent date earlier than the one already on the record? The platform ignores it . The row still imports, nothing fails, nothing warns you — and the date you think you loaded is not the date that's there.

title: How many consent statuses does the MC Next record support, and what does the CRM object ca
text: How many consent statuses does the MC Next record support, and what does the CRM object carry instead? Only two — opt-in and opt-out, nothing in between. The CRM CommSubscriptionConsent object (the empty one) carries OptInPending / OptOutPending since API 58.0 — every state a double opt-in flow could want, on the object that has no bearing on sends.

title: Which message types require a consent check?
text: Which message types require a consent check? Promotional email required ; transactional email not required ; promotional SMS/WhatsApp/RCS required ; transactional SMS/WhatsApp/RCS required .

title: What must you accept to disable consent checks entirely, and what does the change not affe
text: What must you accept to disable consent checks entirely, and what does the change not affect? You must affirm in writing that you accept responsibility for compliance problems. ⚠️ The change does not affect active flows — anything already running keeps checking.

title: How does SMS/WhatsApp/RCS opt-out granularity differ from email?
text: How does SMS/WhatsApp/RCS opt-out granularity differ from email? Each SMS code, WhatsApp number and RCS agent maps to one or more subscriptions , and opting out of the channel opts the person out of every subscription mapped to it . There is no per-subscription opt-out over SMS.

title: What is the one exception to the one-channel-one-consent rule?
text: What is the one exception to the one-channel-one-consent rule? RCS — Salesforce says you can reuse existing SMS consent when the messaging use case stays the same, and tells you to check that with your legal team.

title: How do Compliance BCC and CC recipients behave with consent checks?
text: How do Compliance BCC and CC recipients behave with consent checks? Compliance BCC is excluded from consent checks entirely (it doesn't represent a person). CC recipients are suppressed if the primary recipient doesn't get the email because the address lacks consent.

title: What are the three consent models in Salesforce, and which does MC Next read?
text: What are the three consent models in Salesforce, and which does MC Next read? 1) Salesforce Consent Data Model (legal basis). 2) Data 360 consent objects (activation eligibility). 3) Communication Subscription Consent (MC Next sends). MC Next reads only the third , through the cache.

title: Name the four consent objects and the Id prefixes of the first three.
text: Name the four consent objects and the Id prefixes of the first three. Communication Subscription ( 0Xl ), Engagement Channel Type ( 0eF ), Communication Subscription Channel Type ( 0eB ), Communication Subscription Consent (no prefix). The first three are CRM objects ; the consent record lives in Data 360 only .

title: Since which API version have CommSubscription and CommSubscriptionConsent existed?
text: Since which API version have CommSubscription and CommSubscriptionConsent existed? API 48.0 (Spring '20) — roughly five years before Marketing Cloud Next existed.

title: Does Engagement Channel Type have a DMO?
text: Does Engagement Channel Type have a DMO? No. Communication Subscription Channel Type carries an ssot EngagementChannelTypeId c with no relationship attached — on the Data 360 side the channel is a bare identifier pointing nowhere.

title: Can you change a subscription's scope after creation?
text: Can you change a subscription's scope after creation? No. With business units (Advanced), a subscription is assigned to a single BU or all BUs, and the scope cannot be edited after creation . It also limits which channels you can add.

title: What happens when you delete a Communication Subscription?
text: What happens when you delete a Communication Subscription? It deletes all of its consent data — a legal exposure, not just an admin inconvenience. Salesforce's recommendation is simply not to delete subscriptions once consent has been collected.

title: Does a new subscription automatically appear on the preference page?
text: Does a new subscription automatically appear on the preference page? No. MC Next ships one customizable email preference page containing only the default marketing subscription. Adding subscriptions to it is a separate step after creation.

title: Does MC Next support frequency capping on a subscription?
text: Does MC Next support frequency capping on a subscription? No. The platform has a CommSubscriptionTiming object for exactly this, but MC Next doesn't map it . Send-frequency rules live in your journey logic or segment.

title: What is the whole join key for a consent record, and what does it make possible/impossible
text: What is the whole join key for a consent record, and what does it make possible/impossible? Contact point value + Communication Subscription Channel Type Id . Searching consent by email address works ; searching it by person doesn't . The consent DMO has exactly one traversable relationship (N:1 to CSCT).

title: What is the state of the Party field on the consent DMO?
text: What is the state of the Party field on the consent DMO? It's an out-of-the-box relationship between Individual.Id and CommunicationSubscriptionConsent.Party , wired end to end from the DLO — and always empty . Never build on it.

title: How do you correctly join a consent record back to a person?
text: How do you correctly join a consent record back to a person? Through the Contact Point Email or Contact Point Phone DMO (which carry the PartyId mapping), matching on the contact point value — the same way the Privacy Consent Status component does it.

title: What are the two namespaces of the consent DMO, and why does it matter?
text: What are the two namespaces of the consent DMO, and why does it matter? The older ssot CommunicationSubscriptionConsent dlm and the newer std CommunicationSubscriptionConsentDmo dlm (API version 254). Their field lists are not identical — the public reference for the older one lists ssot ContactPointId c and no contact point value field at all .

title: What is the name of the data kit that carries consent, and how many streams does it instal
text: What is the name of the data kit that carries consent, and how many streams does it install? UnifiedMessagingConsent — it installs two data streams: one for the consent records ( MessagingConsentV2 ) and one for the audit trail ( ConsentAuditTrailV2 ).

title: What are the two ways an org ends up with duplicate consent records for the same contact p
text: What are the two ways an org ends up with duplicate consent records for the same contact point and subscription? 1) The documented generation switch (pre-Summer '25 orgs moved MessagingConsent → MessagingConsentV2 ). 2) The org-ID naming quirk — Salesforce appended the org ID to stream names, both spellings stayed active, so even a V2-only org gets duplicates.

title: Why is the org-ID naming quirk dangerous for queries?
text: Why is the org-ID naming quirk dangerous for queries? Send-time behaviour is fine ( latest record wins ), but a naive SELECT against the DMO returns both rows with no signal which one the platform acted on — unexplained duplicate rows in consent exports.

title: Why is no consent DLO name portable?
text: Why is no consent DLO name portable? The org ID is appended to the stream name, so the name differs per org (and changes when the org ID changes). Nothing that references the consent DLO by name is portable — not a Data Transform, saved query, Calculated Insight, or runbook.

title: What are the key fields in the V2 consent stream → DMO mapping?
text: What are the key fields in the V2 consent stream → DMO mapping? ConsentId (primary key = contact point value + CSCT Id), ConsentCapturedDateTime (when the person decided) and UpdatedTime (when the row changed) as separate fields, and PartyId mapped to Party (carrying nothing). Ten fields mapped, seventeen left unmapped.

title: What is the one rule governing consent writes?
text: What is the one rule governing consent writes? Only writes that go through the consent service count. The service writes into a DLO mapped to the CSC DMO and updates the cache. Everything else produces a row and changes nothing in the cache.

title: Name the supported consent write methods.
text: Name the supported consent write methods. Bulk CSV import (50k rows/file), Privacy Consent Status component, unsubscribe URLs / preference pages / SMS & WhatsApp opt-outs, landing page forms paired with an Automation Event-Triggered Flow, and the Consent Request / Create Consent flow action.

title: When did the Consent Request element become available in Record-Triggered Flows?
text: When did the Consent Request element become available in Record-Triggered Flows? Winter '27 Release — with some orgs receiving the option before the official release window.

title: Name the unsupported consent write methods and why they fail.
text: Name the unsupported consent write methods and why they fail. Data stream mapped directly to the consent DLO; Bulk Ingestion API writing to the consent DMO; Batch Data Transforms updating a mapped DLO; legacy MessagingConsent / MessagingConsentV2 flow actions; external systems writing into the consent DMO. All bypass the consent service .

title: How does an unsupported write fail, and does anything error?
text: How does an unsupported write fail, and does anything error? It fails in both directions — an email may fail to send to an address that appears opted in, and may send to an address that appears opted out. The DMO can also disagree with the Privacy Consent Status component. Nothing errors anywhere.

title: How do you fix consent written through an unsupported path?
text: How do you fix consent written through an unsupported path? There is no cache flush — re-issue every affected consent change through a supported method. Small sets: the component. Larger: a Data Cloud-Triggered Flow calling Create Consent across the affected population, or CSV import as a replay tool.

title: Where can you find consent data?
text: Where can you find consent data? On the record via the Privacy Consent Status component (Lead/Contact/Person Account); in Data Explorer against the CSC DMO (search on contact point value); in Query Editor for joins and audit-trail data (Data Explorer won't show the audit trail).

title: What four things can you currently not see about consent?
text: What four things can you currently not see about consent? 1) The cache . 2) Who changed a record (no actor field). 3) Consent history on the record. 4) Anything in the Party field. (Plus: the component shows only the 100 most recent records.)

title: How long do consent changes take to appear in the DMO?
text: How long do consent changes take to appear in the DMO? Minutes — long enough that a test looks like it failed when it has only just started, and long enough that people retry the write and create a second problem. With Consent Changes in flows, up to a couple of hours.

title: How do you undo a bad initial consent import?
text: How do you undo a bad initial consent import? You can't self-serve — audit trail rows cannot be deleted through any self-service route , so it means opening a case with Salesforce Support. Plan the initial import as if you cannot undo it.

title: What is the unresolved question about the 90-day cache clock?
text: What is the unresolved question about the 90-day cache clock? Whether it runs from the write or the last read , and whether a send refreshes the entry. If it resets on read, 90 days is a floor rather than a ceiling .

title: What is the unresolved question about merging Contacts?
text: What is the unresolved question about merging Contacts? What happens to consent when two Contacts with different email addresses are merged. Nothing in the documentation covers it, and it matters to anyone running deduplication at scale.

title: Name the five Data 360 segment types and their primary job.
text: Name the five Data 360 segment types and their primary job. Standard (scheduled audience on a DMO), Real-Time (millisecond on-demand), Waterfall (priority-ranked mutually-exclusive offers), Dynamic (parameterized query, no persistence), Data Kit (predefined segment).

title: What's the default lookback window, and its maximum?
text: What's the default lookback window, and its maximum? Default 90 days; up to 2 years (or 360 days via the "Days" dropdown). Container criteria can override the segment-level window.

title: What's the maximum number of segments per org?
text: What's the maximum number of segments per org? 9,950.

title: What can't a real-time segment do?
text: What can't a real-time segment do? Use exclusion criteria, nested batch segments, segment counts, or manual publish. (Requires Segment ID + Timestamp fields in the real-time data graph.)

title: What problem does a waterfall segment solve?
text: What problem does a waterfall segment solve? It processes segments in priority order so a customer matching multiple segments is placed only in the highest-priority one — creating mutually exclusive audiences (one offer per person).

title: What are three key waterfall segment constraints?
text: What are three key waterfall segment constraints? Max 20 segments; a segment can exist in only one waterfall (no nested segments); rapid publish not available.

title: How is a dynamic segment run, and why?
text: How is a dynamic segment run, and why? Via API call through a broadcast flow supplying runtime values — because it uses placeholders and doesn't persist data in Segment Membership DMOs (can't be scheduled/published via UI).

title: What are the standard and rapid publish intervals?
text: What are the standard and rapid publish intervals? Standard = 12 or 24 hours; Rapid = 1 or 4 hours (Marketing Cloud Engagement / file storage targets only).

title: How many rapid-publish segments can you create, and can you convert standard → rapid?
text: How many rapid-publish segments can you create, and can you convert standard → rapid? Up to 20 rapid-publish segments; you cannot change a standard publish to rapid publish after creation.

title: What do the "Latest" and "History" segment membership DMOs store?
text: What do the "Latest" and "History" segment membership DMOs store? Latest = profiles in the most recent publish; History = prior publish (last 30 days), with Delta Type marking New/Existing/Removed.

title: Why should you "stop the publish schedule" instead of deactivating a segment you might reu
text: Why should you "stop the publish schedule" instead of deactivating a segment you might reuse? Deactivation is permanent (can't be re-enabled); stopping the schedule preserves the segment for future use.

title: Why do composite keys cause problems in the Segment Canvas?
text: Why do composite keys cause problems in the Segment Canvas? The canvas joins on single-field relationships; composite keys only work in manual queries where every field is explicitly defined. Use DMOs with a single unique primary key.

title: What's the difference between a direct and a related attribute?
text: What's the difference between a direct and a related attribute? Direct = single data point (postal code, name; 1:1 or N:1); related = collection of data points (purchase history; 1:N, often behavioral).

title: How do same-container vs. separate-container attributes behave?
text: How do same-container vs. separate-container attributes behave? Same container = AND on the same row (single record); separate containers = independent filters (bought any X AND any Y).

title: What are the five aggregation types?
text: What are the five aggregation types? Count, Sum, Average, Max, Min.

title: What are the filter/attribute/container limits in the segment canvas?
text: What are the filter/attribute/container limits in the segment canvas? 50 filters per tab (Include/Exclude), 100 attributes per segment, 20 filters per container.

title: What are the nesting limits?
text: What are the nesting limits? Up to 3 levels within a container; up to 10 levels across containers.

title: What three steps make up Group/Rank/Limit?
text: What three steps make up Group/Rank/Limit? (1) Group By a shared attribute, (2) Sort By an attribute with order, (3) Limit the maximum records per group.

title: What are two constraints on grouping/ranking/limiting rules?
text: What are two constraints on grouping/ranking/limiting rules? Max 3 group + 3 sort rules per ruleset; applies only within qualified profiles (not global), and only to direct attributes.

title: How are object joins and value matching case-sensitive?
text: How are object joins and value matching case-sensitive? Object joins are case-sensitive (c12d3 ≠ C12D3); queries honor exact matching (accents, leading zeros) but text operators are case-insensitive.

title: What is the Approximate Segment Population field?
text: What is the Approximate Segment Population field? A 95%-confidence range estimate of the population (enable in Feature Manager); less accurate for small populations or low Segment On counts.

title: What does an attribute shortcut store, and what's its limit?
text: What does an attribute shortcut store, and what's its limit? Segment-on object + object path + target attribute (reusable filter); limit 500 per tenant, scoped to data space.

title: What does hierarchical aggregation do, and on which entities?
text: What does hierarchical aggregation do, and on which entities? Rolls up revenues across account hierarchies (parent/subsidiary); supported on Account/Unified Account, up to 5 containers and 3 levels per DMO.

title: How far back can an Engagement DMO's event date field go in a segment?
text: How far back can an Engagement DMO's event date field go in a segment? Up to 24 months; a segment fails if the date range exceeds this.

title: What are the value limits of the Is In operator?
text: What are the value limits of the Is In operator? Up to 100 comma-separated values (bulk paste up to 10,000 via import).

title: What two prerequisites must be met before creating an Einstein segment?
text: What two prerequisites must be met before creating an Einstein segment? A completed identity resolution ruleset creating a Unified Individual DMO with ≥10 records, and enabling generative AI + Einstein Segment Creation in Feature Manager.

title: How does Einstein Segment Creation reduce bias and improve accuracy?
text: How does Einstein Segment Creation reduce bias and improve accuracy? Demographic attributes are removed by default, and attributes producing fewer than 10 results are stripped.

title: What does Einstein Data Prism do?
text: What does Einstein Data Prism do? Grounds generative AI by scanning metadata (schema, relationships, sample values, descriptions), auto-generating descriptions, and returning focused grounding data for natural-language queries.

title: What does Metadata Studio let you do?
text: What does Metadata Studio let you do? Validate/edit object+field descriptions and exclude irrelevant entities so they aren't sent to the LLM or used for grounding.

title: Where are Einstein Data Prism and Metadata Studio unsupported?
text: Where are Einstein Data Prism and Metadata Studio unsupported? Government Cloud Plus — don't enable the feature there.

title: When are segmentation credits consumed?
text: When are segmentation credits consumed? On segment publish (Data Services "Segmentation" / Flex Credits "Data 360 Segmentation"), plus Data Queries for counting/building/previewing.

title: How many questions, how long, and what's the pass mark for the Marketing Cloud Next Consul
text: How many questions, how long, and what's the pass mark for the Marketing Cloud Next Consultant exam? 60 scored multiple-choice questions (plus up to 5 unscored ones randomly integrated), 105 minutes , pass mark 72% (at least 44 of 60 correct). Average 1 minute 45 seconds per question. Pass/fail — no benefit to scoring above the threshold.

title: What are the formal prerequisites for the exam, and which release is it based on?
text: What are the formal prerequisites for the exam, and which release is it based on? No formal prerequisites , but a solid understanding of Salesforce CRM and Data 360 Fundamentals is highly recommended. Content is based on the Summer '26 release .

title: How many key areas does the exam cover, and what does each percentage represent?
text: How many key areas does the exam cover, and what does each percentage represent? Six key areas. Each percentage is the weighting — approximately how many questions you can expect from that category.

title: Is Marketing Cloud a product? What is it?
text: Is Marketing Cloud a product? What is it? It's not a single product — it's the broader brand of Salesforce's next-generation marketing portfolio. Marketing Cloud Next is just one product inside it.

title: Name the four products in the Marketing Cloud portfolio and what each evolved from.
text: Name the four products in the Marketing Cloud portfolio and what each evolved from. Marketing Cloud Next (evolution of Marketing Cloud Engagement) · Salesforce Personalization (evolution of Marketing Cloud Personalization, real-time) · Marketing Intelligence (evolution of Marketing Cloud Intelligence, AI-powered analytics) · Loyalty Management (no-code B2B/B2C loyalty & rewards).

title: What two editions does Marketing Cloud Next offer, and how do they relate?
text: What two editions does Marketing Cloud Next offer, and how do they relate? Growth Edition and Advanced Edition . Advanced includes all Growth capabilities plus additional features. The list isn't exhaustive — new capabilities arrive each release.

title: Which scoring types are available in which editions?
text: Which scoring types are available in which editions? Individual (people) scoring = both Growth and Advanced. Account scoring = Advanced only . The predictive AI features Engagement Scoring and Engagement Frequency are also Advanced only .

title: How does Salesforce frame the Marketing Cloud Next setup process?
text: How does Salesforce frame the Marketing Cloud Next setup process? As configuration rather than implementation — MC Next and Data 360 can be enabled in just a few clicks with a setup interface guiding you through the process.

title: At a minimum, how many key configuration steps are there, and what are the first three?
text: At a minimum, how many key configuration steps are there, and what are the first three? Six key steps (plus optional ones not required for core functionality). The first three — driven by the Setup Assistant — are: set up Data 360 , enable Marketing Cloud , and deploy the required data streams .

title: Which two permission sets must a System Administrator-profile user assign before anyone co
text: Which two permission sets must a System Administrator-profile user assign before anyone configures MC Next? Data Cloud Architect (Data 360 setup, data modelling objects, install data kits, deploy streams, configure identity resolution) and Marketing Admin (configure most marketing settings in Setup, publish/activate campaigns and segments).

title: What happened to the Data Cloud Admin permission set?
text: What happened to the Data Cloud Admin permission set? It was renamed to Data Cloud Architect in the Spring '26 release . ⚠️ A common exam distractor is the old name.

title: Why is "System Administrator" a distractor in permission-set questions?
text: Why is "System Administrator" a distractor in permission-set questions? Because System Administrator is a profile, not a permission set . The permission sets are Data Cloud Architect and Marketing Admin.

title: What three tasks does the Marketing Cloud Next Setup Assistant guide you through?
text: What three tasks does the Marketing Cloud Next Setup Assistant guide you through? Set up Data 360 , enable Marketing Cloud , and deploy the required data streams — each initiated with a single button click that starts the automated enablement process.

title: After the Setup Assistant completes, what two additional required tasks remain?
text: After the Setup Assistant completes, what two additional required tasks remain? 1) Add the company's physical address to the Company Information page (included in the footer of promotional emails for regulatory compliance). 2) Create an authenticated domain .

title: How does domain setup differ between Marketing Cloud Engagement and Marketing Cloud Next?
text: How does domain setup differ between Marketing Cloud Engagement and Marketing Cloud Next? MCE uses a sender authentication package to configure the sending domain and branded account domains. MC Next has you add an authenticated domain , generate the required DNS records , and publish them through your DNS provider.

title: What are the steps to add an authenticated domain in MC Next?
text: What are the steps to add an authenticated domain in MC Next? Setup → Quick Find "Authenticated Domains" → Add Domain → Continue → define the subdomain → create a default From email username → download a DNS zone file or view individual DNS records → add them at your DNS provider → tick the confirmation checkbox → Activate My Domain .

title: What's the difference between an authorized email domain and an authenticated domain?
text: What's the difference between an authorized email domain and an authenticated domain? An authorized email domain verifies ownership with a simple verification record and does not provide the complete DKIM/DNS sending configuration. An authenticated domain establishes the full DKIM and DNS sending configuration. Authorized domains are required for dynamic From or Reply-to addresses .

title: What causes a DMARC alignment failure with From addresses?
text: What causes a DMARC alignment failure with From addresses? For DMARC alignment, the domain in the From address must align with the authenticated sending domain . Using a personal email address on the root domain as the From address may result in DMARC alignment failures.

title: Name the four levels of attributing consent to promotional communications.
text: Name the four levels of attributing consent to promotional communications. Level 1 = the entire individual record (all channels/subscriptions/contact points). Level 2 = a communication channel as a whole (e.g., all email). Level 3 = a specific contact point value (email/phone), regardless of subscription. Level 4 = a specific contact point and a specific subscription type.

title: Which consent level does Marketing Cloud Next enforce?
text: Which consent level does Marketing Cloud Next enforce? Level 4 — the most granular level, applying to a specific contact point (email address or phone number) and a specific subscription type.

title: Name the four objects that manage Level 4 consent and what each represents.
text: Name the four objects that manage Level 4 consent and what each represents. Communication Subscription (the type/purpose/category of communication) · Communication Subscription Channel Type (the channel used to deliver a subscription) · Communication Subscription Consent (the individual's consent status for a subscription at a specific contact point value + subscription channel type) · Engagement

title: Give a concrete example of what a Communication Subscription Consent record stores.
text: Give a concrete example of what a Communication Subscription Consent record stores. Someone at example.com opted into Marketing via email — i.e., a contact point value + subscription + channel combination.

title: What are the limitations of the consent file import?
text: What are the limitations of the consent file import? It's a manual, user-driven process; each file is limited to 50,000 rows ; each upload covers one channel , applies to one subscription , and assigns one consent status (opt-in or opt-out).

title: In which flow types is the Create Consent element available, and what is it called in each
text: In which flow types is the Create Consent element available, and what is it called in each? Available in Automation Event-Triggered Flows , On-Demand Flows , and Data Cloud-Triggered Flows . In Automation Event-Triggered and On-Demand flows it's labelled Consent Request ; in Data Cloud-Triggered flows it's Create Consent .

title: Name the four unsupported methods for updating consent.
text: Name the four unsupported methods for updating consent. Batch Data Transform , direct mapping from a data stream , bulk ingestion using the Bulk Ingestion API , and the MessagingConsentV2 flow action . They can materialize records from a DLO into the CSC DMO, but aren't supported consent management methods.

title: How long can it take for a consent record created via a data stream to materialise in the
text: How long can it take for a consent record created via a data stream to materialise in the CSC DMO? Approximately 15 minutes — records ingested through data streams aren't available in the DMO in real time.

title: Why did Salesforce build a caching layer into the consent service?
text: Why did Salesforce build a caching layer into the consent service? To provide read-after-write consistency for consent updates — so the latest consent status is immediately available rather than waiting for the DMO to refresh.

title: What is the time-to-live of a consent cache entry?
text: What is the time-to-live of a consent cache entry? 90 days , after which it expires automatically.

title: When a consent record is created through the consent service, what order do things happen
text: When a consent record is created through the consent service, what order do things happen in? The cache is updated first (making the latest status immediately available), then the record is written to the underlying DLO , and the CSC DMO is later hydrated with the updated record.

title: At send time, how does the send engine decide which consent value to use?
text: At send time, how does the send engine decide which consent value to use? It looks at the cache first . If there's no value for a contact point value, it looks at the value in the CSC DMO and then updates the cache. If a value is in the cache, it does not look at the DMO.

title: Walk through the scenario where an opt-out is ignored at send time.
text: Walk through the scenario where an opt-out is ignored at send time. 1) A consent record is created (opt-in) and materialised in the DMO via an unsupported method (e.g., direct data stream mapping). 2) An email is sent — no prior cache entry, so the cache is populated with the current (opt-in) status. 3) An opt-out record is streamed to the consent DLO — but there's no automatic cache update . 4) T

title: Why is there no automatic cache update when consent is written via a data stream mapping?
text: Why is there no automatic cache update when consent is written via a data stream mapping? Because there is currently no process that automatically updates an existing cache record when the status update is retrieved using a data stream mapping. Only supported write paths (which go through the consent service) refresh the cache.

title: How does the Create Consent element behave in a Data Cloud-Triggered Flow?
text: How does the Create Consent element behave in a Data Cloud-Triggered Flow? When a change occurs on the contact point email DMO, the flow evaluates a condition (e.g., a consent status field updated). When satisfied, it triggers the consent action. When the flow interview reaches the action, consent values are written immediately to both the cache layer and the underlying DLO — so subsequent reads r

title: Where can you use the Privacy Consent Status Lightning Web Component to trigger the consen
text: Where can you use the Privacy Consent Status Lightning Web Component to trigger the consent service? On Lead, Contact, and Personal Account records.

title: What did the Spring and Summer releases each add to preference pages?
text: What did the Spring and Summer releases each add to preference pages? Spring: introduced custom preference pages . Summer: expanded to allow multiple preference pages (e.g., separate pages per brand).

title: What can you configure when building a preference page?
text: What can you configure when building a preference page? A brand (colours, typography, buttons, spacing, borders), content blocks (dividers, headings, lists, paragraphs), layouts , and image blocks — plus designate a default preference page used across all marketing message sends.

title: How does the message channel affect which preference page is used?
text: How does the message channel affect which preference page is used? The channel automatically determines the page type: email messages link to the email preference manager ; SMS messages use a separate SMS-specific page. A unified email+SMS page isn't available out-of-the-box.

title: Name four limitations of out-of-the-box preference pages.
text: Name four limitations of out-of-the-box preference pages. No unified cross-channel page (needs custom development) · no native multilingual support (needs custom forms/development) · no custom code (AMPscript, Apex, server-side JavaScript) · can't pre-populate from URL parameters .

title: What can't you edit in the standard subscription block, and what's the workaround?
text: What can't you edit in the standard subscription block, and what's the workaround? You can't edit button labels, headings, subheadings , or the order of the subscription list . Partial workaround: rename the communication subscriptions from the Consent tab . Full text customization is planned for an upcoming release.

title: When you publish multiple preference pages, where do they appear?
text: When you publish multiple preference pages, where do they appear? In the merge field selector , so you can choose the appropriate one when adding a preference page link to a message.

title: Why is the CRM Communication Subscription Consent object a distractor?
text: Why is the CRM Communication Subscription Consent object a distractor? Because the Communication Subscription Consent object in CRM is not the same object as the Communication Subscription Consent DMO — they're different halves of the model.

title: Does the "Has Opted Out of Email" field on Lead/Contact records update consent in MC Next?
text: Does the "Has Opted Out of Email" field on Lead/Contact records update consent in MC Next? No — it does not update consent in Marketing Cloud Next. It's a common exam distractor.

title: What three areas does Session 2 cover?
text: What three areas does Session 2 cover? 1) Key Data 360 topics referenced in the exam objectives. 2) How Salesforce CRM integrates with Marketing Cloud Next. 3) The different types of marketing flows .

title: What does the exam guide recommend regarding Data 360, and is it a prerequisite?
text: What does the exam guide recommend regarding Data 360, and is it a prerequisite? It's not a prerequisite , but the exam guide recommends candidates consider earning the Salesforce Certified Data 360 Consultant certification first. Candidates are expected to have some Data 360 experience.

title: Why do you need Data 360 knowledge for the MC Next exam?
text: Why do you need Data 360 knowledge for the MC Next exam? Because Marketing Cloud Next is a Lightning app built on Data 360 — you need a solid understanding of core Data 360 concepts, though not deep expertise in every area.

title: What should you understand about the Data 360 object model?
text: What should you understand about the Data 360 object model? The role of DLOs (Data Lake Objects) and DMOs (Data Model Objects). You don't need to go deeply into unstructured data .

title: What should you understand about data streams?
text: What should you understand about data streams? How to create data streams and how data is mapped from DLOs into DMOs .

title: Name the Data 360 capabilities the exam expects you to be familiar with.
text: Name the Data 360 capabilities the exam expects you to be familiar with. Data 360 object model · data streams & DLO→DMO mapping · data spaces · data kits · calculated insights · data graphs · segmentation · activations · identity resolution .

title: Where does Salesforce recommend building your Data 360 foundation?
text: Where does Salesforce recommend building your Data 360 foundation? Trailhead — search for the Data 360 Learning Journey , a progressive multi-part learning experience.

title: How has the Data 360 dependency for audience data changed?
text: How has the Data 360 dependency for audience data changed? Earlier releases required audience/decisioning/personalization data to exist in Data 360 . Spring '26 began reducing that dependency (CRM records as an audience source); Summer '26 went further (campaign members + actionable lists).

title: What did Spring '26 add to CRM integration?
text: What did Spring '26 add to CRM integration? You can use CRM records directly as an audience source — either on a scheduled basis or based on an event .

title: What did Summer '26 add to CRM integration?
text: What did Summer '26 add to CRM integration? Support for campaign members and actionable lists .

title: What does the Sales Data Kit create, and which objects does it cover?
text: What does the Sales Data Kit create, and which objects does it cover? Pre-configured data streams and mappings for common CRM objects — leads, contacts, accounts, and prospects , plus related objects.

title: Is the Sales Data Kit required, and what happens if you skip it?
text: Is the Sales Data Kit required, and what happens if you skip it? It's optional . Skip it if you manage identity outside Salesforce or want more control over CRM data. ⚠️ If you skip it, some features (like reporting dashboards) need extra configuration , and Opportunity Influence requires it .

title: How does Flow work with CRM audiences?
text: How does Flow work with CRM audiences? You can add campaign members or CRM records on a schedule , or respond to Change Data Capture (CDC) events — such as when a CRM record is created or updated.

title: What is an actionable list?
text: What is an actionable list? A fixed (static) collection of audience members — useful when you already know exactly who you want to engage.

title: Give three examples of when to use an actionable list.
text: Give three examples of when to use an actionable list. Attendees captured at a trade show · selected leads or contacts from CRM · a curated audience that needs to be activated.

title: How do you create an actionable list from a CSV import?
text: How do you create an actionable list from a CSV import? Import → Import from File → choose the CSV → enable Add to Actionable List → select an existing list or create a new one → review field mappings → Start Import . Members then appear on the Actionable Lists tab.

title: What happens to consent when you add new leads or contacts to an actionable list?
text: What happens to consent when you add new leads or contacts to an actionable list? Marketing Cloud Next does not automatically create corresponding consent records . Those consent records must be created or loaded separately — otherwise the audience is suppressed at send time (strict opt-in).

title: How does CRM integration extend beyond audience selection?
text: How does CRM integration extend beyond audience selection? Within Flow you can perform standard operations on Salesforce records using the Get, Create, Update, and Delete Records elements.

title: What reporting capabilities combine CRM and Data 360 data?
text: What reporting capabilities combine CRM and Data 360 data? Standard Salesforce CRM reports alongside Data 360 data, including reports based on DMOs , plus analytics experiences such as the Unified Engagement History Dashboard .

title: What is the single orchestration engine for outbound messaging in MC Next, and how does th
text: What is the single orchestration engine for outbound messaging in MC Next, and how does that differ from MCE? Flow is the orchestration engine. In Marketing Cloud Engagement , messages could be sent from many tools/contexts (journeys, automations, triggered sends, UI sends, Salesforce sends, Content Builder sends). In MC Next, all outbound messaging is orchestrated through Flow .

title: What are marketing flows also called, and how do they differ from core flows?
text: What are marketing flows also called, and how do they differ from core flows? Also called high-scale flows . They run on a separate high-scale processing engine and run off-core (outside the core Salesforce transactional runtime), so traditional governor-limit, transaction-management, and scaling concerns don't apply the same way .

title: Name the six flow types in Marketing Cloud Next.
text: Name the six flow types in Marketing Cloud Next. Audience flow · Activation-triggered flow · Automation event-triggered flow · On-demand flow · Broadcast flow · Data Cloud-triggered flow .

title: What are audience flows, and what do they unify?
text: What are audience flows, and what do they unify? A Summer '26 concept that unifies several previously separate flow types into a single simplified orchestration experience — covering segments, actionable lists, CRM records, and campaign members . You choose the audience source directly in the flow configuration.

title: What Journey Builder concept do audience flow re-entry conditions mirror?
text: What Journey Builder concept do audience flow re-entry conditions mirror? Journey Builder's contact entry mode . The three options are no re-entry , re-entry at any time , and re-entry only after exiting .

title: When were activation-triggered flows introduced, and what target type do they use?
text: When were activation-triggered flows introduced, and what target type do they use? Winter '26 ; they use the Data 360 activation target type .

title: What four things can you configure when creating an activation?
text: What four things can you configure when creating an activation? Add filters to activation membership · add contact point filters · limit audience size based on attributes · append additional attributes from related objects associated with a segment member.

title: Why is the activation-as-personalization-source capability significant?
text: Why is the activation-as-personalization-source capability significant? Messages can use the activation directly as the personalization source , so email merge fields and repeaters can reference enriched Data 360 activation attributes — without additional lookups at send time .

title: What event sources can start an automation event-triggered flow?
text: What event sources can start an automation event-triggered flow? 1) Standard engagement events (email opens, clicks, form submissions — no extra config). 2) Engagement signals (custom events like website interactions, PDF downloads). 3) CRM record-triggered events (Spring '26 — prospect/lead/contact/related object created or updated).

title: When were CRM record-triggered events introduced, and what fires them?
text: When were CRM record-triggered events introduced, and what fires them? Spring '26 . They fire when a prospect, lead, contact, or any related object record is created or updated.

title: What are on-demand flows, and what makes them powerful?
text: What are on-demand flows, and what makes them powerful? They let external systems trigger transactional messaging instantly through the REST API . Real-time personalization data can be passed directly in the API payload using an Apex-defined data schema — no need to ingest or hydrate data into Data Cloud first.

title: What is the typical latency of an on-demand flow, and what is it ideal for?
text: What is the typical latency of an on-demand flow, and what is it ideal for? Approximately 1 to 3 seconds . Ideal for one-time passcodes, order confirmations, password resets, and real-time service alerts .

title: What two values are required in an on-demand flow API call, and what's the rule about the
text: What two values are required in an on-demand flow API call, and what's the rule about the individual ID? Both the email address and individual ID are required. The individual ID doesn't need to correspond to an Individual record in Data 360 — it simply cannot be null . The request won't create an Individual DMO record, but engagement still appears in the Email Engagement DMO .

title: What are broadcast flows designed for, and how do they differ from on-demand flows?
text: What are broadcast flows designed for, and how do they differ from on-demand flows? Designed for fan-out processing — a single event triggers communication to a large group simultaneously . Both use the REST API, but on-demand targets an individual while broadcast targets all members of a segment .

title: What segment type must a broadcast flow use, and when is it evaluated?
text: What segment type must a broadcast flow use, and when is it evaluated? A dynamic segment — evaluated at execution time using variables passed into the flow, allowing highly contextual audience resolution.

title: Give three use cases for broadcast flows.
text: Give three use cases for broadcast flows. Airline flight delay notifications · utility outage alerts · emergency notifications .

title: What happens when a broadcast flow API call executes?
text: What happens when a broadcast flow API call executes? 1) The flow passes the parameter values required by the dynamic segment. 2) The segment refreshes and evaluates all individuals matching both static and dynamic criteria . 3) Every qualifying member is admitted into the flow . 4) Each recipient receives the personalized message.

title: Can broadcast flows run synchronously or asynchronously?
text: Can broadcast flows run synchronously or asynchronously? Either , depending on the use case.

title: What triggers a Data Cloud-triggered flow, and how does it work under the hood?
text: What triggers a Data Cloud-triggered flow, and how does it work under the hood? It executes when a record within a Data Cloud DMO (or Calculated Insight object ) is created or updated. Data 360 monitors the DMO ; when a matching change occurs, a data action publishes a platform event that triggers the flow.

title: Is a Data Cloud-triggered flow a marketing flow?
text: Is a Data Cloud-triggered flow a marketing flow? ⚠️ Technically not — but it's still considered a high-scale flow type .

title: What is the most common use of a Data Cloud-triggered flow?
text: What is the most common use of a Data Cloud-triggered flow? Automating consent management based on DMO or Calculated Insight object record changes, using the Create Consent flow action — which updates the Communication Subscription DMO and the consent cache layer .

title: Which two flow types cannot send emails from Marketing Cloud Next?
text: Which two flow types cannot send emails from Marketing Cloud Next? Record-triggered flows (they're CRM flows) and Data Cloud-triggered (Data 360-triggered) flows .

title: What does "off-core" mean, and what does it change?
text: What does "off-core" mean, and what does it change? Marketing flows execute outside the core Salesforce transactional runtime on a separate high-scale engine. Because of this, traditional concerns around governor limits, transaction management, and scaling patterns don't apply in the same way .

title: How is personalization data supplied to on-demand and broadcast flow emails?
text: How is personalization data supplied to on-demand and broadcast flow emails? Via an Apex class data provider — an Apex wrapper class defines the variables passed in the API payload, and the email uses the Apex class data provider to personalize content from those properties.

title: What does the "Available for Input" option do on a flow variable?
text: What does the "Available for Input" option do on a flow variable? It allows external systems to pass values into the flow through an API request — required for on-demand and broadcast flow variables supplied externally.

title: What two areas does Session 3 cover?
text: What two areas does Session 3 cover? 1) How Salesforce CMS integrates with Marketing Cloud Next (business units, workspaces, content). 2) The different options for content personalization (data providers, content variables, marketing objects, and personalization methods).

title: What do business units separate in MC Next, and where is all marketing content stored?
text: What do business units separate in MC Next, and where is all marketing content stored? They separate content and data across teams, brands, or regions. All marketing content (images, landing pages, forms, brand assets, emails) is stored in CMS content workspaces .

title: What is each CMS content workspace associated with?
text: What is each CMS content workspace associated with? A specific business unit . This structure works alongside Data 360's data spaces .

title: What are the cardinalities between data spaces, business units, and content workspaces?
text: What are the cardinalities between data spaces, business units, and content workspaces? A data space can be associated with no business units or one business unit . A business unit can be associated with one or more content workspaces .

title: How does the system filter content by business unit?
text: How does the system filter content by business unit? When marketers create an asset, the system displays only the content available to the associated business unit . The same filtering applies when selecting content from a campaign or flow .

title: Can content be accessed directly across business units?
text: Can content be accessed directly across business units? ⚠️ No — by design, content cannot be accessed directly across business units. Each CMS content workspace must be associated with a specific business unit in Setup.

title: How do you share content across business units?
text: How do you share content across business units? Post content as a common asset , which makes it available to all business units . Users in other business units can then copy that asset into their own workspaces and use it locally.

title: What content access does each business unit role have?
text: What content access does each business unit role have? Marketing Standard = access to both the data space and CMS content . Marketing Read-Only = access to only the data space (no CMS content).

title: Who can only be assigned the Marketing Read-Only role?
text: Who can only be assigned the Marketing Read-Only role? Users without the Marketing Manager or Marketing Admin permission sets.

title: What can you configure from a business unit's setup page?
text: What can you configure from a business unit's setup page? Associate CMS workspaces , assign authenticated email domains and channel-specific settings, configure preference pages for each domain , enable specific AI features , add members (with roles), and enable common assets (Business Unit Settings).

title: What is a Marketing Workspace, and how can you organise assets?
text: What is a Marketing Workspace, and how can you organise assets? Where content is stored. Use the default Marketing Cloud Content Workspace or create additional workspaces to organise assets by campaign, initiative, brand, or team — and to support collaboration across teams.

title: How can content be shared between workspaces?
text: How can content be shared between workspaces? Share content between marketing workspaces , or with a general workspace used by other users. Example: manage brand assets in a marketing workspace, then share them with a general workspace so other teams can use them.

title: How do you organise and move content within/between workspaces?
text: How do you organise and move content within/between workspaces? Organise content into folders within each workspace. Export content assets and import them into another Salesforce org — e.g., moving content between production and sandbox orgs.

title: Besides business-unit-level roles, how else can access be managed?
text: Besides business-unit-level roles, how else can access be managed? By assigning roles at the individual workspace level .

title: How do you create a Marketing Workspace?
text: How do you create a Marketing Workspace? Content tab → Add Workspace → choose Marketing Workspace → enter a name and default language .

title: Which content types should you be familiar with?
text: Which content types should you be familiar with? The most commonly used: images, landing pages, forms, and emails . (MC Next supports many more, but you don't need to know all of them.)

title: After saving content, what must happen before it can be used?
text: After saving content, what must happen before it can be used? It must be published . Saving alone isn't enough.

title: Why must a form be created before a landing page?
text: Why must a form be created before a landing page? Because the form needs to exist before it can be placed on a page .

title: How do you set up a form's data source?
text: How do you set up a form's data source? Add a data source and choose the CRM object where submissions should create records (e.g., name it "leads" and select the Lead object).

title: What happens when you select "New Flow" on a form?
text: What happens when you select "New Flow" on a form? It creates a form handler . Flow Builder pre-adds a Create Records element with mappings between the form fields and the corresponding record fields (e.g., Lead).

title: What happens when you publish a form?
text: What happens when you publish a form? It also activates the associated flow .

title: What do you configure when building a landing page with a form?
text: What do you configure when building a landing page with a form? Add the published form , add other elements (e.g., a header image), configure the page title and SEO title , then save and publish . When a visitor submits the form, the flow runs and creates a new record in CRM.

title: What is the primary data source for personalization in Marketing Cloud Engagement?
text: What is the primary data source for personalization in Marketing Cloud Engagement? Data extensions — either a sendable data extension (personalization strings reference subscriber data directly) or a non-sendable one (AMPscript retrieves the required fields). There are some exceptions, but data extensions remain primary.

title: What three mechanisms does MC Next offer for personalization?
text: What three mechanisms does MC Next offer for personalization? Data providers , content variables , and marketing objects .

title: Which channel's personalization does the exam cover?
text: Which channel's personalization does the exam cover? Email content personalization only — not other channels.

title: What do merge fields do?
text: What do merge fields do? Insert a single value from the selected data source into your content — the simplest option for field-level personalization .

title: What do repeaters do?
text: What do repeaters do? Display a collection of related items (recent purchases, upcoming events, recommended products). You design one item connected to a data source, and MC Next repeats that layout for each relevant record .

title: What does dynamic content do?
text: What does dynamic content do? Changes an entire component or field based on targeting rules — the same email can show different images, offers, or messages depending on location, interests, or loyalty status. If a customer qualifies for multiple variations, you can prioritise which they see.

title: What does Handlebars provide?
text: What does Handlebars provide? A templating language that can access nested data , apply conditional logic , format values , and iterate through collections — giving developers more control over how personalized content is rendered.

title: What's the caveat about AMPscript in MC Next?
text: What's the caveat about AMPscript in MC Next? You can use it for complex personalization logic and data operations, but ⚠️ not every AMPscript function available in Marketing Cloud Engagement is supported in Marketing Cloud Next .

title: Which personalization methods are marketer-friendly vs. developer-oriented?
text: Which personalization methods are marketer-friendly vs. developer-oriented? Marketer configuration: merge fields, repeaters, dynamic content. Developer flexibility: Handlebars and AMPscript.

title: Name the eight data providers in Marketing Cloud Next.
text: Name the eight data providers in Marketing Cloud Next. 1) Data graph 2) Event 3) Activation 4) Salesforce record 5) Apex class 6) Personalization recommender 7) Lookup graph 8) Offer .

title: What is a data graph, and how does it work?
text: What is a data graph, and how does it work? A pre-assembled view combining selected fields from multiple related DMOs. It begins with a primary DMO (typically Individual or Unified Individual) and connects related objects (contact points, accounts, orders, products, engagement activity). Data 360 prepares it as a single read-only record , so MC Next retrieves customer data quickly without joining

title: What does an event data provider do, and what's its key limitation?
text: What does an event data provider do, and what's its key limitation? It makes data from an event-triggered automation flow available for content. Each event has a defined schema corresponding to the underlying engagement DMO that triggers the flow (form submissions, email sends/opens, engagement signals). ⚠️ It supports direct attributes from the event DMO, but not related collections — e.g., an or

title: What does an activation data provider do?
text: What does an activation data provider do? Makes the direct and related attributes configured in the activation available for content personalization. It supports segments based on either Individual or Unified Individual .

title: Can a message use both an activation and an event data provider?
text: Can a message use both an activation and an event data provider? ⚠️ No. Each requires a specific flow orchestration pattern, so using both would create a conflict in how the data is bound to the message .

title: What does a Salesforce record data provider do?
text: What does a Salesforce record data provider do? Lets you personalize content with current data from Salesforce CRM objects — add a case, lead, or another supported object as a data source, then insert its fields using merge fields.

title: What does an Apex class data provider do, and what is it designed for?
text: What does an Apex class data provider do, and what is it designed for? It defines a custom data structure for personalization — the Apex class primarily defines the schema (fields and data types) that content can reference. It's designed for on-demand or broadcast flows passing data into an email, but can be used with other flow types.

title: What does a personalization recommender do?
text: What does a personalization recommender do? Brings recommendations from Salesforce Personalization into an email — returning a collection of relevant products, services, or content per recipient, displayed using a Repeater component.

title: What does a lookup graph data provider do?
text: What does a lookup graph data provider do? Provides access to non-profile data that doesn't have a direct relationship back to a unified individual. It takes a value from the recipient's primary data graph and uses it as a key to retrieve matching information from a second, smaller data graph (e.g., a product identifier → product details from a catalog graph). Results display in merge fields or re

title: What does the offer data provider do?
text: What does the offer data provider do? Works with Salesforce Loyalty Management to deliver tailored promotions in email content. Use merge fields for offer name/description/coupon code, and dynamic content rules to show different offers by customer attribute (e.g., loyalty tier).

title: What are content variables, and how do they differ from a data graph?
text: What are content variables, and how do they differ from a data graph? Custom placeholders defined within an email and populated at runtime from Salesforce Flow . Unlike a data graph, they don't retrieve data from predefined customer data structures — the email defines what it expects (order number, appointment date, discount amount, support rep's name) and the flow supplies the values at send time

title: What can a content variable be mapped to?
text: What can a content variable be mapped to? Any data source available to Salesforce Flow — including Salesforce data, MuleSoft integrations, and HTTP connectors. Useful when information is calculated during the flow or comes from a system outside Data 360 .

title: What data types do content variables support?
text: What data types do content variables support? Boolean, Text, Date, DateTime, and Number — plus a Record ID value that references a Salesforce record.

title: In simple terms, how do content variables work?
text: In simple terms, how do content variables work? The content defines the placeholders , and the flow supplies their values at send time .

title: What is a marketing object, and what's the MCE comparison?
text: What is a marketing object, and what's the MCE comparison? A flexible data store in MC Next holding information for marketing use cases. The closest MCE comparison is a data extension .

title: What are marketing objects useful for storing?
text: What are marketing objects useful for storing? Product catalogs, reference tables, rewards balances, promotional codes, and more.

title: Why do marketing objects give marketers autonomy?
text: Why do marketing objects give marketers autonomy? Because an admin doesn't need to create a Salesforce object or modify the Data 360 data model — a marketer creates one by importing a CSV, defining fields, and identifying a primary key.

title: How do you use marketing object data in a message?
text: How do you use marketing object data in a message? Query the marketing object with Handlebars or AMPscript . Example: use the recipient's address from the default data graph to find their matching record in a marketing object and retrieve their current rewards balance.

title: What field types do marketing objects support, and how is data refreshed?
text: What field types do marketing objects support, and how is data refreshed? Text, number, and decimal fields. Data can be fully refreshed by uploading a new CSV file, which replaces existing records .

title: In summary, what is a marketing object?
text: In summary, what is a marketing object? A marketer-managed table of data that can be queried at runtime to personalize content.

title: How do you create a marketing object?
text: How do you create a marketing object? From the Data Management tab in the Marketing app → New → upload a CSV → Next → give it a name → review the fields and data types detected from the file (adjust if needed) → select the primary key field → done.

title: What can you define when inserting a merge field?
text: What can you define when inserting a merge field? A fallback value to use when the customer's data is missing (e.g., "Friend" when the first name is absent). The merge field menu shows the configured data providers alongside options like global strings .

title: What two levels of personalization does the back-in-stock demo illustrate?
text: What two levels of personalization does the back-in-stock demo illustrate? Merge fields provide a simple, marketer-friendly way to insert data; Handlebars and AMPscript give more control over how data is retrieved and formatted (e.g., converting a name to uppercase, formatting a price as currency).

title: What does dynamic content require?
text: What does dynamic content require? A data graph configured as a data source.

title: Walk through the US West States variation demo.
text: Walk through the US West States variation demo. Select the header image → in the dynamic content section of the image properties panel click New Variation → name it → define the targeting rule by selecting the State/Province field from the individual's related contact point address data → choose the isIn operator → enter the state values → save → assign a different header image. You can preview ea

title: What three areas does the final session cover?
text: What three areas does the final session cover? 1) How contact point resolution works at send time. 2) Agentforce and other AI-powered innovations . 3) Analytics and performance insight reports and dashboards.

title: How does the contact point model differ between MCE and Data 360?
text: How does the contact point model differ between MCE and Data 360? MCE subscribers can only have one email address . In Data 360, an individual can have multiple email addresses , plus multiple contact point values for other channels like SMS.

title: Do reconciliation rules determine which contact point is used?
text: Do reconciliation rules determine which contact point is used? ⚠️ No. Reconciliation rules determine which single value is selected for a unified field that can't contain multiple values (like an individual's name). They don't apply to contact points such as email addresses or phone numbers.

title: What happens to all contact points after identity resolution?
text: What happens to all contact points after identity resolution? They are all retained as part of the unified profile and remain available for segmentation and activation .

title: If a unified individual has records with three email addresses, two of which are the same,
text: If a unified individual has records with three email addresses, two of which are the same, how many emails are sent? Two — a separate message is sent to each unique email address , and a duplicate address is treated as a single contact point (one send).

title: Name the four ways MC Next determines which contact point to use at send time.
text: Name the four ways MC Next determines which contact point to use at send time. 1) Data graph selected in the flow's automation properties. 2) On-demand flow API payload . 3) Activation source priority order (activation-triggered flows). 4) Activation template (audience flows using a segment).

title: What must the flow's data graph include for contact point selection to work?
text: What must the flow's data graph include for contact point selection to work? A specific structure and field set — otherwise messages won't send successfully. (The required structure is documented on a Salesforce Help page.)

title: In an on-demand flow, what takes precedence — the API payload or a configured data graph?
text: In an on-demand flow, what takes precedence — the API payload or a configured data graph? The contact point is typically derived from the API payload , but if a data graph is configured in the flow's automation properties, that data graph takes precedence .

title: What is an activation template?
text: What is an activation template? A template that lets you define the source priority order and use rules to filter the segment members or contact points included in an activation. You select it when configuring a send message element in a flow.

title: When is an activation template required?
text: When is an activation template required? When the segment's segment-on object is NOT Unified Individual .

title: Walk through creating an activation template.
text: Walk through creating an activation template. Activations tab in Data 360 → New → select Template as the activation type → Continue → select a data space and the DMO used as the segment-on criteria (typically Individual or Unified Individual) → choose Data Cloud as the platform → Continue → define the priority order for contact point selection (expand the email channel → Edit ) → Save → optionally

title: In the demo, what source priority order was configured, and what's the result?
text: In the demo, what source priority order was configured, and what's the result? Salesforce → Contact , then Salesforce → Lead , then Any (all other sources). MC Next prioritises an email from a Contact record; if unavailable, a Lead record; then any other source .

title: Which DMO holds the telephone number field for phone contact point selection?
text: Which DMO holds the telephone number field for phone contact point selection? The Contact Point Phone DMO — not the Individual or Unified Individual DMO.

title: Name the five out-of-the-box AI agents in Marketing Cloud Next.
text: Name the five out-of-the-box AI agents in Marketing Cloud Next. Segment Creation Agent , Campaign Creation Agent , Content Creation Agent , Journey Decisioning Agent , and Account Discovery Agent .

title: What does the Segment Creation Agent do?
text: What does the Segment Creation Agent do? Uses natural language prompts to create Data 360 audience segments — translating an audience description into editable segmentation criteria .

title: What does the Campaign Creation Agent do?
text: What does the Campaign Creation Agent do? Creates campaign briefs, flows, and multi-channel content from conversational prompts — accelerating campaign planning and development.

title: What does the Content Creation Agent do?
text: What does the Content Creation Agent do? Drafts and refines content for emails, landing pages, and SMS messages — adjusting messaging, tone, length, or audience relevance.

title: What does the Journey Decisioning Agent do?
text: What does the Journey Decisioning Agent do? Selects the most appropriate journey or flow and creates personalized content for each individual.

title: What does the Account Discovery Agent do?
text: What does the Account Discovery Agent do? Provides account insights and identifies potential buying group members — helping discover stakeholders and guide nurturing or follow-up activities.

title: Walk through the "Draft with Agentforce" campaign flow.
text: Walk through the "Draft with Agentforce" campaign flow. Marketing Home → New Campaign → Draft with Agentforce → describe the campaign objective → choose to draft a brief → ask Agentforce to generate a campaign → Agentforce creates a draft campaign brief → open the campaign preview (flow + content) → save as a new campaign → open the campaign record.

title: How does Einstein Segment Creation fit into the campaign demo?
text: How does Einstein Segment Creation fit into the campaign demo? Select Segment → Segment Builder → Next → Create with Einstein Segment Creation → choose the DMO → Next . Einstein has already drafted an audience definition based on the campaign objective ; you can refine it or edit rules manually, then Create Segment .

title: Name the three predictive AI capabilities in MC Next, and which are Advanced-only?
text: Name the three predictive AI capabilities in MC Next, and which are Advanced-only? Engagement Frequency , Engagement Scoring , and Send Time Optimization . ⚠️ Engagement Frequency and Engagement Scoring are Advanced only — not Growth.

title: How do you use predictive AI insights for segmentation and decisioning?
text: How do you use predictive AI insights for segmentation and decisioning? Configure the required data graph first, then use fields like Email Engagement Frequency or Engagement Score to create branches with a Decision element — or use those DMO fields as segment criteria .

title: What is the goal of Engagement Frequency?
text: What is the goal of Engagement Frequency? To determine how often each contact should receive an email — maximising engagement while reducing email fatigue and unsubscribes .

title: What does Engagement Frequency analyse, and how is it trained?
