text: What does Engagement Frequency analyse, and how is it trained? Up to 90 days of email activity — sends, opens, clicks, bounces, unsubscribes, spam complaints, and sending patterns . It compares each individual's behaviour at different frequencies with similar individuals , then calculates an ideal frequency range . ⚠️ Trained only on your org's data ; scores refreshed weekly .

title: What are the four Engagement Frequency classifications?
text: What are the four Engagement Frequency classifications? The Email Engagement Classification field in the Email Engagement Frequency DMO assigns each individual to: Saturated · Almost Saturated · On Target · Under Saturated .

title: What does Engagement Scoring estimate?
text: What does Engagement Scoring estimate? How likely each individual is to engage with future marketing communications .

title: What does Engagement Scoring analyse?
text: What does Engagement Scoring analyse? Up to 90 days of historical behaviour, placing greater emphasis on the most recent activity — email sends, opens, clicks, bounces, unsubscribes, subscription history , and website interactions .

title: What three likelihood predictions does Engagement Scoring generate?
text: What three likelihood predictions does Engagement Scoring generate? Likelihood to open an email, likelihood to click a link, and likelihood to remain subscribed .

title: Name the four Engagement Scoring personas and their open/click likelihoods.
text: Name the four Engagement Scoring personas and their open/click likelihoods. Loyalists (high open, high click) · Selective Subscribers (low open, high click) · Window Shoppers (high open, low click) · Win Back / Dormant (low open, low click).

title: How might you use the Engagement Scoring personas?
text: How might you use the Engagement Scoring personas? Send surveys to understand selective subscribers, engage window shoppers via alternative channels , and place dormant subscribers into a dedicated win-back campaign .

title: What four tiers are the likelihood predictions grouped into?
text: What four tiers are the likelihood predictions grouped into? Most Likely · More Likely · Less Likely · Least Likely — usable in a Decision element to route individuals along different flow paths.

title: What does Send Time Optimization do?
text: What does Send Time Optimization do? Determines when each individual is most likely to engage with an email — rather than sending to everyone at the same time.

title: What does STO analyse, and how often are predictions updated?
text: What does STO analyse, and how often are predictions updated? Up to 90 days of email engagement history — sends, opens, clicks, bounces, unsubscribes, spam complaints, plus the timestamps of those events. Predictions update approximately once a week .

title: Which editions support STO, and what setup is required?
text: Which editions support STO, and what setup is required? Both Growth and Advanced editions, and it must be enabled in Setup . Add the Send Time Optimization DMO to your data graph (required structure), then select the Hourly Scores by Week field.

title: What is the STO optimization window range?
text: What is the STO optimization window range? From 2 hours up to 1 week . MC Next sends each message at the recipient's predicted optimal time within that window.

title: Name the three out-of-the-box reporting capabilities and what each provides.
text: Name the three out-of-the-box reporting capabilities and what each provides. Campaign Performance Dashboard (end-to-end view of an individual campaign — sends, opens, clicks, bounces, contact progression) · Marketing Performance Dashboard (broader cross-channel view over time — audience growth, program-level engagement trends) · Semantic Data Model (consistent business layer for custom reports, st

title: Where are marketing performance dashboards available, and what do they show?
text: Where are marketing performance dashboards available, and what do they show? From the Marketing Analytics tab . They give a consolidated view across marketing activities — overall campaign engagement and top-performing campaigns, audience segments, content, and channels — bringing together web, email, SMS, WhatsApp, and mobile .

title: Where else do the performance dashboards appear?
text: Where else do the performance dashboards appear? Embedded directly in each campaign record , so you can evaluate an individual campaign's results in context without navigating to a separate reporting tab.

title: How do you access content performance dashboards?
text: How do you access content performance dashboards? Select the corresponding element in your active flow (e.g., a Send Email Message element) → from the Analytics tab click Details → review pulse card metrics for the content type plus row-level data .

title: What do the deliverability dashboards cover, and what are they for?
text: What do the deliverability dashboards cover, and what are they for? SMS, WhatsApp, and mobile app messaging . They provide visibility into message delivery health and campaign performance, and help you understand why a message failed to reach specific recipients .

title: What is the semantic data model, and what does it do?
text: What is the semantic data model, and what does it do? Powered by Tableau Next , it's the foundation for reports and dashboards in MC Next, available from the Analytics tab . The Marketing Intelligence Semantic Data Model combines data from multiple Data 360 objects and defines the relationships and metrics for campaign performance, engagement, and deliverability — applied centrally so metrics calc

title: What can you do with the semantic data model?
text: What can you do with the semantic data model? Create reports answering specific business questions, combine them as widgets in a dashboard , customise standard dashboards (widgets, labels, layouts, filters), extend it to other Data 360 objects, build custom reports , share data with stakeholders outside Salesforce CRM , or connect any external tool .

title: What is the Unified Engagement History dashboard?
text: What is the Unified Engagement History dashboard? A pre-built dashboard giving sales and marketing teams a shared view of activities performed by the leads and contacts associated with an account . Sales reps use it to identify the most engaged people , understand their interests, and decide who to contact next . Powered by Data 360 and Tableau Next .

title: How do you embed the Unified Engagement History dashboard?
text: How do you embed the Unified Engagement History dashboard? Add the Unified Engagement History dashboard component to the page layout of account, lead, and contact records.

title: What did the masterclass series say about scope?
text: What did the masterclass series say about scope? The purpose wasn't to cover every feature — it focused on the concepts and capabilities in the exam guide . Topics not covered include scoring rules, convergent features with MCE, RCS and WhatsApp channels, retail triggers, Einstein Metrics Guard, and distributed marketing.

title: How do match rules vs. match criteria affect consolidation rate?
text: How do match rules vs. match criteria affect consolidation rate? More match rules = higher consolidation (more match opportunities); more criteria per rule = lower consolidation (harder to match).

title: Name the five match methods.
text: Name the five match methods. Exact, Exact Normalized, Fuzzy - High Precision, Fuzzy - Medium Precision, Fuzzy - Low Precision.

title: What AI model powers fuzzy matching, and what's its confidence threshold?
text: What AI model powers fuzzy matching, and what's its confidence threshold? BERT language model trained on 150+ countries, 3B English words, 20M names; 0.7 confidence threshold.

title: How does real-time matching differ from scheduled matching?
text: How does real-time matching differ from scheduled matching? In real-time, all criteria except phone/email run Exact; phone and email run Exact Normalized (unless Exact was the scheduled method).

title: What's the risk of Match on Blank, and when is it ignored?
text: What's the risk of Match on Blank, and when is it ignored? Can cause overmatching (e.g., middle name) and the "matched 50,000+ profiles" error; it's ignored in real-time matching.

title: Why isn't matching on a single contact point recommended?
text: Why isn't matching on a single contact point recommended? It can mix household members sharing an email/phone into a single unified profile (except unique external identifiers like party ID).

title: What are the four default match rules for individuals?
text: What are the four default match rules for individuals? Fuzzy Name + Normalized Email; Fuzzy Name + Normalized Phone; Fuzzy Name + Normalized Address; Fuzzy Name + Normalized Phone + Normalized Email.

title: How many match rules can a household ruleset have?
text: How many match rules can a household ruleset have? Only one. Recommended: last name + address, or party identifier.

title: When is a unified profile considered known vs anonymous?
text: When is a unified profile considered known vs anonymous? Known if any source profile was designated known; anonymous if only anonymous sources. Account profiles are always known.

title: What are the three reconciliation rule types?
text: What are the three reconciliation rule types? Last Updated, Most Frequent, Source Priority.

title: Do reconciliation rules apply to contact points?
text: Do reconciliation rules apply to contact points? No — they only reconcile Unified Individual object fields. Use source priority order in activations to deliver contact points.

title: Which reconciliation rule should you use on ID fields, and why?
text: Which reconciliation rule should you use on ID fields, and why? Source Priority — to stabilize ID values.

title: Does ingesting via the internal Salesforce connector consume credits?
text: Does ingesting via the internal Salesforce connector consume credits? No — free as of Aug 7, 2025 (included with Data 360). External ingestion consumes credits.

title: When does Activate DMO - Streaming double the records processed?
text: When does Activate DMO - Streaming double the records processed? When a data graph is used with the activation (1 record change = 2 records processed).

title: When does a Batch Calculated Insight charge credits?
text: When does a Batch Calculated Insight charge credits? Only when underlying objects change; no charge if no changes. Objects used multiple times counted once.

title: How is Batch Profile Unification billed after the first run?
text: How is Batch Profile Unification billed after the first run? Only new or modified source profiles count (deleted or suppressed profiles count as modified).

title: What's the minimum credit decrement per usage type?
text: What's the minimum credit decrement per usage type? 1 credit, where fractional usage amounts to 1+ credits over the monthly billing period.

title: In which flow type is the Create Consent element available?
text: In which flow type is the Create Consent element available? Automation Event-Triggered flows only (per the marketing flow elements table).

title: What edition + add-on do Path Experiments require?
text: What edition + add-on do Path Experiments require? Advanced edition + Personalization.

title: Which edition supports On-Canvas Insights?
text: Which edition supports On-Canvas Insights? Advanced only.

title: Is a paused flow considered active?
text: Is a paused flow considered active? Yes — a paused flow counts as active, so only one version can be active.

title: Which activation target type do activation-triggered flows support?
text: Which activation target type do activation-triggered flows support? Only Data 360 activation target type; other target types error on save.

title: What's the concurrency limit for Marketing Cloud/Data 360 activation-triggered flows?
text: What's the concurrency limit for Marketing Cloud/Data 360 activation-triggered flows? 15,000,000 actions/hour with 210 concurrent threads.

title: What error-rate threshold triggers additional rate limiting?
text: What error-rate threshold triggers additional rate limiting? Elements failing more than 2.5% of the time.

title: What allowance do real-time-response flows get?
text: What allowance do real-time-response flows get? 50% additional allowance to the concurrency limit (e.g., 210 → 315).

title: What are the four audience sources for an audience flow?
text: What are the four audience sources for an audience flow? Segment, List, Record, Campaign.

title: What type of segment do broadcast flows use?
text: What type of segment do broadcast flows use? Dynamic segments — membership is determined after the flow starts.

title: What category of DMO can be used for engagement signals?
text: What category of DMO can be used for engagement signals? Only DMOs categorized as Engagement.

title: What are the four identifier types in an engagement signal?
text: What are the four identifier types in an engagement signal? User Identifier, Timestamp Identifier, Item Identifier, Event Identifier.

title: What happens to flow sharing when a campaign is deleted?
text: What happens to flow sharing when a campaign is deleted? Sharing reverts to the flow's own rules; if none, the flow becomes private (owner, admins, View All Non-Setup Flows/Manage Flow only).

title: What's the REST endpoint to run an autolaunched flow?
text: What's the REST endpoint to run an autolaunched flow? POST /services/data/v65.0/actions/custom/flow/FLOW API NAME

title: What's the difference between Invocable.Action and Flow.Interview in Apex?
text: What's the difference between Invocable.Action and Flow.Interview in Apex? Invocable.Action = dynamic reference + bulkification; Flow.Interview = static reference (referential integrity) but no bulkification.

title: Which flow version does REST run vs. Apex-as-admin?
text: Which flow version does REST run vs. Apex-as-admin? REST runs the active version; Apex as flow admin runs the latest version regardless of activation.

title: What's the limit of associated journeys per Campaign?
text: What's the limit of associated journeys per Campaign? 20 journeys per Campaign.

title: What journey modes are required to connect to a Campaign?
text: What journey modes are required to connect to a Campaign? Draft, Running, Finishing, Paused, or Stopped.

title: Which flows don't appear on the Marketing Calendar?
text: Which flows don't appear on the Marketing Calendar? Event/form-triggered flows (no start date).

title: What three admin roles are involved in Marketing Cloud Next setup?
text: What three admin roles are involved in Marketing Cloud Next setup? Salesforce admin (System Administrator profile), Data Cloud admin (installs data kits, deploys streams, configures identity resolution & scoring), and Marketing admin (Marketing Cloud Admin permission set).

title: What makes Marketing Cloud Next fundamentally different from legacy email tools?
text: What makes Marketing Cloud Next fundamentally different from legacy email tools? It's built natively on Data Cloud , so data unification, identity, segments, and AI all depend on the Data Cloud foundation.

title: What two things must be enabled before accessing required/additional setup settings?
text: What two things must be enabled before accessing required/additional setup settings? Enable Data Cloud and enable Marketing Cloud Next in Basic Settings.

title: What is a data kit, and what does installing one trigger?
text: What is a data kit, and what does installing one trigger? A pre-built package of DMOs, fields, and data connections. Installing auto-deploys its related data streams in Data Cloud.

title: Which data kits are always required regardless of channel add-ons?
text: Which data kits are always required regardless of channel add-ons? Marketing Setup Objects, Consent Objects, Flows Integration, Email Channel, and Sales (accounts/leads/contacts). SMS/WhatsApp kits only for those add-ons.

title: What does an identity resolution ruleset do?
text: What does an identity resolution ruleset do? Defines relationships among DMOs/fields so Data Cloud unifies related/duplicate records into Unified Individual records for targeting.

title: What three match rules are in a generated Individual ruleset?
text: What three match rules are in a generated Individual ruleset? Normalized Email, Lead to Contact, and Device to Known.

title: Why does Salesforce recommend one ruleset per object?
text: Why does Salesforce recommend one ruleset per object? Identity resolution consumes Data Cloud credits; two active rulesets per object doubles billing.

title: What's the key difference between Marketing Cloud Admin and Marketing Cloud Manager?
text: What's the key difference between Marketing Cloud Admin and Marketing Cloud Manager? Admin gets Salesforce Setup access; Manager gets full control on campaigns/segments/flows but no full Setup access.

title: Which CMS content role can manage users and sharing?
text: Which CMS content role can manage users and sharing? Content Admin (also creates/publishes all content and assigns default brand).

title: What two permission sets must an Identity-licensed marketing user receive?
text: What two permission sets must an Identity-licensed marketing user receive? Marketing Cloud Manager + Tableau Next Included App Business User.

title: What three things are required to send email?
text: What three things are required to send email? Authenticate a sending domain, verify a From address, and provide a physical address.

title: What do DKIM, SPF, and DMARC each do?
text: What do DKIM, SPF, and DMARC each do? DKIM adds a digital signature; SPF verifies the sending server is authorized; DMARC tells receivers how to handle failures.

title: What triggers auto-unsubscribe in Reply Mail Management?
text: What triggers auto-unsubscribe in Reply Mail Management? A manual reply containing unsub/unsubscribe/opt-out/remove/stop in the first 200 characters.

title: What three requests are needed for a 10-digit US long code?
text: What three requests are needed for a 10-digit US long code? Brand Request, Campaign Request, and Code Request.

title: Which channels are NOT supported in Government Cloud?
text: Which channels are NOT supported in Government Cloud? SMS, WhatsApp, and Mobile App Messaging.

title: What does a single consent import correspond to, and what can't it do?
text: What does a single consent import correspond to, and what can't it do? One channel + one subscription + one status. It can't create new leads/contacts — only updates existing contact points.

title: What phone format is required for SMS/WhatsApp consent imports?
text: What phone format is required for SMS/WhatsApp consent imports? ITU E.164 with country code, e.g. +12065550123.

title: What four activities does web tracking track?
text: What four activities does web tracking track? Page views, form submissions, link clicks, button clicks.

title: What cookie stores the tracking consent decision?
text: What cookie stores the tracking consent decision? sfmc consent (True = opted in, False = opted out/ignored).

title: What are the three score types?
text: What are the three score types? Engagement Score, Fit Score, and Overall Marketing Score (normalized 0–100).

title: How must attribute values be entered in scoring rules?
text: How must attribute values be entered in scoring rules? Exact, case-sensitive — e.g. "UNSUBSCRIBE" not "unsubscribe".

title: Which edition supports account scoring?
text: Which edition supports account scoring? Advanced edition only.

title: Which three Einstein features are Advanced edition only?
text: Which three Einstein features are Advanced edition only? Engagement Scoring, Engagement Frequency, and (partially) Send Time Optimization global model opt-out.

title: Does a low or high Metrics Guard score indicate a real click?
text: Does a low or high Metrics Guard score indicate a real click? Low score = higher confidence it's real (high = machine-generated).

title: Which objects deploy first from sandbox to production?
text: Which objects deploy first from sandbox to production? Data Cloud objects first (segments, DMOs, data graphs, calculated insights), then Marketing Cloud Next objects.

title: What does the sandbox email blackhole do?
text: What does the sandbox email blackhole do? Prevents test emails reaching real customer addresses (with up to 5 allowed domains); doesn't suppress Preview/Test or Debug flow sends.

title: How many active flows do Growth vs. Advanced allow?
text: How many active flows do Growth vs. Advanced allow? Growth 500, Advanced 750.

title: What's the difference between contact point selection and source priority order ?
text: What's the difference between contact point selection and source priority order ? Selection = which objects/fields (email, phone, MAID…) are included in an activation; source priority = which value wins when a contact has that data from multiple sources.

title: Why can't reconciliation rules determine which contact point to deliver?
text: Why can't reconciliation rules determine which contact point to deliver? Reconciliation rules only reconcile Unified Individual object fields — NOT unified contact point objects. Source priority controls contact-point delivery.

title: What do "Primary", "Personal", and "Business" priority values depend on?
text: What do "Primary", "Personal", and "Business" priority values depend on? Primary = Primary Flag mapped in Data Streams; Personal = For Personal Use field = 1; Business = For Business Use field = 1 (Any = no Primary Flag mapped).

title: What happens when you remove "Any Source/Any Type" from source priority?
text: What happens when you remove "Any Source/Any Type" from source priority? The activation uses only specific sources, so the population count drops (fewer sources = fewer matches).

title: Which platforms have a fixed (unchangeable) default source priority order?
text: Which platforms have a fixed (unchangeable) default source priority order? B2C Commerce Cloud and MobilePush (MC Engagement → Primary).

title: Which activation targets accept the Email Address contact point?
text: Which activation targets accept the Email Address contact point? Cloud File Storage, External Platform, Marketing Cloud Personalization, and Marketing Cloud Engagement.

title: What are the three functional subdomains and their inbound purpose?
text: What are the three functional subdomains and their inbound purpose? reply (reply handling), bounce (bounce notifications), leave (unsubscribe requests) — each needs a CNAME to …inbound.[tenant].mx.salesforce.com .

title: Why is applying p=reject DMARC at the root domain risky?
text: Why is applying p=reject DMARC at the root domain risky? It affects ALL corporate email from that domain; misconfiguration can fail legitimate mail — coordinate with IT.

title: How does Marketing Cloud Next handle shared vs. dedicated IPs?
text: How does Marketing Cloud Next handle shared vs. dedicated IPs? Starts on shared IPs; automatically assigns dedicated IPs based on volume; continuously rebalances traffic across pools based on volume and delivery trends (managed — no manual IP management).

title: Why must you warm your domain even though IPs are managed automatically?
text: Why must you warm your domain even though IPs are managed automatically? Major mailbox providers now use domain reputation as the PRIMARY sender-reputation signal (IP reputation is a fallback for unknown domains).

title: What's the recommended starting volume for a brand-new sending domain?
text: What's the recommended starting volume for a brand-new sending domain? No more than a few hundred emails per day, using a slow, methodical approach.

title: What's the daily max volume on days 1–3 of the warming schedule?
text: What's the daily max volume on days 1–3 of the warming schedule? 500 emails (then 1,000 on days 4–5, 1,500 day 6, 2,000 day 7, 2,500 day 8).

title: What are the bounce-rate and complaint-rate targets?
text: What are the bounce-rate and complaint-rate targets? Bounce rate < 2%; complaint rate < 0.1%.

title: What are the two spam-trap types and what does each signal?
text: What are the two spam-trap types and what does each signal? Honeypot (created to catch spammers → opt-in/purchased-data issues) vs. Recycled (reused after 6–12 months inactivity → list hygiene issues).

title: What three things does one-click List-Unsubscribe require?
text: What three things does one-click List-Unsubscribe require? List-Unsubscribe + List-Unsubscribe-Post headers, HTTPS, and a DKIM signature.

title: What DKIM key size does Marketing Cloud Next use by default, and which records carry it?
text: What DKIM key size does Marketing Cloud Next use by default, and which records carry it? 2048-bit keys, carried by the 3 outbound CNAME records (s1/s2/s3-e360).

title: Is DMARC required to activate a domain in Marketing Cloud Next?
text: Is DMARC required to activate a domain in Marketing Cloud Next? No — recommended but not required to activate; however, it IS required for bulk senders (Gmail/Yahoo). Related - marketing-cloud-next-overview - data-kits-and-data-streams - identity-resolution-rulesets - scoring-models - ai-features - sandbox-and-deployment

title: What is a data source in Marketing Cloud Next, and where do you manage them?
text: What is a data source in Marketing Cloud Next, and where do you manage them? An object or element from your org that contains fields and data; its attributes become available for merge fields, expressions, repeaters, and dynamic content. Managed in the Data Sources tab of Content Builder.

title: What must you do if you change a data source after its attributes are used in merge fields
text: What must you do if you change a data source after its attributes are used in merge fields? Delete those merge fields, add the new data source, then recreate the merge fields.

title: What is a data graph, and what's it usually based on for personalization?
text: What is a data graph, and what's it usually based on for personalization? A Data 360 object built from a primary DMO plus related objects, flattened into a streamlined table. For personalization it's usually a profile data graph based on the Unified Individual DMO.

title: What's the trade-off between standard and real-time data graphs?
text: What's the trade-off between standard and real-time data graphs? Real-time graphs provide faster response times but cost more.

title: When can't you remove or replace a data graph?
text: When can't you remove or replace a data graph? If an email has dynamic content variations or a Personalization recommender; or when a landing page content block is published. For landing pages, use a real-time graph for better performance.

title: How do SMS and WhatsApp messages use the data graph?
text: How do SMS and WhatsApp messages use the data graph? Only the default data graph is available; it doesn't appear in the Data Sources panel, but its data still works in merge fields.

title: What happens if you delete the default data graph, and what's the only personalization opt
text: What happens if you delete the default data graph, and what's the only personalization option in Starter/Pro Suite emails? The Unified Individual DMO data provider is the fallback. In Starter and Pro Suite emails, merge fields can only refer to the Unified Individual DMO.

title: What are the limits of an Event data source?
text: What are the limits of an Event data source? Max 1 event data source per content item; repeaters don't support custom event data in emails; once published you can't remove or replace it.

title: What does an Offer data source do, and what's its limit?
text: What does an Offer data source do, and what's its limit? Delivers tailored promotions in email (name, description, coupon code) with dynamic content rules by attribute (e.g., loyalty tier). Max 5 offer data providers per email.

title: What rules govern Personalization Recommender data sources?
text: What rules govern Personalization Recommender data sources? Only trained recommenders based on the same data graph as the email are selectable; needs a training period with at least one successful refresh; you can replace but not remove them; data works only in a repeater and its merge fields.

title: What data types do content variables support?
text: What data types do content variables support? Boolean, string, date, date time, number, and recordId (references a Salesforce record). Mapped to any Flow data source including MuleSoft and HTTP connectors.

title: What are the rules for Lookup Data Graph data sources?
text: What are the rules for Lookup Data Graph data sources? Uses non-profile Data 360 data (e.g., product catalog) to complement the default graph; requires a primary key; can't be nested under other lookup providers; max 5 per content item.

title: What can an Apex Class data source do, and what's its limit?
text: What can an Apex Class data source do, and what's its limit? Passes data from a flow directly into content — simple parameters or complex structured data (order collections). One Apex class data source per message.

title: What does the Activation data source do, and what's its limit?
text: What does the Activation data source do, and what's its limit? References a Data 360 segmentation activation, making segment attributes available in email merge fields for real-time audience targeting. One activation data source per message.

title: Which data sources are available only on landing pages and forms?
text: Which data sources are available only on landing pages and forms? Marketing Object and Prospect (both via the read data provider).

title: Where can you add merge fields in an email?
text: Where can you add merge fields in an email? In the subject line and preheader (Add Merge Field), or in the text of content via the Add Merge Field icon in the editing toolbar.

title: What is a saved expression, and where is it stored?
text: What is a saved expression, and where is it stored? Saved filter and sort criteria across related data objects that select the right attribute for a merge field. Stored in Salesforce CMS; reusable in email, SMS, and WhatsApp.

title: What permissions are needed to create vs. publish an expression?
text: What permissions are needed to create vs. publish an expression? Create/edit: Marketing Cloud Manager permission set + any CMS workspace contributor role. Publish/unpublish: Marketing Cloud Manager + a CMS workspace contributor role of content admin or content manager.

title: What must be set up before you can create an expression?
text: What must be set up before you can create an expression? A data graph.

title: What is a personalization point?
text: What is a personalization point? A content element eligible for a personalization decision (subject line, preheader, image component). Configuring the first variation auto-creates one for that component/field.

title: What's the difference between a personalization decision and a targeting rule?
text: What's the difference between a personalization decision and a targeting rule? A decision determines who's eligible for a response based on targeting rules (each variation relates to a decision with the same name). A targeting rule defines the conditions for showing a specific variation.

title: What are the limits for personalization points and variations?
text: What are the limits for personalization points and variations? 25 personalization points per email/landing page; 15 variations per component. Subject line + preheader count as one component.

title: What's the difference between "All Conditions Are Met" and "Any Conditions Are Met"?
text: What's the difference between "All Conditions Are Met" and "Any Conditions Are Met"? All = recipient must meet every condition; Any = recipient meets at least one condition.

title: Can you change the priority of the default variation?
text: Can you change the priority of the default variation? No — the default variation's priority can't be changed; it shows when a recipient doesn't qualify for any personalized variation.

title: What's the difference between cloning and linking a personalization point?
text: What's the difference between cloning and linking a personalization point? Cloning creates a separate copy with its own rules/settings; linking shares one point so changes apply to all linked components. Linking requires the point to already exist in the content item and the component to have no variations.

title: What happens when you add, delete, or edit a variation on a linked component?
text: What happens when you add, delete, or edit a variation on a linked component? Adding a variation adds it to all linked components; deleting removes it everywhere; editing targeting rules or priorities applies to all linked components. Content and style edits stay independent.

title: What happens when you unlink a component from a personalization point?
text: What happens when you unlink a component from a personalization point? The personalization point is cloned (e.g., "Copy of Personalization Point A") so the component keeps its targeting rules, priorities, variations, content, and style, but becomes independent. Other components stay linked to the original.

title: Can you export or import content that contains variations?
text: Can you export or import content that contains variations? No — content with variations can't be exported or imported.

title: What happens if a repeater source has no data for a recipient?
text: What happens if a repeater source has no data for a recipient? The repeater appears empty when that recipient opens the email.

title: What happens if you change a repeater layout when it contains content or data?
text: What happens if you change a repeater layout when it contains content or data? The content, data, and any style settings within the repeater get removed.

title: What must you do if you change a repeater source after its attributes are used in merge fi
text: What must you do if you change a repeater source after its attributes are used in merge fields? Delete those merge fields, add the new repeater source, then recreate the merge fields.

title: When adding a merge field inside a repeater, which item do you expand?
text: When adding a merge field inside a repeater, which item do you expand? The item with the same name as the repeater source — it's the first item in the Add Merge Field menu and contains the source's attributes.

title: Why must you allocate time when using a new recommender?
text: Why must you allocate time when using a new recommender? The recommender needs a training period with at least one successful refresh before it can be used.

title: How does an objective-based recommender differ from rule-based image variations?
text: How does an objective-based recommender differ from rule-based image variations? Instead of writing rules to decide which image each contact sees, the recommender chooses the best image for each contact at send time, learning from engagement over time.

title: Why does the design canvas show a placeholder for recommender content, and how do you see
text: Why does the design canvas show a placeholder for recommender content, and how do you see real output? The recommender chooses content per contact, so there's no single fixed result. Use Preview, enter parameters such as a segment to simulate a contact context, and review what the recommender returns.

title: Where are component/template landing pages vs. code-view landing pages hosted?
text: Where are component/template landing pages vs. code-view landing pages hosted? Component/template pages → the auto-generated Marketing Landing Pages Experience Cloud site; code-view pages → a marketing site (managed from the Marketing Sites tab).

title: What permissions are needed to create vs. publish landing page content?
text: What permissions are needed to create vs. publish landing page content? Create/edit: Marketing Cloud Manager + any CMS workspace contributor role. Publish/unpublish: Marketing Cloud Manager + a CMS workspace contributor role of content admin or content manager. AMPscript authoring adds the AMPscript Author permission.

title: When can you edit a landing page URL alias, and what happens on publish?
text: When can you edit a landing page URL alias, and what happens on publish? Only in Draft status (default alias = title + content key). After publish you can't change it; publishing activates the alias.

title: What happens when you publish a landing page that contains a form?
text: What happens when you publish a landing page that contains a form? The form is published and the flow related to the form is activated.

title: What structured data format is allowed in landing page head tags?
text: What structured data format is allowed in landing page head tags? Only JSON-LD ( <script type="application/ld+json" ). Head tags don't support JavaScript; only <link , <meta , and <script tags are allowed.

title: What are the requirements for a landing page redirect URL?
text: What are the requirements for a landing page redirect URL? Must begin with https:// and be fewer than 2,000 characters. Set it up before unpublishing to avoid the "URL no longer exists" page.

title: What's required to preview a landing page, and what's unresolved in preview?
text: What's required to preview a landing page, and what's unresolved in preview? You must be a site contributor to the Marketing Landing Pages site. Merge fields are unresolved in preview; external images need their domain in the Trusted URL list.

title: What does locking a landing page template component protect — and what doesn't it protect?
text: What does locking a landing page template component protect — and what doesn't it protect? It protects content and settings only. Authors can still edit targeting rules, add/delete variations, and modify personalization logic on locked components — clone the personalization point for control over the logic.

title: What happens when a marketer creates a landing page from a template with dynamic content?
text: What happens when a marketer creates a landing page from a template with dynamic content? All dynamic content rules and variants are copied to the new landing page automatically. The fallback variant renders when no rules match or the data lookup fails.

title: What one-time admin setup is needed for LinkedIn posts?
text: What one-time admin setup is needed for LinkedIn posts? Add the Social Posts related list to the campaigns object (Object Manager → Campaigns Layout → Related List), then connect a LinkedIn account via Manage Connections.

title: What are the minimum requirements for a form, and the unique names for submission fields?
text: What are the minimum requirements for a form, and the unique names for submission fields? At least one input component and one button. Email field = unique name Email, first name = FirstName, last name = LastName (case-insensitive, no extra characters/spaces).

title: How many forms per landing page, and how many flows per form?
text: How many forms per landing page, and how many flows per form? One form per landing page; a form relates to only one flow. View modes must match (block ↔ block, code ↔ code).

title: What objects can a form's write data provider use, and what's the default?
text: What objects can a form's write data provider use, and what's the default? Account, Contact, Lead, Prospect, or an available marketing object. If a marketing object is available it's the default; otherwise the form defaults to Lead. Only one write data source object at a time.

title: What can a form's read data providers supply, and what's the lookup limit?
text: What can a form's read data providers supply, and what's the lookup limit? Pre-fill fields and drive progressive profiling (they don't receive submitted data). Sources: recipient data graph, marketing object, or Prospect; up to 2 lookup data providers (max 1 marketing object + 1 recipient data graph).

title: Which field types are supported on forms, and which standard field isn't?
text: Which field types are supported on forms, and which standard field isn't? Checkbox, Date, Date/Time, Time, Email, Phone Number, Number, Picklist, Text, Text Area, Text Area (Long), URL. Number of Employees (Account/Lead/Prospect) isn't supported.

title: What happens if you edit a CRM field's API name after using it in a form?
text: What happens if you edit a CRM field's API name after using it in a form? Any new data submitted to that field isn't saved. Also, a data source field can appear only once on a form (no duplicates).

title: What's required for a hidden form field marked as required?
text: What's required for a hidden form field marked as required? A fallback value — used when the URL parameter is invalid or missing. Hidden fields are visible on the canvas but not in preview/live form.

title: Where does Google reCAPTCHA v2 apply, and what breaks it?
text: Where does Google reCAPTCHA v2 apply, and what breaks it? Only marketing landing pages with forms (not LWR/template sites); once enabled it shows on every form. Changing My Domain breaks it on existing published sites — add the new domain in the Google admin console.

title: What are the restrictions on progressive profiling rules?
text: What are the restrictions on progressive profiling rules? Can't add a rule to a hidden field; can't hide a field that has a profile rule; can't apply to a related object. Changing the read data provider/source removes all rule connections.

title: What should you avoid pre-filling in forms?
text: What should you avoid pre-filling in forms? Personally identifiable information such as Social Security numbers or credit card numbers.

title: What happens when you unpublish a form?
text: What happens when you unpublish a form? Its flow is deactivated and the Submit button stops working (an in-flight submission still completes). The form reverts to draft; to edit/republish, save the flow as a new version.

title: What makes up the form embedding code for external sites?
text: What makes up the form embedding code for external sites? Two <script tags (hosting + Lightning Out bootstrap) and a custom HTML <fragment element. Generated from the published version — republish to refresh.

title: What security configuration is needed before embedding a form externally?
text: What security configuration is needed before embedding a form externally? CORS Allowed Origin List entry, clickjack protection (Trusted Domains for Inline Framing or allow any page), Trusted Sites for Scripts, then publish the Experience Cloud site (skipping publish causes a frame-ancestors 'self' CSP error).

title: What does a form handler do, and what does creating one also create?
text: What does a form handler do, and what does creating one also create? Captures data from an existing external website form and creates/updates Salesforce records (no site rebuild needed). Creating one also creates a data source in Data 360.

title: What must match exactly for a form handler to capture a value?
text: What must match exactly for a form handler to capture a value? The external field name must exactly match the HTML name attribute of the field in your form. Date = YYYY-MM-DD; Time = hh:mm:ss; DateTime = ISO 8601; selected checkbox = true.

title: What's a honeypot field, and what name should you give it?
text: What's a honeypot field, and what name should you give it? A hidden field that bots fill in — the handler blocks submissions containing a value there. Use an appealing generic label (company, website), not an obvious name like honeypot or do not fill. Combine with reCAPTCHA.

title: When must you map fields relative to creating the form-handler flow?
text: When must you map fields relative to creating the form-handler flow? Add and map all required fields before creating the flow — edits after don't reflect automatically (new flow versions include updated mappings).

title: What's the difference between client-side and server-side form handler connections?
text: What's the difference between client-side and server-side form handler connections? Client-side (JavaScript snippet) supports web tracking and identity resolution; server-side (direct POST URL) doesn't, but works with third-party builders, strict CSP, and backend posts. Both need a CORS Allowlist entry.

title: What does a marketing site host, and what permission is needed to manage it?
text: What does a marketing site host, and what permission is needed to manage it? Code-view landing pages and forms (component/template pages use the Marketing Landing Pages site). Editing settings and publishing requires the Marketing Cloud Admin permission set.

title: What must you do to publish a landing page in a non-default language?
text: What must you do to publish a landing page in a non-default language? Add the language to the marketing site (Languages tab) and republish the site.

title: What is 1:1 in Marketing Cloud Next?
text: What is 1:1 in Marketing Cloud Next? Business Unit ↔ Data Space mapping.

title: What takes up to 48 hours?
text: What takes up to 48 hours? DNS propagation after adding domain authentication records.

title: What does 95% confidence trigger?
text: What does 95% confidence trigger? The Path Experiment auto-declared winner (Bayesian).

title: What do 72% and 30% represent?
text: What do 72% and 30% represent? 72% = pass score; 30% = Section 4 exam weight.

title: What is 2048-bit?
text: What is 2048-bit? The DKIM key strength.

title: What is the max number of segments per org?
text: What is the max number of segments per org? 9,950 .

title: What is the max number of Business Units?
text: What is the max number of Business Units? 150 (deactivation is permanent).

title: What do 25 / 15 / 50 / 100 represent?
text: What do 25 / 15 / 50 / 100 represent? 25 personalization points per item · 15 variations per component · 50 filters per tab · 100 attributes per segment.

title: What do 5 / 5 / 1 / 1 / 1 represent?
text: What do 5 / 5 / 1 / 1 / 1 represent? Max Offers (5) / Lookup Data Graphs (5) / Event (1) / Apex Class (1) / Activation (1) data sources per content item or message.

title: How many components are the subject line and preheader?
text: How many components are the subject line and preheader? One component — they are personalized together.

title: Which data source can be replaced but not removed?
text: Which data source can be replaced but not removed? The Personalization Recommender .

title: What is the recommender training requirement?
text: What is the recommender training requirement? ≥1 successful refresh .

title: Which data graph is recommended for landing pages?
text: Which data graph is recommended for landing pages? A real-time data graph (faster, costs more).

title: What is the 80-character limit?
text: What is the 80-character limit? The prospect Title conversion limit — conversion fails if the lead Title 80 (the prospect allows 128).

title: What lasts 90 days?
text: What lasts 90 days? The View as Web Page link validity (re-renders personalized values per open). Also the default segment lookback window and the send-time consent cache TTL.

title: What is the max email file attachment size?
text: What is the max email file attachment size? 5 MB (a PDF from CMS).

title: What do 30 / 30 represent in Distributed Marketing?
text: What do 30 / 30 represent in Distributed Marketing? Max 30 approved images and 30 approved phrases per template.

title: What is the max landing page redirect URL length?
text: What is the max landing page redirect URL length? 2,000 characters (must start with https:// ).

title: What is the form cardinality rule?
text: What is the form cardinality rule? 1 form per landing page; 1 flow per form — view modes must match.

title: What is the max number of lookup data providers on a form?
text: What is the max number of lookup data providers on a form? 2 (1 marketing object + 1 recipient data graph).

title: What is the max form data source name length?
text: What is the max form data source name length? 20 characters (alphanumeric + underscores only).

title: What are the reputation targets?
text: What are the reputation targets? < 2% bounce and < 0.1% complaint .

title: What is the 6-month rule?
text: What is the 6-month rule? The engagement cutoff for list hygiene.

title: What is E.164?
text: What is E.164? The phone format required for consent imports.

title: What are the SMS opt-out keywords?
text: What are the SMS opt-out keywords? STOP / QUIT / CANCEL / END / UNSUBSCRIBE .

title: What are the SMS encoding character limits?
text: What are the SMS encoding character limits? GSM-7 = 160 chars / UCS-2 = 70 chars .

title: What is the max number of MCE journeys per campaign?
text: What is the max number of MCE journeys per campaign? 20 .

title: What do 15M and 210 represent?
text: What do 15M and 210 represent? The activation-triggered flow rate limit — 15M actions/hr + 210 threads (MC/Data 360).

title: What does 2.5% represent?
text: What does 2.5% represent? The flow element error rate that triggers rate limiting.

title: What does +50% represent?
text: What does +50% represent? The concurrency allowance for real-time-response flows.

title: What does 0.7 represent?
text: What does 0.7 represent? The fuzzy match AI confidence threshold.

title: What happened on Aug 7, 2025?
text: What happened on Aug 7, 2025? The internal Data Pipeline became free .

title: What happened on Sept 4, 2025?
text: What happened on Sept 4, 2025? The Segmentation/Activation billing card was retired (merged into Data Services).

title: What is the max number of exit rules per flow?
text: What is the max number of exit rules per flow? 10 (evaluated on start/resume).

title: What is the max Subflow variable API name length?
text: What is the max Subflow variable API name length? 40 characters .

title: What is the Get Records record limit range?
text: What is the Get Records record limit range? 2–20,000 .

title: What is the Recycle Bin retention for deleted records?
text: What is the Recycle Bin retention for deleted records? 15 days .

title: What is the default in-app message expiration?
text: What is the default in-app message expiration? 180 days .

title: What is the max number of Collection Sort fields?
text: What is the max number of Collection Sort fields? 3 fields .

title: What do 1 and 255 represent in the Transform element?
text: What do 1 and 255 represent in the Transform element? Max 1 nested collection and a 255-character formula limit. ---

title: Which flow type is Create Consent available in?
text: Which flow type is Create Consent available in? Automation Event-Triggered flows (also Data Cloud-Triggered / On-Demand). ⚠️ Never MessagingConsent .

title: What is the rule for all MC Next consent writes?
text: What is the rule for all MC Next consent writes? All writes must use Create Consent (Data Cloud or Automation Event-triggered); direct DMO field mapping is ignored at send time .

title: What edition and add-on does a Path Experiment require?
text: What edition and add-on does a Path Experiment require? Advanced + Personalization .

title: ⚠️ Do reconciliation rules govern contact points?
text: ⚠️ Do reconciliation rules govern contact points? No — source priority does.

title: ⚠️ Does a paused flow count as active?
text: ⚠️ Does a paused flow count as active? Yes — a paused flow counts as active.

title: ⚠️ What happens to a campaign when one flow errors?
text: ⚠️ What happens to a campaign when one flow errors? The whole campaign shows Error.

title: ⚠️ What does an Update Records element with no filter do?
text: ⚠️ What does an Update Records element with no filter do? Updates ALL records.

title: ⚠️ What does NOT refresh the send-time consent cache?
text: ⚠️ What does NOT refresh the send-time consent cache? Direct DMO/DLO writes (e.g., a mapped DLO import) — consent can look saved yet be stale at send.

title: ⚠️ How does a Preference Page unsubscribe affect metrics?
text: ⚠️ How does a Preference Page unsubscribe affect metrics? It is a consent update , not an Email Engagement event — so it skews Email Opt-Out Rate lower.

title: ⚠️ What is not recorded when consent is required?
text: ⚠️ What is not recorded when consent is required? The first page view .

title: ⚠️ What is counterintuitive about the Metrics Guard score?
text: ⚠️ What is counterintuitive about the Metrics Guard score? Lower = more likely real .

title: ⚠️ Which marketing object properties are immutable?
text: ⚠️ Which marketing object properties are immutable? Field API name, data type, and primary key designation.

title: ⚠️ What is the risk of Match on Blank?
text: ⚠️ What is the risk of Match on Blank? It is ignored in real-time and can cause overmatching (the "50,000+ profiles" error).

title: ⚠️ What personalization is lost when copying an email?
text: ⚠️ What personalization is lost when copying an email? Only default variations are copied — other variations, rules, and recommenders are not.

title: ⚠️ Is Convert to Code reversible?
text: ⚠️ Is Convert to Code reversible? No — it is one-way and removes dynamic content.

title: ⚠️ What can authors still edit on a locked template?
text: ⚠️ What can authors still edit on a locked template? Targeting rules and variations (locking protects content/settings only).

title: ⚠️ What happens when you share a dashboard?
text: ⚠️ What happens when you share a dashboard? It won't appear to users — sharing alone does not grant visibility.

title: ⚠️ What flow type do Wait elements require?
text: ⚠️ What flow type do Wait elements require? Autolaunched flows — they cannot be mixed with screens or choice.

title: ⚠️ What can a Subflow not call?
text: ⚠️ What can a Subflow not call? Flows with wait elements .

title: ⚠️ Is "Define with AI" supported for Marketing Cloud flows?
text: ⚠️ Is "Define with AI" supported for Marketing Cloud flows? No .

title: ⚠️ Which flows don't appear on the Marketing Calendar?
text: ⚠️ Which flows don't appear on the Marketing Calendar? Event-triggered and form-triggered flows.

title: ⚠️ What is the critical form handler rule?
text: ⚠️ What is the critical form handler rule? External field names must exactly match the HTML name attributes.

title: ⚠️ When must form handler fields be mapped?
text: ⚠️ When must form handler fields be mapped? Before creating the flow — edits afterwards don't reflect automatically.

title: ⚠️ Why never delete a Communication Subscription?
text: ⚠️ Why never delete a Communication Subscription? It destroys the audit trail.

title: ⚠️ Does transactional SMS require consent?
text: ⚠️ Does transactional SMS require consent? Yes (TCPA) — even for OTP/2FA.

title: ⚠️ Does "Unsubscribe from all" persist as a permanent block?
text: ⚠️ Does "Unsubscribe from all" persist as a permanent block? No .

title: ⚠️ Can content with variations be exported/imported?
text: ⚠️ Can content with variations be exported/imported? No .

title: ⚠️ What must you do if you change a data source after using attributes in merge fields?
text: ⚠️ What must you do if you change a data source after using attributes in merge fields? Delete the merge fields, add the new source, and recreate them.

title: ⚠️ What is required when combining a form and a landing page?
text: ⚠️ What is required when combining a form and a landing page? The data graphs must match .

title: ⚠️ What breaks prospect → lead conversion?
text: ⚠️ What breaks prospect → lead conversion? A lead Title 80 characters , or custom required fields on the Lead.

title: ⚠️ Are composite keys supported in the segment canvas?
text: ⚠️ Are composite keys supported in the segment canvas? No — single-field joins only.

title: ⚠️ When is a marketing object delete blocked?
text: ⚠️ When is a marketing object delete blocked? When any other object references it.

title: ⚠️ What happens if you manually edit the plain text version?
text: ⚠️ What happens if you manually edit the plain text version? It desyncs from the HTML version — future changes are not included.

title: ⚠️ What breaks reCAPTCHA?
text: ⚠️ What breaks reCAPTCHA? Changing My Domain .

title: ⚠️ What should you avoid with progressive profiling?
text: ⚠️ What should you avoid with progressive profiling? Pre-filling PII .

title: ⚠️ What happens when you unpublish a form?
text: ⚠️ What happens when you unpublish a form? It deactivates its flow and Submit stops working.

title: ⚠️ What does opening element details consume?
text: ⚠️ What does opening element details consume? Data Cloud credits .

title: ⚠️ For which runs is on-canvas analytics unavailable?
text: ⚠️ For which runs is on-canvas analytics unavailable? Runs before Winter '25 . ---

title: What does 4 represent in the consent model?
text: What does 4 represent in the consent model? The number of consent granularity levels — and the level MC Next enforces ( Level 4 = contact point + subscription type).

title: What does 6 represent?
text: What does 6 represent? The minimum number of configuration steps , and the number of flow types (audience, activation-triggered, automation event-triggered, on-demand, broadcast, Data Cloud-triggered).

title: What are the five out-of-the-box marketing agents?
text: What are the five out-of-the-box marketing agents? Segment Creation · Campaign Creation · Content Creation · Journey Decisioning · Account Discovery.

title: How many data providers are there, and what are they?
text: How many data providers are there, and what are they? Eight: data graph, event, activation, Salesforce record, Apex class, personalization recommender, lookup graph, offer.

title: How many ways can contact point selection be determined at send time?
text: How many ways can contact point selection be determined at send time? Four: data graph in flow properties, on-demand API payload, activation source priority order, activation template.

title: What does 90 days represent (three things)?
text: What does 90 days represent (three things)? The consent cache TTL , the View as Web Page link validity, and the analysis window for all three predictive AI models.

title: What is the STO optimization window range?
text: What is the STO optimization window range? From 2 hours up to 1 week .

title: ⚠️ Can a message use both an activation and an event data provider?
text: ⚠️ Can a message use both an activation and an event data provider? No — each requires a specific flow orchestration pattern, creating a conflict in how data binds to the message.

title: ⚠️ Do reconciliation rules resolve contact points?
text: ⚠️ Do reconciliation rules resolve contact points? No — they only select single values for unified fields that can't hold multiple values (like name). All contact points are retained in the unified profile.

title: How many emails are sent when a unified individual has two unique email addresses across t
text: How many emails are sent when a unified individual has two unique email addresses across three records? Two — one per unique address; duplicate addresses count as a single contact point.

title: ⚠️ When is an activation template required?
text: ⚠️ When is an activation template required? When the segment's segment-on object is NOT Unified Individual .

title: ⚠️ Which two flow types cannot send email?
text: ⚠️ Which two flow types cannot send email? Record-triggered flows and Data Cloud-triggered flows .

title: What does "off-core" mean for marketing flows?
text: What does "off-core" mean for marketing flows? They run on a separate high-scale processing engine outside the core Salesforce transactional runtime — so governor limits and transaction-scaling concerns don't apply the same way.

title: ⚠️ What's the difference between an authorized and an authenticated email domain?
text: ⚠️ What's the difference between an authorized and an authenticated email domain? Authenticated = full DKIM/DNS sending configuration. Authorized = ownership only, required for dynamic From/Reply-to addresses .

title: ⚠️ How do you share content across business units?
text: ⚠️ How do you share content across business units? Post it as a common asset , then copy it into the target workspace — content can't be accessed directly across business units.

title: Name the four Engagement Scoring personas with their open/click likelihoods.
text: Name the four Engagement Scoring personas with their open/click likelihoods. Loyalists (high/high) · Selective Subscribers (low open/high click) · Window Shoppers (high open/low click) · Win Back/Dormant (low/low).

title: What are the four Engagement Frequency classifications?
text: What are the four Engagement Frequency classifications? Saturated · Almost Saturated · On Target · Under Saturated.

title: What are the three out-of-the-box reporting capabilities?
text: What are the three out-of-the-box reporting capabilities? Campaign Performance Dashboard · Marketing Performance Dashboard · Semantic Data Model — all included with no extra license.

title: What powers the semantic data model, and what's its name?
text: What powers the semantic data model, and what's its name? Tableau Next powers it; it's the Marketing Intelligence Semantic Data Model . ---

title: Which Salesforce editions and product tiers support Marketing Cloud Next?
text: Which Salesforce editions and product tiers support Marketing Cloud Next? Enterprise and Unlimited editions, with either the Growth or Advanced product tier.

title: What is the core difference between the Growth and Advanced tiers?
text: What is the core difference between the Growth and Advanced tiers? Growth is the standard tier; Advanced unlocks extra capabilities — Business Units, Engagement Scoring/Frequency, on-canvas insights, Path Experiments, and higher marketing-object storage limits.

title: What platform is Marketing Cloud Next built natively on?
text: What platform is Marketing Cloud Next built natively on? Salesforce Data Cloud (Data 360) — it is not a standalone product bolted onto the old Marketing Cloud.

title: What must be installed first when setting up Marketing Cloud Next, and what follows automa
text: What must be installed first when setting up Marketing Cloud Next, and what follows automatically? Data kits install first (the data plumbing); data streams auto-deploy afterwards.

title: What are the two Data 360 provisioning models to know for the exam?
text: What are the two Data 360 provisioning models to know for the exam? A core-org configuration (Data 360 in the same org) versus a Data Cloud One / companion-org configuration. ⚠️ This is a thin spot in the source material — know that provisioning model is an explicit exam objective. ---

title: What are the two core Marketing Cloud Next permission sets and how do they differ?
text: What are the two core Marketing Cloud Next permission sets and how do they differ? Marketing Cloud Admin (includes Setup access) and Marketing Cloud Manager (campaigns, segments, and flows only — no Setup).

title: How do CMS content roles differ from permission sets?
text: How do CMS content roles differ from permission sets? Content roles ( Content Admin / Manager / Author ) are separate from permission sets and govern what a user can do with CMS content, not platform access.

title: What is an identity-licensed user in Marketing Cloud Next?
text: What is an identity-licensed user in Marketing Cloud Next? A user licensed to access identity-resolved profile data — relevant when granting access to unified individual records.

title: Which permission set is needed to work with Marketing Triggers?
text: Which permission set is needed to work with Marketing Triggers? The Marketing Triggers Admin permission set. ---

title: Which edition tier is required for Business Units?
text: Which edition tier is required for Business Units? Advanced only.

title: What is the relationship between a Business Unit and a data space?
text: What is the relationship between a Business Unit and a data space? A 1:1 mapping — one Business Unit equals one data space, which provides data isolation.

title: What is the maximum number of Business Units, and can they be reactivated?
text: What is the maximum number of Business Units, and can they be reactivated? Maximum 150 . Deactivation is permanent — you cannot reactivate a deactivated Business Unit.

title: Can you deactivate the last remaining Business Unit?
text: Can you deactivate the last remaining Business Unit? No — the system prevents deactivating the final Business Unit.

title: What are the two Business Unit member roles and how do they differ?
text: What are the two Business Unit member roles and how do they differ? Marketer-Standard (can activate flows) and Marketer-ReadOnly (cannot activate flows). ---

title: How does sharing work between Enhanced CMS workspaces?
text: How does sharing work between Enhanced CMS workspaces? You share from a source workspace to a target workspace.

title: What does "sharing is non-transitive" mean for CMS workspaces?
text: What does "sharing is non-transitive" mean for CMS workspaces? If you share workspace A to B, and B to C, C does not automatically get A's content. You must share the source to each target individually.

title: What are the three Enhanced CMS workspace roles?
text: What are the three Enhanced CMS workspace roles? Content Admin , Content Manager , and Content Author . ---

title: What exactly do you authenticate in Marketing Cloud Next?
text: What exactly do you authenticate in Marketing Cloud Next? The sending subdomain — via DKIM, SPF, and DMARC records.

title: How long can DNS propagation take after adding authentication records?
text: How long can DNS propagation take after adding authentication records? Up to 48 hours .

title: Name the three functional subdomains and what each handles.
text: Name the three functional subdomains and what each handles. reply (replies) · bounce (bounces) · leave (unsubscribes). Each requires its own CNAME record.

title: What key strength does Marketing Cloud Next use for DKIM, and how is it configured?
text: What key strength does Marketing Cloud Next use for DKIM, and how is it configured? 2048-bit , configured via 3 outbound CNAME records .

title: Is DMARC required to activate a sending domain?
text: Is DMARC required to activate a sending domain? No — DMARC is recommended but not required to activate.

title: What is a branded tracking domain and what does it need?
text: What is a branded tracking domain and what does it need? A custom domain used for click/open tracking links, secured with a CA-signed certificate . ---

title: How are managed dedicated IPs assigned in Marketing Cloud Next?
text: How are managed dedicated IPs assigned in Marketing Cloud Next? They are auto-assigned by volume , with continuous rebalancing across the pool.

title: What is the PRIMARY signal for domain reputation?
text: What is the PRIMARY signal for domain reputation? Domain reputation (not IP reputation) is the primary signal.

title: How should you start a domain warming program?
text: How should you start a domain warming program? Begin with a few hundred sends per day and ramp gradually.

title: What are the target bounce and complaint rate thresholds?
text: What are the target bounce and complaint rate thresholds? Bounce rate < 2% and complaint rate < 0.1% .

title: What engagement cutoff is recommended for list hygiene?
text: What engagement cutoff is recommended for list hygiene? 6 months of no engagement. ---

title: Is Marketing Cloud a product?
text: Is Marketing Cloud a product? ⚠️ No — it's the portfolio brand. It contains four products: Marketing Cloud Next (← MCE), Salesforce Personalization (← MC Personalization), Marketing Intelligence (← MC Intelligence), and Loyalty Management (no-code B2B/B2C loyalty).

title: How many configuration steps are there, and which are automated?
text: How many configuration steps are there, and which are automated? Six minimum. The Setup Assistant automates the first three: set up Data 360, enable Marketing Cloud, deploy required data streams. Then add the physical address and create an authenticated domain .

title: Which two permission sets must be assigned before configuring MC Next?
text: Which two permission sets must be assigned before configuring MC Next? Data Cloud Architect (Data 360 setup, data modelling, data kits, streams, identity resolution) + Marketing Admin (most marketing Setup settings, publish/activate campaigns & segments).

title: What replaced the Data Cloud Admin permission set?
text: What replaced the Data Cloud Admin permission set? Data Cloud Architect — renamed in the Spring '26 release . ⚠️ System Administrator is a profile , not a permission set.

title: What's the difference between an authorized and an authenticated email domain?
text: What's the difference between an authorized and an authenticated email domain? Authenticated = full DKIM/DNS sending configuration. Authorized = ownership only (one verification record, no sending config), required for dynamic From/Reply-to addresses .

title: What causes a DMARC alignment failure?
text: What causes a DMARC alignment failure? Using a personal email address on the root domain as the From address — the From domain must align with the authenticated sending domain .

title: Where is all marketing content stored, and what is each workspace tied to?
text: Where is all marketing content stored, and what is each workspace tied to? In CMS content workspaces , each associated with a specific business unit .

title: What are the cardinalities between data spaces, business units, and content workspaces?
text: What are the cardinalities between data spaces, business units, and content workspaces? Data space → no business unit or one . Business unit → one or more content workspaces .

title: How do you share content across business units?
text: How do you share content across business units? ⚠️ Content can't be accessed directly across business units . Post it as a common asset (available to all units), then copy it into the target workspace .

title: Which business unit role gets CMS content access?
text: Which business unit role gets CMS content access? Marketing Standard = data space + CMS content. Marketing Read-Only = data space only. ⚠️ Users without Marketing Manager/Admin permission sets can only be Read-Only.

title: What must happen before content can be used, and what does publishing a form do?
text: What must happen before content can be used, and what does publishing a form do? Content must be published (saving isn't enough). Publishing a form activates its associated flow . ---

title: What consent model does Marketing Cloud Next use?
text: What consent model does Marketing Cloud Next use? Strict opt-in — the absence of an explicit "Yes" means the contact is blocked .

title: What three things make up the consent composite key?
text: What three things make up the consent composite key? Subscription + Contact Point + Channel Type .

title: Is consent tied to the person or the contact point?
text: Is consent tied to the person or the contact point? The contact point (email address, phone number, device ID) — not the person.

title: What is consent keyed on, and why is PartyID blank?
text: What is consent keyed on, and why is PartyID blank? Keyed on Contact Point value + CSCT ID , not PartyID. PartyID is blank by design because one address can map to multiple individuals.

title: What happens when two people share one email and one opts out?
text: What happens when two people share one email and one opts out? The opt-out affects everyone on that address — there is no way to send to some and suppress others sharing the same contact point. ---

title: Name the five consent-related DMOs.
text: Name the five consent-related DMOs. Contact Point (address) · Communication Subscription (topic) · Engagement Channel Type (medium) · Communication Subscription Channel Type (delivery method) · Communication Subscription Consent (the opt-in/opt-out record).

title: What does the Communication Subscription Consent (CSC) DMO store?
text: What does the Communication Subscription Consent (CSC) DMO store? The current consent status for a contact point + subscription + channel combination (updated in place).

title: What is the key difference between the Consent Audit Trail and the CSC DMO?
text: What is the key difference between the Consent Audit Trail and the CSC DMO? The Audit Trail is append-only (full history of every change); the CSC DMO stores only the current status and is updated in place.

title: What fields does the Consent Audit Trail capture?
text: What fields does the Consent Audit Trail capture? TimeStamp, ConsentStatus, ContactPointValue, CSCT ID, and caller-provided source attribution.

title: How do you attribute "who" made a consent change in the audit trail?
text: How do you attribute "who" made a consent change in the audit trail? There is no UserId/ActorId field . Use caller-provided source attribution (ConsentCapturedSourceType, ConsentCapturedSourceName, ConsentCapturedSourceDetails, SenderId).

title: How do you delete audit trail rows for GDPR?
text: How do you delete audit trail rows for GDPR? Use the Consent API ShouldForget endpoint on the Individual — async deletion reprocessed at 30/60/90 days , then permanent.

title: ⚠️ How many consent models exist in a Salesforce org, and which does MC Next read?
text: ⚠️ How many consent models exist in a Salesforce org, and which does MC Next read? Three — Salesforce Consent Data Model (legal basis), Data 360 consent objects (activation eligibility), and Communication Subscription Consent (MC Next sends). MC Next reads only the third , through the cache.

title: What are the Id prefixes for the three CRM consent objects?
text: What are the Id prefixes for the three CRM consent objects? Communication Subscription 0Xl · Engagement Channel Type 0eF · Communication Subscription Channel Type 0eB . The consent record itself lives in Data 360 only .

title: ⚠️ Does Engagement Channel Type have a DMO?
text: ⚠️ Does Engagement Channel Type have a DMO? No. Communication Subscription Channel Type carries an ssot EngagementChannelTypeId c with no relationship attached — the channel is a bare identifier on the Data 360 side.

title: What four subscription rules must you get right at creation?
text: What four subscription rules must you get right at creation? 1) Scope can't change (single BU or all BUs). 2) Deleting a subscription deletes all its consent data . 3) A new subscription doesn't appear on the preference page by default. 4) No frequency capping ( CommSubscriptionTiming exists but isn't mapped).

title: ⚠️ What is the state of the Party field on the consent DMO?
text: ⚠️ What is the state of the Party field on the consent DMO? Wired end to end from the DLO but always empty . Never build on it — join to a person through the Contact Point Email/Phone DMO instead. ---

title: What data kit carries consent, and how many streams does it install?
text: What data kit carries consent, and how many streams does it install? UnifiedMessagingConsent — it installs two streams: consent records ( MessagingConsentV2 ) and audit trail ( ConsentAuditTrailV2 ).

title: ⚠️ What are the two ways an org ends up with duplicate consent records for the same contac
text: ⚠️ What are the two ways an org ends up with duplicate consent records for the same contact point + subscription? 1) The documented pre-Summer '25 generation switch ( MessagingConsent → MessagingConsentV2 ). 2) The org-ID naming quirk — Salesforce appended the org ID to stream names, both spellings stayed active, so even a V2-only org gets duplicates.

title: ⚠️ Why is no consent DLO name portable?
text: ⚠️ Why is no consent DLO name portable? The org ID is appended to the stream name, so it differs per org (and changes when the org ID changes). Always read the actual stream name in your org before copying any query or transform.

title: What are the key fields in the V2 consent stream → DMO mapping?
text: What are the key fields in the V2 consent stream → DMO mapping? ConsentId (primary key = contact point value + CSCT Id) · ConsentCapturedDateTime (when the person decided) ≠ UpdatedTime (when the row changed) · PartyId mapped to Party but empty. ---

title: Name the four supported ways to create or manage consent.
text: Name the four supported ways to create or manage consent. 1) Preference Pages (subscriber self-service) · 2) Consent Status LWC (admin drops on layouts) · 3) Consent Imports (CSV) · 4) Salesforce Flow (Create Consent / Consent Request).

title: What are the four input parameters of the Create Consent action?
text: What are the four input parameters of the Create Consent action? Consent Status, Contact Point, Channel, and Communication Subscription.

title: In which flow types is Create Consent available?
text: In which flow types is Create Consent available? Data Cloud-Triggered , Automation Event-Triggered , and On-Demand flows (plus Record-Triggered from Winter '27). ⚠️ Never use the legacy MessagingConsent action.

title: What is the CSV consent import limit and its intended purpose?
text: What is the CSV consent import limit and its intended purpose? 50,000 rows per file, intended for one-time loads — not sustained high-volume sync.

title: Name the unsupported consent write paths that cause stale consent.
text: Name the unsupported consent write paths that cause stale consent. Data Stream → Consent DLO · Bulk Ingestion API → Consent DMO · Batch Data Transform → DLO mapped to CSC DMO · legacy MessagingConsent/MessagingConsentV2.

title: ⚠️ What happens when external consent is mapped straight into the CSC DMO?
text: ⚠️ What happens when external consent is mapped straight into the CSC DMO? It appears saved but is ignored at send time — causing silent dropouts, compliance violations, and UI misalignment.

title: What is the recommended 2-step process for consent at scale?
text: What is the recommended 2-step process for consent at scale? 1) Batch Data Transform → DLO (initial load). 2) Data Cloud-Triggered Flow with Create Consent to write consent so it is honoured at send time.

title: What does "contactPointValue provided value cannot be formatted" mean?
text: What does "contactPointValue provided value cannot be formatted" mean? The Contact Point field must reference a contact point value (e.g., an email address), not a contact point ID . ---

title: At send time, does Marketing Cloud Next read consent directly from the DMO?
text: At send time, does Marketing Cloud Next read consent directly from the DMO? No — it reads a cache keyed by recipient email. The cache is populated on a miss and used for 90 days unless updated.

title: Which actions refresh the send-time consent cache?
text: Which actions refresh the send-time consent cache? Manual layout update · Unsubscribe link / Preference Center · CSV import · and (officially) the Create Consent flow activity. ⚠️ Direct DMO/DLO writes do not refresh the cache.

title: ⚠️ Why can consent "look saved" yet still be stale at send time?
text: ⚠️ Why can consent "look saved" yet still be stale at send time? Because a direct DMO/DLO write (e.g., a mapped DLO import) does not refresh the send-time cache — the cache still holds the old value. ---

title: What are the two steps of double opt-in?
text: What are the two steps of double opt-in? 1) Submit the sign-up form and receive a transactional confirmation email. 2) Click the confirmation link to verify intent — only then is consent recorded.

title: Why must the DOI confirmation email be Transactional?
