text: Why must the DOI confirmation email be Transactional? Only Transactional emails can be sent to contacts without confirmed consent; a Promotional email would fail delivery.

title: What does the Wait Until Event step monitor in a DOI flow?
text: What does the Wait Until Event step monitor in a DOI flow? The transactional confirmation email (flow action to monitor) and the opt-in confirmation link/CTA (link to monitor). ---

title: ⚠️ Why might Email Opt-Out Rate look lower than expected?
text: ⚠️ Why might Email Opt-Out Rate look lower than expected? Preference Page unsubscribes are processed as consent updates , not Email Engagement Unsubscribe events — so they are excluded from the Email Opt-Out Rate.

title: What is the opt-out scope for Email, SMS, and WhatsApp?
text: What is the opt-out scope for Email, SMS, and WhatsApp? Email = per subscription + channel · SMS = per sender code · WhatsApp = per contact point (blocked in-app).

title: ⚠️ Which message types require a consent check?
text: ⚠️ Which message types require a consent check? Promotional email required · transactional email not required · promotional SMS/WhatsApp/RCS required · transactional SMS/WhatsApp/RCS required . Separate switches under Setup → email channel settings.

title: What must you accept to disable consent checks, and what does the change not affect?
text: What must you accept to disable consent checks, and what does the change not affect? You must affirm in writing that you accept responsibility for compliance problems. ⚠️ The change doesn't affect active flows — anything already running keeps checking.

title: ⚠️ How does SMS/WhatsApp/RCS opt-out granularity differ from email?
text: ⚠️ How does SMS/WhatsApp/RCS opt-out granularity differ from email? Each code/number/agent maps to one or more subscriptions , and opting out of the channel opts out of all mapped subscriptions — there is no per-subscription opt-out over SMS. RCS exception: can reuse existing SMS consent when the use case matches.

title: How do Compliance BCC and CC recipients behave with consent checks?
text: How do Compliance BCC and CC recipients behave with consent checks? Compliance BCC is excluded from consent checks entirely (it doesn't represent a person). CC recipients are suppressed if the primary recipient lacks consent.

title: How long do consent changes take to appear in the DMO?
text: How long do consent changes take to appear in the DMO? Minutes (up to a couple of hours with Consent Changes in flows) — long enough that a test looks like it failed when it has only just started.

title: What four things can you currently not see about consent?
text: What four things can you currently not see about consent? 1) The cache . 2) Who changed a record (no actor field). 3) Consent history on the record. 4) Anything in the Party field. (Plus: the component shows only the 100 most recent records.)

title: Does "Unsubscribe from all" create a permanent block?
text: Does "Unsubscribe from all" create a permanent block? No — it does not persist as a permanent block.

title: ⚠️ Why should you never delete a Communication Subscription?
text: ⚠️ Why should you never delete a Communication Subscription? Deleting it destroys the audit trail for that subscription.

title: What are the consent rules for transactional email and transactional SMS?
text: What are the consent rules for transactional email and transactional SMS? Transactional email consent check is off by default , but selecting a Communication Subscription turns it on. Transactional SMS (OTP/2FA) still requires consent (TCPA).

title: What does a spam complaint (FBL) plus Reply Mail Management opt the contact out of?
text: What does a spam complaint (FBL) plus Reply Mail Management opt the contact out of? All current subscriptions — there is no channel-level or account-level opt-out today.

title: What are the SMS opt-out keywords?
text: What are the SMS opt-out keywords? STOP / QUIT / CANCEL / END / UNSUBSCRIBE .

title: What phone format is required for consent imports?
text: What phone format is required for consent imports? E.164 format. ---

title: What cookie does the consent banner use and how long does it last?
text: What cookie does the consent banner use and how long does it last? sfmc consent , storing True/False for 365 days .

title: ⚠️ What is the consent banner trap on the first page view?
text: ⚠️ What is the consent banner trap on the first page view? The first page view is not recorded when consent is required.

title: What is the rule for all Marketing Cloud Next consent writes in the 3-flow sync architectu
text: What is the rule for all Marketing Cloud Next consent writes in the 3-flow sync architecture? All writes must use Create Consent (Data Cloud-Triggered or Automation Event-Triggered). ⚠️ Direct DMO field mapping is ignored at send time .

title: How do you segment on consent, and what is the cost implication?
text: How do you segment on consent, and what is the cost implication? Use a Calculated Insight workaround — it is metered and consumes credits. ---

title: Name the four levels of consent granularity.
text: Name the four levels of consent granularity. L1 = entire individual record (all channels/subscriptions/points) · L2 = a channel as a whole (all email) · L3 = a specific contact point value · L4 = a specific contact point + a specific subscription type.

title: Which consent level does Marketing Cloud Next enforce?
text: Which consent level does Marketing Cloud Next enforce? ⚠️ Level 4 — the most granular (contact point + subscription type).

title: Name the four objects that manage Level 4 consent.
text: Name the four objects that manage Level 4 consent. Communication Subscription (purpose/category) · Communication Subscription Channel Type (subscription + channel) · Communication Subscription Consent (the consent record) · Engagement Channel Type (email/SMS/WhatsApp/RCS).

title: How does the message channel affect preference pages?
text: How does the message channel affect preference pages? The channel automatically determines the page: email → email preference manager; SMS → separate SMS-specific page. ⚠️ No unified cross-channel page out-of-the-box.

title: Name four limitations of out-of-the-box preference pages.
text: Name four limitations of out-of-the-box preference pages. No unified cross-channel page · no native multilingual support · no custom code (AMPscript/Apex/server-side JS) · can't pre-populate from URL parameters .

title: What did Spring and Summer add to preference pages?
text: What did Spring and Summer add to preference pages? Spring = custom preference pages. Summer = multiple preference pages (e.g., per brand).

title: What can't you edit in the standard subscription block?
text: What can't you edit in the standard subscription block? Button labels, headings, subheadings , and the order of the subscription list . Partial workaround: rename the subscriptions from the Consent tab . ---

title: What are the three data layers in Marketing Cloud Next, in order?
text: What are the three data layers in Marketing Cloud Next, in order? 1) DLO (Data Lake Object) — raw intake, unprocessed. 2) DMO (Data Model Object) — standardized structure. 3) Unified Individual — identity-resolved single profile.

title: What is a data graph?
text: What is a data graph? The "map" that exposes which DMO fields are available for personalization and decisioning. Unified Individual must be the primary object.

title: What is the key rule about field availability in a data graph?
text: What is the key rule about field availability in a data graph? A field must be explicitly added to the data graph to be usable. Data in Data 360 does not automatically become available everywhere.

title: What are the approximate ingestion lags for each stage?
text: What are the approximate ingestion lags for each stage? DLO 3 min (CDC) / 10 min (batch) · DMO same cycle · identity resolution once per day · segment 15–30 min · data graph up to 24 hours .

title: What are data kits and what do they do?
text: What are data kits and what do they do? Pre-built bundles that install the data plumbing (DMOs, mappings, streams) for a use case; data streams auto-deploy with them. ---

title: What does identity resolution do?
text: What does identity resolution do? Matches source records into a Unified Individual profile via rulesets.

title: What does the generated Individual ruleset contain?
text: What does the generated Individual ruleset contain? 3 match rules : Normalized Email, Lead-to-Contact, and Device-to-Known.

title: How many active rulesets are recommended per object, and why?
text: How many active rulesets are recommended per object, and why? One per object (Individual + Account) — running two doubles billing .

title: How often does identity resolution run, and is there a faster option?
text: How often does identity resolution run, and is there a faster option? Approximately once per day ; real-time resolution is available for immediate needs.

title: What are the two custom Identity Match Types?
text: What are the two custom Identity Match Types? lead-to-contact and device-to-known . ---

title: What is the difference between a match rule and match criteria?
text: What is the difference between a match rule and match criteria? A match rule is an opportunity to match (records match if any one rule's criteria are met). Match criteria is precision within a rule (records must match all criteria).

title: How do more match rules vs more criteria affect consolidation?
text: How do more match rules vs more criteria affect consolidation? More rules → higher consolidation. More criteria → lower consolidation.

title: Name the five match methods.
text: Name the five match methods. Exact · Exact Normalized · Fuzzy High Precision · Fuzzy Medium Precision · Fuzzy Low Precision.

title: What is the difference between Exact and Exact Normalized matching?
text: What is the difference between Exact and Exact Normalized matching? Exact is case-insensitive (Maryanne = maryanne). Exact Normalized transforms data first (email: strips whitespace/quotes, gmail . / + ; phone: libphonenumber validation; address: country rules).

title: What powers fuzzy matching and what is its confidence threshold?
text: What powers fuzzy matching and what is its confidence threshold? A BERT AI model (150+ countries, 3B words, 20M names) with a 0.7 confidence threshold. ⚠️ Not available for Account fields.

title: In real-time matching, which methods are used regardless of the scheduled method?
text: In real-time matching, which methods are used regardless of the scheduled method? All criteria run Exact , except phone/email which run Exact Normalized .

title: ⚠️ What is the risk of the "Match on Blank" advanced setting?
text: ⚠️ What is the risk of the "Match on Blank" advanced setting? It is ignored in real-time and can cause overmatching (the "50,000+ profiles" error).

title: ⚠️ Why should you avoid matching on a single contact point?
text: ⚠️ Why should you avoid matching on a single contact point? It mixes household members into one profile — except when using unique external IDs .

title: How many default match rules exist for Accounts, Individuals, and Households?
text: How many default match rules exist for Accounts, Individuals, and Households? Accounts = 2 · Individuals = 4 · Households = 1 rule only .

title: When is a unified profile considered "known"?
text: When is a unified profile considered "known"? If any source profile is known; account profiles are always known. Known profiles from all rulesets count toward entitlement. ---

title: What do reconciliation rules do?
text: What do reconciliation rules do? Select a single value for a unified field that cannot hold multiple values (e.g., name).

title: Name the three reconciliation rule types.
text: Name the three reconciliation rule types. Last Updated (ties → alphabetical) · Most Frequent (ties → last updated) · Source Priority (use on ID fields to stabilize).

title: ⚠️ Do reconciliation rules govern contact points?
text: ⚠️ Do reconciliation rules govern contact points? No — all contact points stay in the unified profile; use source priority in activations instead.

title: Does reconciliation change source data?
text: Does reconciliation change source data? No — it only determines what is shown in the unified profile; it never changes source data. ---

title: Name the five segment types and their purpose.
text: Name the five segment types and their purpose. Standard (scheduled audience on a DMO) · Real-time (millisecond on-demand) · Waterfall (priority-ranked, mutually exclusive offers) · Dynamic (parameterized placeholders) · Data kit (predefined, editable).

title: What are the key segment limits?
text: What are the key segment limits? 9,950 segments/org · 50 filters/tab · 100 attributes · 20 filters/container · nest 3 (container) / 10 (across).

title: What is the default lookback window and its maximum?
text: What is the default lookback window and its maximum? Default 90 days , maximum 2 years (container criteria override the segment-level setting).

title: What are the standard and rapid publish cadences?
text: What are the standard and rapid publish cadences? Standard 12/24h · Rapid 1/4h (max 20, SFMC/file storage only, cannot convert to standard).

title: What can a real-time segment NOT do?
text: What can a real-time segment NOT do? No exclusion, no nesting, no counts, and no manual publish. It needs Segment ID + Timestamp in the real-time graph.

title: What is a waterfall segment and its limit?
text: What is a waterfall segment and its limit? Priority-ranked, mutually exclusive offers — max 20 segments, one waterfall each, no rapid publish.

title: What is a dynamic segment?
text: What is a dynamic segment? A parameterized segment with placeholders, run via API or broadcast flow — it does not persist.

title: What are the canvas nesting limits?
text: What are the canvas nesting limits? Nest 3 levels within a container, 10 levels across the segment.

title: ⚠️ Are composite keys supported in the segment canvas?
text: ⚠️ Are composite keys supported in the segment canvas? No — only single-field joins . Use single unique primary key DMOs.

title: What aggregation functions does the segment canvas support?
text: What aggregation functions does the segment canvas support? Count, Sum, Average, Max, Min. Group/Rank/Limit allows max 3 group + 3 sort rules . ---

title: What is the difference between a Prospect and a Lead?
text: What is the difference between a Prospect and a Lead? Prospect = top of funnel, unqualified, marketing-owned, may have interacted once, no owner, low-to-medium conversion potential. Lead = middle of funnel, qualified, sales-owned, actively engaging, medium-to-high potential.

title: What is the progression of person records?
text: What is the progression of person records? Prospect (unqualified, marketing) → Lead (qualified, sales) → Contact (customer).

title: Can Individual or Unified Individual records be created manually?
text: Can Individual or Unified Individual records be created manually? No — they are created only via sync and harmonization .

title: What is required to create a Contact?
text: What is required to create a Contact? An Account .

title: What does a Campaign Member record do and what statuses does it use?
text: What does a Campaign Member record do and what statuses does it use? It relates a person to a campaign; statuses include Responded and Attended .

title: How is a Prospect converted to a Lead?
text: How is a Prospect converted to a Lead? Manually, or via a Data 360-Triggered Flow on an engagement score threshold.

title: How is a Prospect converted to a Contact?
text: How is a Prospect converted to a Contact? Manually, or via a Record-Triggered Flow (Prospect created/updated, e.g., ProspectStatus = Qualified) using the Convert Prospect action.

title: What are the inputs to the Convert Prospect action?
text: What are the inputs to the Convert Prospect action? Prospect ID, Converted Status + Converted checkbox, Existing/New Contact, Existing/New Account, and optional Opportunity.

title: When converting to an existing lead, which fields are overwritten?
text: When converting to an existing lead, which fields are overwritten? Only empty fields.

title: Which currency wins on prospect conversion?
text: Which currency wins on prospect conversion? The prospect's currency code wins (avoids conversion problems).

title: ⚠️ What Title length breaks prospect conversion?
text: ⚠️ What Title length breaks prospect conversion? A lead Title 80 characters breaks conversion (the prospect allows 128).

title: ⚠️ What blocks a prospect → lead conversion?
text: ⚠️ What blocks a prospect → lead conversion? Custom required fields on the Lead object.

title: How do key prospect fields map on conversion?
text: How do key prospect fields map on conversion? Company → Account Name · City/State/Zip → Mailing (Contact) / Billing (Account) · Email/Phone → same · Industry → Account only · Prospect Currency → Lead/Contact/Account Currency.

title: Name three restrictions on Prospect records.
text: Name three restrictions on Prospect records. Cannot be added as a campaign member · not in the Data Import Wizard · cannot be cloned or bulk deleted.

title: What do Lead Assignment Rules determine?
text: What do Lead Assignment Rules determine? The record owner after conversion; each rule entry = processing order + condition + assigned user.

title: What is an actionable list?
text: What is an actionable list? A static collection of leads OR contacts (never both), used with a list-triggered flow. ---

title: What are the field type limits for marketing objects?
text: What are the field type limits for marketing objects? Text ≤ 255 · Number ≤ 18 digits · Decimal. Storage: Growth 10GB / 25 objects , Advanced 40GB / 100 objects ; 100 columns per object.

title: How are marketing objects created and what defines the object?
text: How are marketing objects created and what defines the object? Via CSV import (data types inferred); the object contains only the file's columns .

title: What are the primary key rules for marketing objects?
text: What are the primary key rules for marketing objects? Multiple primary key fields are allowed, but no composite keys .

title: ⚠️ Which marketing object properties are immutable after creation?
text: ⚠️ Which marketing object properties are immutable after creation? Field API name, data type, and primary key designation — you must delete and recreate the field (which deletes its data).

title: What does a full refresh do and what permissions does it need?
text: What does a full refresh do and what permissions does it need? Deletes and replaces all data (CSV must match columns); needs Manage Marketing Objects + Modify All Marketing Object Records .

title: ⚠️ What happens when you delete a marketing object?
text: ⚠️ What happens when you delete a marketing object? Deletion is permanent (all data gone, cannot restore) and is blocked if any other object references it.

title: What is the difference between the two marketing object permissions?
text: What is the difference between the two marketing object permissions? ViewAllMarketingObjectRecords (view only) vs. ManageMarketingObjects (view + create/delete).

title: What are the AMPscript/Handlebars identifiers for marketing objects?
text: What are the AMPscript/Handlebars identifiers for marketing objects? Marketing object = mo · field = c · data graph = $dataGraph.Field . AMPscript uses Lookup() ; Handlebars uses queryFirst type="MO" . ---

title: When are segmentation credits consumed?
text: When are segmentation credits consumed? On publish .

title: Name three ways to reduce Data 360 credit consumption.
text: Name three ways to reduce Data 360 credit consumption. Fewer schedules, tighter lookback windows, preview before publish, and nesting common filters.

title: What is the cost of the Internal Data Pipeline, and since when?
text: What is the cost of the Internal Data Pipeline, and since when? Free since Aug 7, 2025 (Salesforce CRM / Marketing Cloud / Commerce Cloud / Personalization connectors).

title: Which ingestion consumes credits?
text: Which ingestion consumes credits? External ingestion (Snowflake, S3, streaming).

title: What is the cost rule for Activate DMO - Streaming?
text: What is the cost rule for Activate DMO - Streaming? Charged per record created/updated per activation — and doubles if a data graph is used.

title: When does Batch Calculated Insights charge?
text: When does Batch Calculated Insights charge? Only when underlying objects change; objects used multiple times are counted once .

title: How does Batch Profile Unification charge after the first run?
text: How does Batch Profile Unification charge after the first run? Only new/modified source profiles count.

title: What is the minimum credit decrement?
text: What is the minimum credit decrement? 1 per usage type (when fractional usage ≥ 1 over the month).

title: Which billing card was retired on Sept 4, 2025?
text: Which billing card was retired on Sept 4, 2025? The "Segmentation and Activation" card (merged into the Data Services card). ---

title: Which Data 360 capabilities should you know for the exam?
text: Which Data 360 capabilities should you know for the exam? Object model (DLO/DMO) · data streams & DLO→DMO mapping · data spaces · data kits · calculated insights · data graphs · segmentation · activations · identity resolution. (Deep unstructured-data knowledge not required.)

title: What did Spring '26 and Summer '26 add to CRM integration?
text: What did Spring '26 and Summer '26 add to CRM integration? Spring '26 = CRM records as an audience source (scheduled or event). Summer '26 = campaign members + actionable lists.

title: What does the Sales Data Kit create, and is it required?
text: What does the Sales Data Kit create, and is it required? Pre-configured streams/mappings for leads, contacts, accounts, prospects . Optional — but skipping it means extra config for some features, and Opportunity Influence requires it .

title: What happens to consent when you add new leads to an actionable list?
text: What happens to consent when you add new leads to an actionable list? ⚠️ No consent records are created — they must be loaded separately, or the audience is suppressed at send time (strict opt-in).

title: What are the constraints on an actionable list?
text: What are the constraints on an actionable list? It holds leads OR contacts, never both ; it's static (vs dynamic segments); only the creator can manually remove members.

title: Do reconciliation rules decide which contact point is used?
text: Do reconciliation rules decide which contact point is used? ⚠️ No. Reconciliation rules only select a single value for unified fields that can't hold multiple values (like name). All contact points are retained in the unified profile.

title: If a unified individual has three records with two unique email addresses, how many emails
text: If a unified individual has three records with two unique email addresses, how many emails are sent? Two — one per unique address; duplicate addresses are treated as a single contact point .

title: Name the four ways contact point selection is determined at send time.
text: Name the four ways contact point selection is determined at send time. 1) Data graph in flow automation properties. 2) On-demand API payload (data graph takes precedence). 3) Activation source priority order . 4) Activation template .

title: When is an activation template required?
text: When is an activation template required? ⚠️ When the segment's segment-on object is NOT Unified Individual .

title: Which DMO holds the telephone number field for phone contact point selection?
text: Which DMO holds the telephone number field for phone contact point selection? The Contact Point Phone DMO . ---

title: Name the four main personalization methods and when to use each.
text: Name the four main personalization methods and when to use each. Merge fields (single value, simple 1:1) · Dynamic content / variations (swap whole components per audience) · Repeater (series of items from a data source) · Saved expressions (filter+sort to return ONE value).

title: What is the difference between Handlebars and AMPscript?
text: What is the difference between Handlebars and AMPscript? Handlebars is the templating language with scripting + conditional logic (code view, data lookups). AMPscript is legacy scripting using the Lookup() function for reading marketing objects.

title: What are the key personalization limits?
text: What are the key personalization limits? 25 personalization points per item · 15 variations per component · linking components shares one personalization point · subject line + preheader = one component.

title: ⚠️ Can content with variations be exported/imported?
text: ⚠️ Can content with variations be exported/imported? No — content with variations cannot be exported or imported.

title: What are the identifiers for marketing object, field, and data graph?
text: What are the identifiers for marketing object, field, and data graph? Marketing object = mo · field = c · data graph = $dataGraph.Field . ---

title: Name the five flow types and their triggers.
text: Name the five flow types and their triggers. Audience/Segment (schedule/immediate) · Automation event-triggered (customer action) · Activation-triggered (Data 360 activation publishes) · Broadcast (API/Apex) · On-demand (API/Apex, high-priority).

title: What are the four audience sources for an audience flow?
text: What are the four audience sources for an audience flow? Segment, List, Record, Campaign . The segment must be published first; recurring runs up to every hour.

title: What triggers an automation event-triggered flow and how fast does it run?
text: What triggers an automation event-triggered flow and how fast does it run? A customer action (click, form submit, record update); runs within 15 minutes . ⚠️ The Create Consent element is available here only.

title: What triggers an activation-triggered flow and what is its refresh cadence?
text: What triggers an activation-triggered flow and what is its refresh cadence? A Data 360 activation publishing. Refresh: 10 min (incremental) / 24 hr (standard). It is the only Data 360 target type and uses MuleSoft or HTTP callout.

title: What is unique about a broadcast flow?
text: What is unique about a broadcast flow? It uses dynamic segments (membership determined after start) and can run asynchronously.

title: What is an on-demand flow used for?
text: What is an on-demand flow used for? High-priority API/Apex-triggered sends (e.g., order confirmations); it can include event info like order ID and amount.

title: What is the campaign ↔ flow cardinality?
text: What is the campaign ↔ flow cardinality? 1 campaign = many flows ; 1 flow = 1 campaign .

title: How does flow sharing work for campaign-related vs standalone flows?
text: How does flow sharing work for campaign-related vs standalone flows? Flows related to a campaign inherit its sharing ; standalone flows are private by default (share via categories + sharing rules, or manually).

title: What are the limits for connecting MCE journeys to a campaign?
text: What are the limits for connecting MCE journeys to a campaign? Max 20 journeys per campaign; one campaign per journey. Journey modes: Draft / Running / Finishing / Paused / Stopped.

title: Name the flow statuses.
text: Name the flow statuses. Preparing · Activated · Finishing · Completed · Scheduled · Canceled · Draft · Error. Only one version active ; ⚠️ a paused flow counts as active .

title: Which tiers get On-Canvas Insights vs Flow Reports?
text: Which tiers get On-Canvas Insights vs Flow Reports? On-Canvas Insights = Advanced only ; Flow Reports = Growth + Advanced . ---

title: What data source feeds each of these: segment entry, email merge fields, decision splits,
text: What data source feeds each of these: segment entry, email merge fields, decision splits, Get Records? Segment entry = DMO layer (Data 360) · email merge fields & decision splits = data graph · Get Records = Salesforce Core (bypasses Data 360).

title: Name the data sources available for messaging content.
text: Name the data sources available for messaging content. Data Graph (default) · Unified Individual DMO (fallback) · Event (1 per item) · Offer (max 5) · Personalization Recommender · Content Variable · Salesforce Record · Lookup Data Graph (max 5) · Apex Class (1 per message) · Activation (1 per message) · Marketing Object & Prospect (landing pages/forms only).

title: What is a data graph and what does the Default badge mean?
text: What is a data graph and what does the Default badge mean? A Data 360 object from a primary DMO (usually Unified Individual) plus related objects. The Default badge marks the default graph. Standard vs. real-time (real-time = faster, costs more).

title: ⚠️ When is a data graph locked (cannot be removed/replaced)?
text: ⚠️ When is a data graph locked (cannot be removed/replaced)? If an email has dynamic content variations or a recommender; or once a landing page content block is published . Landing pages should use a real-time graph.

title: Which data graph do SMS and WhatsApp use?
text: Which data graph do SMS and WhatsApp use? Only the default data graph (not shown in the panel, but works in merge fields).

title: When is the Unified Individual DMO used as a data source?
text: When is the Unified Individual DMO used as a data source? As a fallback when no data graph exists; it is the only option in Starter/Pro Suite emails.

title: What are the rules for the Event data source?
text: What are the rules for the Event data source? 1 per item ; repeaters do not support custom event data; cannot be removed/replaced after publish.

title: What are the rules for the Personalization Recommender data source?
text: What are the rules for the Personalization Recommender data source? Only trained recommenders on the same data graph; needs ≥1 successful refresh ; can be replaced but not removed ; data works only in a repeater.

title: What are the rules for a lookup data graph?
text: What are the rules for a lookup data graph? For non-profile data (catalog); needs a primary key; cannot nest ; max 5 .

title: What data types does a Content Variable support?
text: What data types does a Content Variable support? Boolean, string, date, date time, number, recordId — mapped to Flow data (MuleSoft/HTTP).

title: ⚠️ What must you do if you change a data source after attributes are used in merge fields?
text: ⚠️ What must you do if you change a data source after attributes are used in merge fields? Delete the merge fields, add the new source, and recreate them.

title: What is required when combining content types (form + landing page)?
text: What is required when combining content types (form + landing page)? The data graphs must match . ---

title: What is a personalization point?
text: What is a personalization point? A content element eligible for a decision (subject line, preheader, image). The first variation auto-creates the point.

title: What is the difference between a decision and a targeting rule?
text: What is the difference between a decision and a targeting rule? A decision is who is eligible (each variation ↔ a decision with the same name ). A targeting rule is the conditions for showing a variation (attributes, related attributes, calculated insights, segment memberships).

title: What is the difference between "All Conditions Are Met" and "Any Conditions Are Met"?
text: What is the difference between "All Conditions Are Met" and "Any Conditions Are Met"? All = every condition must be true; Any = at least one condition must be true.

title: What is the default variation and can its priority change?
text: What is the default variation and can its priority change? It shows when no rule matches; its priority cannot be changed .

title: What is the difference between cloning and linking a personalization point?
text: What is the difference between cloning and linking a personalization point? Clone = separate copy (component must have no variations; only points on the same data graph are shown). Link = share one point (point must already exist in the content item; component must have no variations).

title: What changes propagate across linked components, and what stays independent?
text: What changes propagate across linked components, and what stays independent? Adding/deleting a variation or editing rules/priorities applies to all linked components; content/style edits stay independent .

title: What does unlinking a personalization point do?
text: What does unlinking a personalization point do? It clones the point ("Copy of …") so the component keeps its settings but becomes independent.

title: What happens to a repeater when there is no data, and when the layout changes?
text: What happens to a repeater when there is no data, and when the layout changes? It is empty if there is no data for the recipient; changing the layout removes content/data/style .

title: How does an objective-based recommender work?
text: How does an objective-based recommender work? It picks the best image per contact at send time (no rules); the canvas shows a placeholder — use Preview with a segment to see real output. ---

title: What do the Entry, Decision, Action, and Wait elements do?
text: What do the Entry, Decision, Action, and Wait elements do? Entry = who enters and when · Decision = branching (first match wins) · Action = send email/SMS, create/update records, create consent, add/remove actionable list · Wait = fixed duration or wait-until-event.

title: What are the two Decision logic methods?
text: What are the two Decision logic methods? Define Manually (outcomes evaluated in order) vs. Define with AI (Advanced; simultaneous — order has no impact). ⚠️ Define with AI is not supported for Marketing Cloud flows .

title: What are the three parts of a decision condition?
text: What are the three parts of a decision condition? Resource (data-graph attribute) + Operator (Equals/Greater Than…) + Value .

title: ⚠️ What flow type do Wait elements require?
text: ⚠️ What flow type do Wait elements require? Autolaunched flows — they cannot be mixed with screens or choice.

title: What time is used for Wait Until Date with no time specified?
text: What time is used for Wait Until Date with no time specified? 12 AM org time zone .

title: ⚠️ Where must a Wait Until Event element sit, and what links are unsupported?
text: ⚠️ Where must a Wait Until Event element sit, and what links are unsupported? It must be immediately after the monitored element; dynamic/merge-field links are unsupported (use Any Link ).

title: What is a Path Experiment and when does it declare a winner?
text: What is a Path Experiment and when does it declare a winner? A random split + optimizer (Advanced + Personalization); auto-declares a winner at 95% confidence (Bayesian). Max 10 variations; percentages are targets, not exact counts .

title: Does manually selecting a Path Experiment winner require a new version?
text: Does manually selecting a Path Experiment winner require a new version? No.

title: What are marketing completion actions and which flow type are they for?
text: What are marketing completion actions and which flow type are they for? Assign to Queue/User and Notify User — Audience flows only .

title: What does the Einstein Decision element do?
text: What does the Einstein Decision element do? Routes by engagement level (Engagement Frequency / Scoring).

title: What does the Determine CRM Record for Individual element do?
text: What does the Determine CRM Record for Individual element do? Branches on contact / lead / prospect.

title: What are the restrictions for Send to Journey?
text: What are the restrictions for Send to Journey? Supports only Running journeys with an API event entry source ; Individual ID maps to SubscriberKey.

title: What are the rules for a Subflow element?
text: What are the rules for a Subflow element? Launches another active flow; ⚠️ cannot call flows with wait elements ; variable API names ≤ 40 chars ; calls the active version (API 61.0+).

title: What are the rules for the Get Records element?
text: What are the rules for the Get Records element? Pulls data in; limit 2–20,000 ; needs DLO→DMO mapping for Data Cloud objects.

title: ⚠️ What happens with an Update Records element that has no filter?
text: ⚠️ What happens with an Update Records element that has no filter? It updates ALL records.

title: Where do deleted records go and how long are they retained?
text: Where do deleted records go and how long are they retained? To the Recycle Bin for 15 days .

title: When do record changes actually take effect in a flow?
text: When do record changes actually take effect in a flow? Only when the transaction completes .

title: What do the Assignment, Loop, Collection Filter, Collection Sort, and Transform elements d
text: What do the Assignment, Loop, Collection Filter, Collection Sort, and Transform elements do? Assignment (consecutive in order) · Loop (Current Item from Loop) · Collection Filter (output null until run; source unchanged) · Collection Sort (up to 3 fields ; modifies directly) · Transform (≤ 1 nested collection ; formula ≤ 255 chars ; no data graphs for joins).

title: ⚠️ Where are In/Not In operators available, and which conditions are NOT filter conditions
text: ⚠️ Where are In/Not In operators available, and which conditions are NOT filter conditions? In/Not In only in Create/Get/Update Records; Contains/Is Changed are not filter conditions. Multi-select picklist matching is fragile → use INCLUDES .

title: What are the rules for flow exit rules?
text: What are the rules for flow exit rules? Up to 10 ; evaluated on start/resume; numeric attributes support aggregation (Average/Sum/Max/Min).

title: What are the rules for engagement signals?
text: What are the rules for engagement signals? Only Engagement-category DMOs ; one related DMO (1:1 or many-to-one); item identifier required for recommenders; identifiers = User/Timestamp/Item/Event; count-based metric by default; custom events from signals = Advanced only .

title: What is the difference between the flow data graph and the org default data graph?
text: What is the difference between the flow data graph and the org default data graph? Org default → message personalization; flow graph → decisioning. ---

title: What is contact point selection?
text: What is contact point selection? Choosing which fields (email, phone, MAID, etc.) go to the activation target.

title: What is source priority order and its values?
text: What is source priority order and its values? Which value wins when a contact has multiple sources. Values: Primary (Primary Flag mapped) · Personal (For Personal Use = 1) · Business (For Business Use = 1) · Any (no flag).

title: ⚠️ What governs contact points — reconciliation rules or source priority?
text: ⚠️ What governs contact points — reconciliation rules or source priority? Source priority — reconciliation rules do not govern contact points.

title: What happens when you remove "Any Source/Any Type"?
text: What happens when you remove "Any Source/Any Type"? A smaller population is targeted. ---

title: What are the three ways to create/edit an email?
text: What are the three ways to create/edit an email? Content tab (Add → Content → Email), the campaign record, or a flow's Send Email Message element.

title: What permissions are needed to create/edit vs publish an email?
text: What permissions are needed to create/edit vs publish an email? Create/edit = Marketing Cloud Manager + any CMS contributor role; publish/unpublish = plus content admin/manager.

title: ⚠️ What personalization is lost when copying an email?
text: ⚠️ What personalization is lost when copying an email? Only default variations are copied — other variations, rules, and recommenders are not (merge fields and repeaters are).

title: What does Convert to Code do and is it reversible?
text: What does Convert to Code do and is it reversible? It is one-way and removes dynamic content (repeaters, conditional logic, content variants); you lose drag-and-drop and the Style tab.

title: How long does the View as Web Page link work and what does it reflect?
text: How long does the View as Web Page link work and what does it reflect? Works 90 days after send; reflects the published version; personalized values re-render against the recipient's current profile on each open.

title: ⚠️ What happens if you manually edit the plain text version?
text: ⚠️ What happens if you manually edit the plain text version? It desyncs from the HTML version — future changes are not included.

title: What are the rules for test sends?
text: What are the rules for test sends? Up to 5 recipients; they count toward message credits ; the From name must be from an authenticated domain .

title: What are the file attachment limits?
text: What are the file attachment limits? A PDF from CMS, up to 5 MB .

title: What does CAN-SPAM require in an email?
text: What does CAN-SPAM require in an email? A Physical Address merge field + an opt-out link (Unsubscribe / Preference Manager / custom preference page). ⚠️ Preference Manager and Unsubscribe links do not work in preview.

title: How does template locking work?
text: How does template locking work? Templates are locked by default; nested components mirror the parent (locking cascades). Unlock template-wide (Settings), subject/preheader (lock icons), data sources, or per-component.

title: What are the rules for dynamic From and Reply addresses?
text: What are the rules for dynamic From and Reply addresses? Static From + dynamic display name = subdomain senders (avoids DMARC alignment failures). Dynamic From = root-domain authenticators. Dynamic reply requires an authorized email domain (unauthorized → fallback). Direct reply bypasses RMM . Always configure an authenticated fallback .

title: What are the Distributed Marketing template limits?
text: What are the Distributed Marketing template limits? 30 approved images + 30 approved phrases ; only one default image ; only phrases can be required (locked) — images cannot.

title: What permissions do non-marketer senders need?
text: What permissions do non-marketer senders need? Send Distributed Marketing Messages + Marketing Cloud Manager .

title: How is Distributed Marketing availability configured?
text: How is Distributed Marketing availability configured? An event-triggered flow with the Distributed Marketing and Alerts Message event; Get Records (List Email) + Decision (Status = Scheduled) prevent canceled sends.

title: What does unscheduling do?
text: What does unscheduling do? It cancels the email (and any others scheduled with it in the campaign).

title: What are the two Distributed Marketing dashboards?
text: What are the two Distributed Marketing dashboards? Distributed Sends (Individual Email / Bulk Email / Bulk Email Recipient Activity; your own sends only) + Unified Engagement History (record pages).

title: What is conversational email and what does it integrate with?
text: What is conversational email and what does it integrate with? Two-way email integrating with Agentforce, Digital Engagement, Data 360 ; replies are analysed for intent → trigger flows, route to agents/human reps, update data in real time. ---

title: Where are landing pages hosted?
text: Where are landing pages hosted? On the Marketing Landing Pages site (component/template pages) or a marketing site (code-view pages).

title: What is a URL alias and when can it be edited?
text: What is a URL alias and when can it be edited? A vanity URL, editable in Draft only; publishing activates aliases. Statuses: Draft / Active / Inactive (reactivatable).

title: What are the redirect URL rules?
text: What are the redirect URL rules? Must start with https:// and be < 2,000 characters ; set it up before unpublishing to avoid the "URL no longer exists" page.

title: When is a form visible?
text: When is a form visible? Only once added to a landing page that is published with an active URL alias .

title: What happens when you publish a landing page with a form?
text: What happens when you publish a landing page with a form? It publishes the form and activates the related flow .

title: What are the SEO rules for landing pages?
text: What are the SEO rules for landing pages? Public page title, description, head tags; only JSON-LD structured data allowed (no JavaScript); allowed tags = <link , <meta , <script .

title: What are the preview requirements and limitations?
text: What are the preview requirements and limitations? Requires site contributor access; merge fields are unresolved ; external images need a Trusted URL list entry.

title: ⚠️ What does template locking protect, and what can authors still edit?
text: ⚠️ What does template locking protect, and what can authors still edit? It protects content/settings only — authors can still edit targeting rules/variations ; clone the personalization point for logic control.

title: What are the two tracking options for landing pages?
text: What are the two tracking options for landing pages? A consent banner (Marketing Cloud Admin config; Manager + content role to publish) or Relaxed CSP + Head Markup set-consent event (no banner). Custom domain → path /lp . Re-publish the site after banner changes. ---

title: What is the form cardinality rule?
text: What is the form cardinality rule? One form per landing page; one flow per form ; view modes must match (block ↔ block, code ↔ code).

title: What is the minimum for a form and what are the unique field names?
text: What is the minimum for a form and what are the unique field names? ≥1 input + 1 button. Unique names: Email , FirstName , LastName (case-insensitive, no extra chars).

title: What are the rules for the write data provider?
text: What are the rules for the write data provider? Account/Contact/Lead/Prospect or a marketing object (default if available, else Lead ); one object at a time; respects FLS .

title: What are the read data providers and their limit?
text: What are the read data providers and their limit? Data graph, marketing object, Prospect — for pre-fill + progressive profiling; up to 2 lookup providers (max 1 marketing object + 1 recipient data graph).

title: What field types are supported on forms, and which are not?
text: What field types are supported on forms, and which are not? Supported: Checkbox, Date, Date/Time, Time, Email, Phone, Number, Picklist, Text, Text Area, Text Area (Long), URL. ⚠️ Number of Employees and multi-picklist are unsupported; no duplicate fields; changing a field's API name breaks future saves.

title: What are the rules for hidden fields and defaults?
text: What are the rules for hidden fields and defaults? Checkbox/Dropdown/Number/Plain Text/Text Area; hidden required fields need a fallback value ; URL parameters (UTM) are supported.

title: What are the reCAPTCHA v2 rules?
text: What are the reCAPTCHA v2 rules? Marketing landing pages with forms only; applies to every form once enabled; one per external page ; changing My Domain breaks it.

title: What are the progressive profiling rules?
text: What are the progressive profiling rules? Needs a read data provider; no rules on hidden fields/related objects; changing the read source removes rule connections. ⚠️ Avoid pre-filling PII.

title: What happens when you unpublish a form?
text: What happens when you unpublish a form? It deactivates its flow; Submit stops working; save the flow as a new version to edit/republish. ---

title: What makes up the external form embedding code?
text: What makes up the external form embedding code? 2 <script tags + 1 <fragment element ; generated from the published version (republish to refresh).

title: What security setup is required for external forms?
text: What security setup is required for external forms? CORS Allowed Origin List + clickjack protection (Trusted Domains for Inline Framing, or allow any page) + Trusted Sites for Scripts → publish the Experience Cloud site (else frame-ancestors 'self' CSP error).

title: What is a form handler?
text: What is a form handler? A way to capture existing external form submissions into Salesforce (also creates a Data 360 data source).

title: ⚠️ What is the critical rule for external form field names?
text: ⚠️ What is the critical rule for external form field names? External field names must exactly match the HTML name attributes. Date = YYYY-MM-DD ; Time = hh:mm:ss ; DateTime = ISO 8601; selected checkbox = true .

title: What is a honeypot field?
text: What is a honeypot field? A spam field that blocks submissions when it has a value; use a generic label, not honeypot .

title: ⚠️ When must you map all fields in a form handler?
text: ⚠️ When must you map all fields in a form handler? Before creating the flow — edits afterwards do not reflect automatically.

title: What is the difference between client-side and server-side form handlers?
text: What is the difference between client-side and server-side form handlers? Client-side (JS snippet): supports web tracking + identity resolution. Server-side (direct POST URL): no tracking/identity resolution; works with strict CSP/third-party builders. Both need a CORS Allowlist entry.

title: Where are LinkedIn posts managed?
text: Where are LinkedIn posts managed? Via the Social Posts related list on the campaigns object; connect a LinkedIn account; Publish Now or Schedule. ---

title: What is the Campaign Stage field and what is the trap?
text: What is the Campaign Stage field and what is the trap? Derived from all flows: In Planning / In Progress / Completed / Error / Canceled / Paused. ⚠️ One Error flow makes the whole campaign Error.

title: What does the Marketing Calendar show and what is the trap?
text: What does the Marketing Calendar show and what is the trap? Campaigns + Campaign Segment Flows + Segment Flows (default); access = Marketing Cloud Admin/Manager or Access Marketing Calendar permission; drag campaigns (not segment flows). ⚠️ Event/form-triggered flows do not appear.

title: What does the NotSentReason field map to, and what are common values?
text: What does the NotSentReason field map to, and what are common values? Maps to Engagement Action Reason on the Email Engagement DMO . Common: no consent, no opt-in, unauthorized From, hard bounce, TTL exceeded.

title: What does on-canvas element analytics show and what are the caveats?
text: What does on-canvas element analytics show and what are the caveats? Run/success/error counts, avg duration, messaging metrics (Sends, Delivery Rate, Opt-Out Rate, Reads, Failed Deliveries, Response Rate, CTR); needs Tableau Next Included App Business User . ⚠️ Open Details consumes Data Cloud credits ; not available for runs before Winter '25 .

title: What do AI campaigns do?
text: What do AI campaigns do? Draft with Agentforce → brief + campaign preview (name, flow, multichannel content); conversational campaigns add a "Forward to Agent" step; agent actions are powered by Salesforce Flow ; Generate Campaign Insights analyses the first flow . ---

title: What is the single orchestration engine for outbound messaging in MC Next?
text: What is the single orchestration engine for outbound messaging in MC Next? Flow — these are marketing flows (high-scale flows) that run off-core , so governor limits and transaction-scaling concerns don't apply the same way.

title: Name the six flow types and their triggers.
text: Name the six flow types and their triggers. Audience (schedule/immediate) · Activation-triggered (activation publishes) · Automation event-triggered (event occurs) · On-demand (REST API, individual) · Broadcast (REST API, dynamic segment) · Data Cloud-triggered (DMO/CIO record changes).

title: Which two flow types cannot send emails from MC Next?
text: Which two flow types cannot send emails from MC Next? ⚠️ Record-triggered flows (CRM flows) and Data Cloud-triggered flows .

title: What re-entry options do audience flows offer?
text: What re-entry options do audience flows offer? Three, mirroring Journey Builder's contact entry mode: no re-entry , re-entry at any time , re-entry only after exiting .

title: Why can an activation be used as the personalization source?
text: Why can an activation be used as the personalization source? Because you can append related-object attributes to the activation — merge fields and repeaters reference enriched activation attributes without additional send-time lookups .

title: What two values are required for an on-demand flow API call?
text: What two values are required for an on-demand flow API call? Email address and individual ID . ⚠️ The ID needn't match a Data 360 Individual record — it just can't be null . No Individual DMO record is created, but engagement lands in the Email Engagement DMO .

title: What is the typical latency of an on-demand flow?
text: What is the typical latency of an on-demand flow? 1–3 seconds — ideal for one-time passcodes, order confirmations, password resets, real-time service alerts.

title: What segment type must a broadcast flow use?
text: What segment type must a broadcast flow use? A dynamic segment , evaluated at execution time using variables passed into the flow. Static and parameterized criteria can be combined.

title: Name the eight data providers.
text: Name the eight data providers. Data graph · Event · Activation · Salesforce record · Apex class · Personalization recommender · Lookup graph · Offer.

title: Can a message use both an activation and an event data provider?
text: Can a message use both an activation and an event data provider? ⚠️ No — each requires a specific flow orchestration pattern, so using both creates a conflict in how data is bound to the message.

title: What does an event data provider NOT support?
text: What does an event data provider NOT support? Related collections — it supports direct attributes from the event DMO only (e.g., Sales Order yes, Sales Order Product no).

title: What are content variables, and what types do they support?
text: What are content variables, and what types do they support? Custom placeholders defined in the email, populated at runtime from Salesforce Flow (any flow data source incl. MuleSoft/HTTP). Types: boolean, text, date, dateTime, number, recordId . The content defines the placeholders; the flow supplies the values .

title: What is a marketing object, and what's the MCE comparison?
text: What is a marketing object, and what's the MCE comparison? A marketer-managed table of data queried at runtime to personalize content. Closest MCE comparison = a data extension . Supports text, number, decimal ; full refresh replaces records.

title: How does MC Next personalization differ from MCE?
text: How does MC Next personalization differ from MCE? MCE relies primarily on data extensions (sendable/non-sendable). MC Next offers data providers, content variables, and marketing objects . ⚠️ Not every MCE AMPscript function is supported.

title: Which personalization methods are marketer-friendly vs developer-oriented?
text: Which personalization methods are marketer-friendly vs developer-oriented? Marketer: merge fields, repeaters, dynamic content. Developer: Handlebars, AMPscript.

title: What can you define when inserting a merge field?
text: What can you define when inserting a merge field? A fallback value used when the customer's data is missing (e.g., "Friend" for a missing first name). ---

title: What can the Campaign Creation agent do?
text: What can the Campaign Creation agent do? Draft a brief, create a campaign from a brief, summarize, and generate insights.

title: What can the Content Builder agent do?
text: What can the Content Builder agent do? Draft content and create sections.

title: What does Einstein Segments do and what does it require?
text: What does Einstein Segments do and what does it require? Turns natural language into a segment; requires a Unified Individual DMO with ≥10 records .

title: What is Einstein Data Prism?
text: What is Einstein Data Prism? The grounding layer for Einstein segments — it scans metadata, auto-generates descriptions, and uses a vector database. Validate/exclude via Metadata Studio . ⚠️ Not supported in Gov Cloud Plus.

title: What does Einstein Segments strip out when generating a segment?
text: What does Einstein Segments strip out when generating a segment? Demographic attributes and attributes that would return < 10 results . ---

title: What is the difference between a channel and an agent in conversational messaging?
text: What is the difference between a channel and an agent in conversational messaging? Channel = pipe (delivery); Agent = brain (LLM + Data 360).

title: What four components make up the conversational ecosystem?
text: What four components make up the conversational ecosystem? Channel + Flow + Agent + Data 360 .

title: What is the difference between subagents and actions?
text: What is the difference between subagents and actions? Subagents = job description (boundaries); Actions = tools (get info / update records).

title: What are the four stages of the conversational lifecycle?
text: What are the four stages of the conversational lifecycle? Trigger → Routing/intent → Execution → Handoff/resolution.

title: What are the key conversational KPIs?
text: What are the key conversational KPIs? Deflection, engagement, and conversion. ---

title: Which edition is required for each predictive AI feature?
text: Which edition is required for each predictive AI feature? Send Time Optimization (STO) = Growth (global model) / Advanced · Metrics Guard = Growth + Advanced · Engagement Scoring = Advanced only · Engagement Frequency = Advanced only.

title: ⚠️ What is counterintuitive about the Metrics Guard score?
text: ⚠️ What is counterintuitive about the Metrics Guard score? Lower = more likely real (a lower score means a lower likelihood of being a bot).

title: What prerequisite do STO, Engagement Scoring, and Engagement Frequency share?
text: What prerequisite do STO, Engagement Scoring, and Engagement Frequency share? An identity resolution ruleset with Individual as the primary object.

title: What are the three scoring model types and their range?
text: What are the three scoring model types and their range? Engagement , Fit , and Overall — scored 0–100 . Account scoring is Advanced only .

title: How does scoring frequency affect cost?
text: How does scoring frequency affect cost? More frequent scoring = more credits consumed. ---

title: Name the components of the Einstein Trust Layer.
text: Name the components of the Einstein Trust Layer. Toxicity detection · dynamic grounding (anti-hallucination) · PII masking · zero data retention · encryption · audit trail · human escalation.

title: What does dynamic grounding do?
text: What does dynamic grounding do? It grounds AI responses in real data to prevent hallucination.

title: What does zero data retention mean in the Trust Layer?
text: What does zero data retention mean in the Trust Layer? Prompts and responses are not retained by the LLM provider. ---

title: Name the five marketing agents and what each does.
text: Name the five marketing agents and what each does. Segment Creation (NL → editable segment criteria) · Campaign Creation (briefs, flows, multi-channel content) · Content Creation (drafts/refines email, LP, SMS) · Journey Decisioning (picks journey/flow + personalizes) · Account Discovery (account insights + buying group members).

title: What does the Account Discovery agent do?
text: What does the Account Discovery agent do? Provides account insights and identifies potential buying group members — helps discover stakeholders and guide nurturing/follow-up.

title: What is the "Draft with Agentforce" workflow?
text: What is the "Draft with Agentforce" workflow? Marketing Home → New Campaign → Draft with Agentforce → describe objective → draft a brief → generate a campaign → review the campaign preview (flow + content) → save as a new campaign .

title: What are the four Engagement Frequency classifications?
text: What are the four Engagement Frequency classifications? Saturated · Almost Saturated · On Target · Under Saturated (Email Engagement Classification field in the Email Engagement Frequency DMO).

title: How is Engagement Frequency trained and refreshed?
text: How is Engagement Frequency trained and refreshed? Trained only on your organisation's data ; scores refreshed weekly . Analyses up to 90 days of email activity.

title: What three likelihood predictions does Engagement Scoring generate?
text: What three likelihood predictions does Engagement Scoring generate? Likelihood to open , likelihood to click , and likelihood to remain subscribed .

title: Name the four Engagement Scoring personas.
text: Name the four Engagement Scoring personas. Loyalists (high open/high click) · Selective Subscribers (low open/high click) · Window Shoppers (high open/low click) · Win Back/Dormant (low/low).

title: What four tiers are the likelihood predictions grouped into?
text: What four tiers are the likelihood predictions grouped into? Most Likely · More Likely · Less Likely · Least Likely — usable in a Decision element.

title: What does Engagement Scoring emphasise in its analysis?
text: What does Engagement Scoring emphasise in its analysis? The most recent activity — it analyses up to 90 days but weights recent behaviour more heavily.

title: What setup does Send Time Optimization require?
text: What setup does Send Time Optimization require? Add the Send Time Optimization DMO to the data graph (required structure), then select the Hourly Scores by Week field. Must be enabled in Setup .

title: What is the STO optimization window range?
text: What is the STO optimization window range? 2 hours up to 1 week — MC Next sends at each recipient's predicted optimal time within that window.

title: Which editions support Send Time Optimization?
text: Which editions support Send Time Optimization? Both Growth and Advanced (unlike Engagement Frequency and Engagement Scoring, which are Advanced only).

title: What must you configure before using predictive AI insights in a flow?
text: What must you configure before using predictive AI insights in a flow? The required data graph — then use fields like Email Engagement Frequency or Engagement Score in a Decision element , or as segment criteria . ---

title: What does the Campaign Performance dashboard show?
text: What does the Campaign Performance dashboard show? Aggregated and individual campaign KPIs.

title: What does the Content Performance dashboard show?
text: What does the Content Performance dashboard show? Cross-channel and variation data.

title: What does the Deliverability dashboard show?
text: What does the Deliverability dashboard show? Email delivery and failure reasons.

title: What does the Email Engagement dashboard show?
text: What does the Email Engagement dashboard show? Email KPIs.

title: Which dashboards cover SMS, forms, and landing pages?
text: Which dashboards cover SMS, forms, and landing pages? The SMS / Forms / Landing Page Engagement dashboards (channel-specific).

title: What dashboards make up B2B Analytics?
text: What dashboards make up B2B Analytics? Account-Based Marketing, Pipeline, Marketing Manager, and B2B Attribution — focused on revenue attribution.

title: Which dashboard would you use to investigate email deliverability failures?
text: Which dashboard would you use to investigate email deliverability failures? The Deliverability dashboard (email delivery + failure reasons). ---

title: What is the Open Rate formula?
text: What is the Open Rate formula? Unique opens ÷ (sends − bounces).

title: What is the Click Rate formula?
text: What is the Click Rate formula? Unique clicks ÷ (sends − bounces).

title: What is the Click-Through Rate (CTR) formula?
text: What is the Click-Through Rate (CTR) formula? Unique clicks ÷ unique opens.

title: What is the Bounce Rate formula?
text: What is the Bounce Rate formula? Bounces ÷ sends.

title: What is the Delivery Rate formula?
text: What is the Delivery Rate formula? (Sends − bounces) ÷ sends.

title: What is the Opt-Out Rate formula?
text: What is the Opt-Out Rate formula? Unsubscribes ÷ (sends − bounces).

title: ⚠️ Why might Opt-Out Rate be understated?
text: ⚠️ Why might Opt-Out Rate be understated? Preference Page unsubscribes are recorded as consent updates , not Email Engagement Unsubscribe events, so they are excluded from the metric. ---

title: What is Marketing Performance and what does installing it require?
text: What is Marketing Performance and what does installing it require? A Data Cloud + Tableau Next analytics surface; installation needs both the Data Cloud admin and Marketing Cloud Admin permission sets; viewing needs Tableau Next Included App Business User .

title: What is Opportunity Influence and what is its attribution window?
text: What is Opportunity Influence and what is its attribution window? Email/SMS click attribution with a 30-day-before window to Closed/Won.

title: What are the two attribution models?
text: What are the two attribution models? First-touch vs. last-touch .

title: ⚠️ What happens when you share folders or dashboards?
text: ⚠️ What happens when you share folders or dashboards? They won't appear to users — sharing alone does not grant visibility.

title: ⚠️ What does opening element details in on-canvas analytics consume?
text: ⚠️ What does opening element details in on-canvas analytics consume? Data Cloud credits . ---

title: Name the three out-of-the-box reporting capabilities.
text: Name the three out-of-the-box reporting capabilities. Campaign Performance Dashboard (individual campaign end-to-end) · Marketing Performance Dashboard (cross-channel over time) · Semantic Data Model (consistent business layer). ⚠️ All included with no additional license .

title: What's the difference between the Campaign Performance and Marketing Performance dashboard
text: What's the difference between the Campaign Performance and Marketing Performance dashboards? Campaign Performance = one campaign, end to end (sends, opens, clicks, bounces, contact progression). Marketing Performance = broader cross-channel view over time (audience growth, program-level trends).

title: Where else do performance dashboards appear?
text: Where else do performance dashboards appear? Embedded directly in each campaign record — no need to navigate to a separate reporting tab.

title: How do you access content performance dashboards?
text: How do you access content performance dashboards? Select the element in the active flow (e.g., Send Email Message) → Analytics tab → Details → pulse card metrics + row-level data.

title: Which channels do the deliverability dashboards cover?
text: Which channels do the deliverability dashboards cover? SMS, WhatsApp, and mobile app messaging — showing delivery health and why messages failed to reach recipients.

title: What is the semantic data model?
text: What is the semantic data model? Powered by Tableau Next , the Marketing Intelligence Semantic Data Model combines multiple Data 360 objects and defines relationships/metrics centrally so metrics calculate consistently.

title: What can you do with the semantic data model?
text: What can you do with the semantic data model? Build custom reports , combine them as dashboard widgets , customise standard dashboards (widgets/labels/layouts/filters), extend to other Data 360 objects, share with stakeholders outside CRM , or connect external tools .

title: What is the Unified Engagement History dashboard, and how is it deployed?
text: What is the Unified Engagement History dashboard, and how is it deployed? A pre-built dashboard giving sales and marketing a shared view of lead/contact activity on an account. Embed by adding the component to account, lead, and contact page layouts . ---
